kept.name: CMF sign run exhaustion
kept.note: Chaikin Money Flow zero crossings, but only the ones that terminate a money-flow regime that has already lasted at least as long as the indicator's own averaging window, and only when the newly arriving flow agrees with the SMA(50) trend. The trigger is the DURATION of the preceding flow state, not its magnitude.
kept.source: Chaikin Money Flow formula verified from the open-source `ta` library source, https://raw.githubusercontent.com/bukosabino/ta/master/ta/volume.py (ChaikinMoneyFlowIndicator: mfv = ((close-low)-(high-close))/(high-low), filled with 0, times volume, rolling-summed and divided by rolling-summed volume). Indicator originally Marc Chaikin; the run-length entry condition and the sign-flip exit are my synthesis.

kept.name: Halloween Exposure Gate
kept.note: The six-month seasonal as an exposure gate: fully long through the November-to-winter_end window, and in the summer window either flat (summer_mode 0, the pure form) or long only inside the turn-of-month windows (summer_mode 1, the paper-suggested softened form, which is where much of the summer return has historically sat). No price condition and no stop rule of its own. Note the pure form is degenerate on any backtest window that lies entirely inside one half of the year -- it will show zero trades there, which is the rule behaving correctly, not a broken signal.
kept.source: Bouman & Jacobsen, "The Halloween Indicator, 'Sell in May and Go Away': Another Puzzle," American Economic Review 92(5), 2002, 1618-1635

kept.name: Composite Operator Anchored VWAP Reclaim
kept.note: Picks the composite operator's average cost the way Wyckoff describes it and Shannon draws it: the anchor is the EVENT bar in [i-look_back, i-min_bars] with the largest volume/SMA(volume,20), subject to that bar's volume clearing vol_mult x average AND its low sitting within ext_atr x ATR(14) of the lowest low of the 60 bars ending there. The anchored VWAP is then carried forward from that bar by prefix sums, the setup requires close under the line on uw_min of the last uw_win bars (the accumulated book is under water) with the line itself flat or rising over slope_look bars (the operator is still bidding, not liquidating), and the trigger is the first bar that closes back above the line, above the prior bar's high, on entry_vol x average volume. Short mirrors every clause. Exits are the idea's own: take profit at AVWAP + sig_tp x sigma where sigma is the standard deviation of (typical price - AVWAP) accumulated from the anchor, hard invalidation on a close invalid_atr x ATR through the line, and the structural stop at the extreme of the stop_look bars preceding the entry padded by stop_atr x ATR. Harness target and stop are switched off so those three exits are the whole exit rule. The 250-bar anchor decay in the source is redundant here and dropped: the anchor search window is only look_back bars deep, so no anchor can survive that long.
kept.source: Wyckoff's composite operator concept (StockCharts ChartSchool, 'The Wyckoff Method'); anchored VWAP as an event-anchored fair-value line popularised by Brian Shannon (Alphatrends, 'Maximum Trading Gains with Anchored VWAP', 2023). The practice of anchoring specifically to 'climax/exhaustion bars' and trading the reclaim/rejection is documented in the TradingView anchored-VWAP script literature I reviewed. The anchor-selection algorithm, underwater filter, slope filter and sigma exit are my quantification (synthesis).

kept.name: Corwin-Schultz spread spike fade
kept.note: Estimates the effective bid-ask spread from highs and lows alone by comparing one two-bar range against the sum of two one-bar ranges (beta/gamma/alpha exactly as in AFML snippet 19.1), then buys when that estimated spread pushes above its own trailing `pct` percentile while price is down over the last `ret_win` bars - the OHLCV signature of market makers widening rather than of news arriving. Exits when the spread estimate falls back under its trailing median, or after `max_hold` bars, with a 2 ATR stop.
kept.source: Corwin & Schultz high-low spread estimator, implemented as AFML snippet 19.1 (p.285) in mlfinlab/microstructural_features/first_generation.py (_get_beta, _get_gamma, _get_alpha, get_corwin_schultz_estimator) - source read from the archived mlfinlab-master.zip at https://github.com/mnewls/MLFINLAB. Also documented in the open-access CRAN package 'bidask' (Ardia, Guidotti & Kroencke, JFE 2024).

kept.name: Tug-of-War Session Split
kept.note: Holds the same signal in one session and only one. S = close above EMA(ema_n) with ADX(14) >= adx_min, read at the last regular-hours bar of the day. arm=0 (overnight) buys at that closing bar and exits at the next regular-session open, carrying zero intraday exposure; arm=1 (intraday) buys at the regular-session open and exits at that day's close, carrying zero overnight exposure. Neither arm has a stop, target or trail - the session boundary IS the exit, which is the whole point of the test. The signal and its parameters are identical across arms so the only difference is which half of the day the exposure is held in.
kept.source: Lou, Polk & Skouras (2019), 'A Tug of War: Overnight versus Intraday Expected Returns', Journal of Financial Economics 134:192-213 (personal.lse.ac.uk/polk/research/tugofwar.pdf).

kept.name: Ariel semi-month exposure split
kept.note: Ariel's month partition, unconditional on price: long from the last trading day of the prior month through the Nth trading day of this one, then short (or flat) until the second-to-last session, flat for one day, repeat. Trading-day indices come from the session calendar -- weekday arithmetic with observed holidays removed -- so no price is used to place a session in its month. The daily hold is expressed as a state signal, which is what a rule with no exit event of its own has to be.
kept.source: Ariel, 'A Monthly Effect in Stock Returns', Journal of Financial Economics 18(1), 1987 - cited from the literature; not re-fetched this session (search budget exhausted). The exact split point (Ariel uses the last day of the prior month plus the first half of the month by trading-day count) is pinned to the 9th trading day here so the rule is unambiguous; sweep it.

kept.name: Cumulative-Violation Severity Clustering
kept.note: Builds Du and Escanciano's cumulative violation H_t = (1/alpha)(alpha - u_t)1{u_t <= alpha} from the probability integral transform of the conditional model, which is 0 on a non-violation day and rises toward 1 the deeper the violation, so it inherits expected shortfall's severity-awareness while staying distribution-free (E[H] = alpha/2, Var = alpha(1/3 - alpha/4)). Two statistics are then rolled over the trailing win bars: the unconditional severity t-statistic U_ES = sqrt(W)(mean(H) - alpha/2)/sqrt(alpha(1/3 - alpha/4)), and the Box-Pierce statistic on the first bp_lags autocorrelations of {H - alpha/2}, whose critical value is the 95th chi-square percentile for those degrees of freedom. Base long entries -- an RSI cross up out of oversold, the least opinionated version of the dip buy this ladder actually does, so what is measured is the gate rather than the entry -- are licensed only while U_ES < u_gate AND BP < that critical value, and only after restore consecutive clean bars. The position is closed on the first bar where BP trips (deep losses are clustering, so the next violation is likely to be a deep one) or where U_ES reaches u_flat. SUBSTITUTION, stated plainly: the conditional CDF comes from an EWMA variance with standardised Student-t innovations rather than a re-estimated GARCH(1,1)-t. The idea's own inputs list allows 'a GARCH-t or EWMA-normal model' and its params sweep the innovation distribution; refitting a GARCH by QML on a rolling 1000-bar window every bar is not affordable at hundreds of thousands of backtests, and nothing the idea is about -- H_t, its mean, the autocorrelation of its severity -- changes under the swap.
kept.source: Du & Escanciano (2017), 'Backtesting expected shortfall: accounting for tail risk', Management Science 63(4), building on Costanzino & Curran (2015). Cumulative violation definition H_t(alpha) = (1/alpha)(alpha - u_t)1{u_t <= alpha}, the moments E[H_t] = alpha/2 and Var = alpha(1/3 - alpha/4), the U_ES t-statistic and the Box-Pierce conditional test as set out in Nieto & Ruiz, UCM working paper Section 4.2.4 (https://docta.ucm.es/bitstreams/661963d3-b3ca-44e1-b46c-ad300c907b79/download); open access at https://caepr.indiana.edu/RePEc/inu/caeprp/caepr2015-001.pdf.

kept.name: Semi-Monthly Payday Window
kept.note: A large share of US employers run semi-monthly payroll on the 15th and at month end, and the payroll-deducted retirement contributions are swept into index and target-date funds a day or two later by buyers with no price sensitivity at all. This holds long from the close of the last session on or before the target day through the close of the first session on or after the exit day, with no indicator condition of any kind. The turn-of-month overlap check is kept so the window cannot double-count the month-end flow that a separate family already tests; `also_eom` deliberately turns that second window back on so the pair can be compared.
kept.source: Aixin Ma and William Robert Pratt, 'Payday Anomaly', SSRN working paper 3257064 - rule, mechanism and performance verified via https://quantpedia.com/strategies/payday-anomaly/, which states the rule as 'Buy and hold the S&P 500 index on the 16th day of each month only' and reports 2.57% annualised at 4.31% volatility, Sharpe ~0.6, 1980-2010, with the authors quoted that 'the 16th day of the month statistically and economically outperforms all other calendar days except the 1st and 2nd'.

kept.name: Factor Momentum on OHLCV Factors
kept.note: Time-series momentum applied to the RETURN PATH of constructed factor portfolios rather than to price. Five OHLCV factor proxies (12-1 momentum, short-horizon reversal, low volatility, dollar-volume growth, proximity to the trailing high) are each held as a signed position, each leg's own realised P&L series is accumulated, and at every rebalance a leg is bought if its trailing return INCLUDING the most recent period is positive and sold if negative, sized inverse to that leg's own return volatility and capped. The net of the five legs is the traded weight.
kept.source: Ehsani & Linnainmaa (2022), 'Factor Momentum and the Momentum Factor', Journal of Finance 77(3) / NBER WP 25551. The must-include-the-most-recent-period requirement is from Arnott, Clements, Kalesnik & Linnainmaa, 'Is Factor Momentum More than Stock Momentum?', arXiv:2009.04824. DEVIATION, stated plainly: the paper forms each factor as an equal-weighted top-minus-bottom-tercile spread across a universe, which a single-symbol harness cannot build. Here each factor is instead a single-name timing leg whose weight is the sign of the score's own trailing z-score, so the cross-sectional demeaning becomes time-series demeaning. The mechanism under test - momentum measured on a constructed portfolio's return series and only then translated into a position - is preserved; the cross-sectional diversification of the real factor legs is not.

kept.name: TD sequential setup nine with perfection
kept.note: DeMark bar counting and nothing else. A buy setup counts consecutive bars closing below the close `off` bars back; at count `setup_len` the perfection inequality is tested (min of the last two setup lows at or below min of setup bars L-3 and L-2) and, if it fails, the count is allowed to extend to max_len looking for the first bar that satisfies it. Sell setup is the mirror. entry_mode 0 enters at the qualifying close, 1 is DeMark's Method 2 (the first later bar that closes back above close[-off]), 2 runs the Countdown to 13 on close <= low[-2]. The TDST target -- the first close beyond the extreme of the setup bars -- is the family's own exit_signal.
kept.source: Thomas DeMark, 'The New Science of Technical Analysis' (1994). Setup rule (9 consecutive closes with Close[i] < Close[i-4]) and the countdown's switch to a close[2]-based comparison confirmed in the open-source implementation https://github.com/Forte11Cuba/TD-Sequential-Tom-DeMark. Independent backtest with the same 4-bar offset, 9-bar count and 'Method 2' entry, across 42 futures markets 1980-2013: https://oxfordstrat.com/trading-strategies/td-sequential-1/ - note performance deteriorates markedly at $100 round-turn costs, so this needs liquid names and passive fills.

kept.name: Corwin-Schultz Spread Shock Fade
kept.note: Recovers the effective bid-ask spread from the geometry of one-bar versus two-bar high/low ranges (Corwin-Schultz), smooths it, and fades the direction of the move whenever that estimated cost of immediacy sits at the top of its own 250-bar distribution -- the mechanical part of short-horizon reversal.
kept.source: Corwin & Schultz (2012), 'A Simple Way to Estimate Bid-Ask Spreads from Daily High and Low Prices', Journal of Finance 67(2):719-759; intraday application per Corwin's Notre Dame notes.

kept.name: Realized GARCH measurement-equation surprise
kept.note: Trades the residual of the Realized GARCH MEASUREMENT equation - the part of realized variation that the bar's own return direction and size cannot account for. K bars stand in for a day and the sub-bar returns inside them for the 5-minute returns, so x_t is a genuine realized variance and y_t the return over the same span. log(sig2) follows the model's volatility recursion w + a*log(x_{t-1}) + b*log(sig2_{t-1}); log(x_t) is then regressed on [1, log(sig2_t), z_t, z_t^2 - 1] - the intercept xi, the loading d and the Hermite leverage function tau(z) = e1*z + e2*(z^2-1) - and utilde is the standardised residual. Long the quiet churn (utilde high, |z| small); short the confirmed bad news (utilde high, z very negative). SUBSTITUTION, stated plainly: joint QML estimation of all seven parameters on a rolling 1000-day window is not affordable at hundreds of thousands of backtests, so a and b are fixed parameters (swept) and only the measurement equation is estimated, by rolling OLS on the window ending before the bar scored, which keeps every residual out of sample. What the idea calls novel - a signal orthogonal by construction to both the return and the volatility level - survives that substitution intact.
kept.source: Hansen, Huang & Shek (2012), 'Realized GARCH: a joint model for returns and realized measures of volatility', Journal of Applied Econometrics 27, 877-906. Model equations, the quadratic Hermite leverage function tau(z) = e1*z + e2*(z^2 - 1) and the news impact curve nu(z) = d*tau(z) as reproduced in the rugarch vignette 'Introduction to the rugarch package', Section 2.2.9, Eqs. (46)-(53): https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/rugarch/vignettes/Introduction_to_the_rugarch_package.pdf

kept.name: Factor Valuation Percentile Timing
kept.note: PARTIAL, AND DELIBERATELY SO. The published rule is a cross-sectional book of K factor spreads sorted into terciles by their own valuation; a single-symbol harness cannot hold a book, so that layer is dropped rather than faked. What is implemented is the signal construction the idea itself calls the novel part: the expanding-window percentile of a STRATEGY's trailing cumulative return, used to decide whether to run that strategy long, inverted, or not at all. The sleeve being valued is a time-series momentum leg on the symbol. `flip` runs the same book with the sign reversed, which is factor momentum - the null the idea asks to be run alongside. Volatility-equalised sizing is not representable and is not simulated.
kept.source: Arnott, Beck, Kalesnik & West, 'How Can Smart Beta Go Horribly Wrong?' (Research Affiliates, 2016) versus Asness, Ilmanen & Maloney, 'Market Timing: Sin a Little' (Journal of Investment Management 2017) and Asness, 'The Siren Song of Factor Timing' (Journal of Portfolio Management 2016). The Research Affiliates URL now redirects to a dead page, so the relative-price percentile is the harvesting agent's own OHLCV-only substitute for the book-to-market spread those papers use. Haddad, Kozak & Santosh, 'Factor Timing' (RFS 2020; NBER WP 26708) independently confirms anomaly portfolios are predictable by their own valuation ratios.

kept.name: Expectile-quantile tail heaviness
kept.note: A tail-SHAPE gate on a dip-buying entry, built from the divergence between a magnitude-weighted tail statistic and a frequency-based one. Every g_step bars, over the trailing g_win returns with losses Y = -r: the tau-expectile xi_tau is solved exactly from the first-order condition of the asymmetric-least-squares objective eta_tau(u) = |1(u<=0)-tau| u^2 (a binary search over the order statistics lands on the same point IRLS converges to - verified equal to 1e-16 against a 500-iteration IRLS, so this is a faster solver for the same estimator, not a different one); the Hill index gamma is estimated from the top g_k order statistics; xi is pushed out to the extreme level tau' by the Weissman relation xi_tau' = ((1-tau')/(1-tau))^(-gamma) * xi_tau; and G = xi_tau' / q_tau' compares it against the empirical quantile of the same window. Base long entries (a g_dip-bar low, the fleet's own dip-buy shape) are taken only while G sits below its g_pct-th percentile over the last g_hist readings, and everything is flattened above the g_flat-th. Deviations, both forced by the harness: position size is a fixed share count, so the idea's 'halve every position' step is expressed as refusing NEW entries in the 80-95th percentile band rather than as a half-size book, and the 5-consecutive-closes re-arm becomes an immediate re-arm once G drops back under the entry percentile. Windows are bar counts on 5-minute bars, not the paper's 1000 daily returns - the estimator is scale-free but the horizon it describes is intraday, and with 500 bars in the window the tau' = 0.999 quantile is the sample maximum, so the grid keeps tau' at 0.995 by default where the empirical quantile is still an average of several observations.
kept.source: Padoan & Stupfler, 'Tail risk inference via expectiles in heavy-tailed time series', arXiv:2004.04078 - the expectile definition with eta_tau(u) = |1(u<=0)-tau| u^2 (Newey & Powell 1987) and the Weissman-type extrapolation xi_tau'/xi_tau ~ ((1-tau')/(1-tau))^(-gamma). Coherence-and-elicitability uniqueness of expectiles: Bellini & Bignozzi, arXiv:1411.0426; Ziegel, 'Coherence and elicitability', arXiv:1303.1690.

kept.name: Rogers-Satchell Drift Detector
kept.note: Ratio of the UNdemeaned close-to-close variance (expectation sigma^2 + mu^2) to the Rogers-Satchell range variance (drift-free), so DR-1 estimates (drift/vol)^2 per bar with no smoothing constant. Trades in the direction of the N-bar return sum when DR clears the gate and the close is the extreme of the last few bars; exits when DR collapses back into the noise. From Rogers & Satchell (1991).
kept.source: Rogers & Satchell (1991), 'Estimating variance from high, low and closing prices', Annals of Applied Probability 1(4), 504-512 (the drift-independent estimator); Parkinson (1980), Journal of Business 53(1), 61-65; Garman & Klass (1980), Journal of Business 53(1), 67-78. Estimator comparison and formulas: https://portfoliooptimizer.io/blog/range-based-volatility-estimators-overview-and-examples-of-usage/ and https://macrosynergy.com/research/six-ways-to-estimate-realized-volatility/ . The drift-ratio construction itself is my synthesis from those estimators' bias properties.

kept.name: Hasbrouck VAR flow forecast
kept.note: A bivariate VAR(lags) in returns and a signed volume-flow proxy, refitted on a rolling est_win window and traded on its one-step point forecast. x is ordered first, so the return equation carries the contemporaneous flow term and a forecast of the return requires forecasting the FLOW first and pushing it through the impact coefficient - the staggered impact and flow persistence a single-equation lambda regression discards. Trade the sign of rhat when |rhat| >= thr_sd x stdev(r,win) and the r-equation's in-sample R^2 clears min_r2; below that the system is fitting noise and the rule says so. Horizon-matched exit: hold while consecutive forecasts keep the same sign, out when the forecast flattens or flips. Rolling cross-moments are updated by rank-one add/drop so a refit is two updates, not est_win of them. Two measured facts about this rule on real 5-minute bars, both worth knowing before reading its results. The r-equation's in-sample R^2 runs about 0.5, because with bar data sign(x_t) IS sign(r_t) by construction and the contemporaneous term is part tautology - so the paper-faithful 0.01 floor never binds, and the sweep carries 0.40 and 0.55 as the values that make it a gate. The FORECAST is untainted by that (it uses xhat, never x_t) and is small: |rhat| runs about 0.09 x stdev(r) at the median and reaches 0.75 only in the top 1%, which is where the default threshold sits.
kept.source: Joel Hasbrouck, 'Measuring the Information Content of Stock Trades', Journal of Finance 46(1), 179-207, 1991 - a VAR of trades and quote revisions with price effects that materialise gradually. Using the fitted VAR as a live one-step forecaster is the harvested idea's own construction.

kept.name: Length-of-night exposure tilt
kept.note: A pure calendar rule with no market data in it at all. Hours of night are computed from the solar-declination formula at a fixed latitude; the SAD variable is hours-of-night minus twelve, nonzero only between the autumn and spring equinoxes, and a fall dummy makes the autumn leg asymmetric. Target exposure E = clip(1 + a*SAD - b*FALL*SAD, 0, 2) is minimum (short) through the lengthening nights of autumn, maximum from the solstice through February, neutral in summer. Fixed share size means E is read as a sign: long above e_long, short below e_short, flat in between - so the rebalance band of the continuous form has no analogue here and the two thresholds do that job.
kept.source: Kamstra, Kramer & Levi, 'Winter Blues: A SAD Stock Market Cycle', American Economic Review 93(1), 2003. The harvester could not re-verify the published coefficient values this session, so a and b are indicative starting points for the sweep, not the paper's estimates; the SAD variable and fall dummy definitions are as specified in that paper.

kept.name: Benjamini-Yekutieli false discovery allocator
kept.note: Twelve candidate rules drawn from twelve different indicator families run side by side. At each recompute the per-bar return series of every rule is turned into a one-sided Newey-West t for the null of zero mean return, the p-values are sorted, and the Benjamini-Yekutieli step-up procedure with c(M) = sum 1/j - valid under arbitrary dependence, which is the case that matters when the candidates overlap - selects the discovery set at false-discovery rate q. Rules outside the set are silent until the next recompute; if nothing clears, the book is flat. The source's 1/i risk allocation across discoveries becomes an equal-weight vote here, because a single-symbol harness holds one position rather than i of them, and vote_min is how much of the funded book has to agree. c(M)=1 in the grid is plain Benjamini-Hochberg, the positive-dependence-only version, so the sweep prices the Yekutieli correction directly. The source's quarterly cadence is not observable inside an intraday research window, so the recompute is every 250 bars over a 1000-bar evidence window, and the Newey-West lag is the textbook floor(4*(n/100)^(2/9)) = 5 rather than a lag chosen to manufacture significance. Worth knowing before reading its results: on the probe bars this family funds nothing at all on SOXL at any q, window or lag, because no rule's leveraged-ETF return stream reaches significance in a 33-day sample, and it therefore sits flat on that symbol. That is the procedure working, not a broken threshold - but it does mean a flat equity curve here is evidence of abstention, not of a signal that failed.
kept.source: Benjamini, Y. & Hochberg, Y. (1995), 'Controlling the False Discovery Rate', JRSS-B 57(1), 289-300; Benjamini, Y. & Yekutieli, D. (2001), 'The Control of the False Discovery Rate in Multiple Testing under Dependency', Annals of Statistics 29(4), 1165-1188. Applied to trading and factor discovery in Harvey, C., Liu, Y. & Zhu, H. (2016), '...and the Cross-Section of Expected Returns', Review of Financial Studies 29(1), 5-68 (their BHY-implied t-hurdle is 3.39 at FDR 1% as of 2012, versus 3.78 for Holm/FWER 5%).

kept.name: Netted Value-Momentum Combination
kept.note: Two rank signals at deliberately opposite horizons on one symbol -- a long-horizon VALUE measure (today's price against a price average lifted from deep in the past) and a 2-to-12-month style MOMENTUM measure that skips the freshest window -- each converted to a percentile rank and NETTED into a single weight before any order exists. Cheap-and-rising gets roughly double weight; cheap-but-still-falling cancels to inside the no-trade band and is never traded. AMP rank the cross-section of an ETF universe; this feed is single-symbol, so the rank is against the measure's own trailing history instead, which keeps the netting structure and the opposite horizons and drops only the cross-sectional part. Horizons are in BARS, scaled so value stays several times longer than momentum.
kept.source: Asness, Moskowitz & Pedersen, 'Value and Momentum Everywhere' (Journal of Finance 2013), equation (3): r_COMBO = 0.5*r_VALUE + 0.5*r_MOM; equation (1) for rank weights; p. 938 for the 5-year value proxy and the choice of MOM2-12 as the momentum measure (the paper explicitly defends 2-12 over 7-12, citing Novy-Marx 2012 and Goyal & Wahal 2012).

kept.name: ARCH-LM Clustering Gate
kept.note: Runs Engle's Lagrange-multiplier test for ARCH effects on a rolling window of the symbol's own log returns (auxiliary OLS of squared demeaned returns on five of their own lags, LM = m*R^2, chi-square(5)). A range-expansion bar is then traded WITH its direction when the test proves volatility clusters, and AGAINST it when the test says it does not -- the specification test picks the side rather than filtering the setup.
kept.source: Engle (1982), 'Autoregressive Conditional Heteroscedasticity with Estimates of the Variance of United Kingdom Inflation', Econometrica 50(4) - the LM test, T*R^2 from the auxiliary regression of squared residuals on their own lags. Chi-square critical values are standard table values; the two-branch regime switch is the harvested idea's synthesis.

kept.name: Gap Already Paid
kept.note: Conditions entry on what the overnight gap revealed. S = close above EMA(ema_n) with ADX(14) >= adx_min is evaluated at the last regular-hours bar of the session; at the FIRST regular-hours bar of the next session the normalised gap g = (open - prior close)/ATR(14) is finally observable, and the trade is taken only if the signed gap is below gap_max ATR. gap_max sweeps the paper's three arms: 99 is unconditional (A), 0.5 skips moves that already happened overnight (B), 0.0 takes only adverse gaps (C). Exit is the session close hold_days later, with the harness stop, so the gap condition is the only difference between arms.
kept.source: Lou, Polk & Skouras (2019), 'A Tug of War: Overnight versus Intraday Expected Returns', Journal of Financial Economics 134:192-213.

kept.name: Turnover-Penalised Sharpe Position
kept.note: The Deep Momentum Network feature set (volatility-normalised returns at five horizons plus three normalised MACD timescale pairs) driving a RECURRENT unit with a tanh output, trained online by gradient ascent on the differential Sharpe ratio of the COST-ADJUSTED return R_t = (X_{t-1}/sigma)*r_t - c*|X_t/sigma - X_{t-1}/sigma|. Note that the 1/sigma which scales the return scales the TURNOVER TERM too, exactly as the paper writes it - drop it and the penalty comes out three orders of magnitude too small to move anything, which is the silent way this idea turns into a plain momentum net. Cost sits inside the objective, not outside the backtest, so the unit learns not to move for signal changes too small to pay for the round trip and the position path goes sticky by itself. Position is taken when |X_t| > dead and goes flat inside the dead band, so the exit is emergent exactly as specified. SUBSTITUTION, stated plainly: the paper's LSTM is replaced by a single recurrent linear-tanh unit trained by the Moody-Saffell online differential-Sharpe update. A per-backtest LSTM fit is not affordable in family_init, and the objective, the turnover penalty, the feature set and the emergent exit structure - the parts the idea says are the novelty - are all preserved.
kept.source: Lim, Zohren & Roberts (2019), arXiv:1904.04912, turnover regularisation section - the cost-adjusted return formula with the c*|X_t/sigma_t - X_{t-1}/sigma_{t-1}| penalty is quoted from the paper's full text (ar5iv). Raising c to retail equity levels and selecting it on net out-of-sample Sharpe is my adaptation. Online differential-Sharpe gradient ascent on a recurrent tanh unit: Moody & Saffell, 'Learning to Trade via Direct Reinforcement', IEEE Trans. Neural Networks 12(4), 2001.

kept.name: Fractionally differenced z-score
kept.note: Lopez de Prado fractional differencing of log close. The weight recursion w_k = -w_{k-1}*(d-k+1)/k is truncated at |w_k| < tol; d is the SMALLEST value on the {0, 0.05, ... 1.00} grid at which an augmented Dickey-Fuller test on the transformed series rejects the unit root at 95%, fitted once on the leading in-sample block and then held fixed. Trades fresh crossings of a +/- z threshold on the standardised series. NOTE ON THE TRUNCATION THRESHOLD: the source specifies 1e-5, which on these sample lengths demands 2000-4000 taps - longer than the usable history, so every low d would be skipped and the 'smallest d' would be decided by the window length rather than by the data. tol is therefore swept at 1e-3/1e-4; 1e-4 needs ~500 taps and retains ~95% of the total weight mass. On the probe symbols the ADF t-statistic is strictly monotone in d, so the upward scan finds a genuine minimum, and the selected d differs by symbol (0.10 to 0.25).
kept.source: Lopez de Prado, 'Advances in Financial Machine Learning', ch.5 sections 5.4.2 and 5.5 (pp.78-83), implemented as FractionalDifferentiation.get_weights and frac_diff in mlfinlab/features/fracdiff.py, with the exact recursion weights_ = -weights[-1]*(diff_amt - k + 1)/k and the threshold-based truncation - source read from the archived mlfinlab-master.zip at https://github.com/mnewls/MLFINLAB. Referenced there to Hosking (1981), https://wwwf.imperial.ac.uk/~ejm/M3S8/Problems/hosking81.pdf

kept.name: Stop-cascade band above round
kept.note: Osler's stop-loss clustering: executed stop BUYS bunch just ABOVE a round number and stop SELLS just BELOW it. Buys a close that has just crossed up into the narrow band above a grid level on at least 2x the 30-bar median volume, and mirrors it below. Target is 40% of the way to the next level, plus an immediate ATR trail and a 20-bar time stop.
kept.source: C. L. Osler, 'Stop-Loss Orders and Price Cascades in Currency Markets', FRBNY Staff Report, https://www.newyorkfed.org/medialibrary/media/research/staff_reports/sr150.pdf - VERIFIED. p.7 and Table III: '14.3 percent of executed stop-loss buy orders have requested execution rates ending in the range [01,10], while only 6.9 percent of those orders have requested execution rates ending in the range [90,99]'. Abstract: 'The response to stop-loss orders is larger than the response to take-profit orders' and 'lasts longer'.

kept.name: Diurnal Volume-Pace Day Typing
kept.note: The intraday volume U-shape used as an integral rather than a point. For each time-of-day slot, the median completion fraction (cumulative RTH volume divided by the day's total) over the trailing 20 sessions gives a symbol-specific curve. At midday the day's realised cumulative volume is divided by what that curve times the 20-session median session volume predicts, giving a pace ratio. A hot day (>=1.5) takes session-extreme breakouts WITH the break; a cold day (<=0.70) takes the same trigger AGAINST it; in between it stands aside. One position at a time, reversals flip it, everything flat at the close. The 20-session curve is built on an expanding window with a 5-session floor so the rule is not blind for its first month.
kept.source: Synthesis. Grounded in the intraday periodicity literature - Jain & Joh, 'The Dependence between Hourly Prices and Trading Volume', Journal of Financial and Quantitative Analysis 23(3), 1988 (the volume U-shape), and Andersen & Bollerslev, 'Intraday Periodicity and Volatility Persistence in Financial Markets', Journal of Empirical Finance 4(2-3), 1997 (the deterministic intraday pattern and the case for deseasonalising by time of day). Cited from the literature, not re-fetched. The pace-ratio day-typing rule and the sign flip are the harvesting agent's.

kept.name: Strong Close Into a New Low
kept.note: Shorts the bar that breaks to a new N-bar low and then closes in the top of its own range (IBS above threshold) -- a failed flush whose bounce is already spent by the close. Optional 200-EMA downtrend filter and an optional intraday session window given in UTC minutes-of-day. Covers on the first close beneath the previous bar's low, which is a bar-versus-bar test rather than an indicator.
kept.source: StockSharp/AlgoTrading, strategy API/1501-1600/1598_10_Bar_Low_Pullback -- 'Low breaks the previous LowestPeriod bars lowest low; IBS > IbsThreshold (0.85); optional close below EMA200; exit on close below previous low'

kept.name: Lottery MAX fade
kept.note: Bali-Cakici-Whitelaw MAX. MAX(N) is the mean of the N largest returns in the trailing formation window - an order statistic of the return distribution's right tail, not a moment. The single-ticker variant: short when MAX(N) sits above the 90th percentile of the ticker's OWN trailing history of MAX(N), long below the 10th, held for one formation window.
kept.source: Turan G. Bali, Nusret Cakici and Robert F. Whitelaw, 'Maxing out: Stocks as lotteries and the cross-section of expected returns', Journal of Financial Economics 99(2), 2011, 427-446 - VERIFIED by reading the PDF at http://pages.stern.nyu.edu/~rwhitela/papers/max jfe11.pdf. Abstract: 'a negative and significant relation between the maximum daily return over the past one month (MAX) and expected stock returns. Average raw and risk-adjusted return differences between stocks in the lowest and highest MAX deciles exceed 1% per month.' p.2: value-weighted decile spread is -1.03%, four-factor alpha -1.18%, July 1962 to December 2005, and 'the results are robust to sorting stocks not only on the single maximum daily return during the month, but also the average of the two, three, four, or five highest daily returns within the month'. Underpinning theory: Barberis and Huang (2008) on probability weighting; Kumar (2009) on lottery-type stocks.

kept.name: Bayesian Run-Length Collapse
kept.note: Runs Adams-MacKay Bayesian online change-point detection on log returns with a Normal-Inverse-Gamma conjugate prior, and trades the bar on which the MAP run length COLLAPSES instead of incrementing, gated on the posterior putting more than 30% of its mass on a run of five bars or fewer. Direction is read from the new segment, so the rule is agnostic between continuation and reversal.
kept.source: Adams & MacKay, 'Bayesian Online Changepoint Detection', arXiv:0710.3742 (2007) -- run-length posterior, message-passing recursion, constant hazard.

kept.name: BVC Absorption Fade
kept.note: Bulk-volume classification turns each bar's volume into signed order flow, OI = V*(2*Phi(dP/sigma)-1). Kyle says price should move in proportion to signed flow; when the trailing 6-bar flow sits in its top decile of 500 bars and the 6-bar price response is under a quarter of an ATR, lambda has locally collapsed - something is absorbing. Fades the flow. Exits when the flow reverts through its own median.
kept.source: Kyle (1985), 'Continuous Auctions and Insider Trading', Econometrica 53(6) for the flow-to-price-impact relation; the absorption interpretation is my own synthesis - the testable formulation is flow in the top decile paired with a price response below a quarter of an ATR.

kept.name: Turn-of-Month Flow Window
kept.note: Pure calendar: long from the close of the second-to-last weekday session of the month through the close of the third session of the new month, with no indicator condition. Optional skip when the previous session's ATR/close sits above the 90th percentile of its own trailing history. McConnell & Xu's four-day turn-of-month window.
kept.source: John J. McConnell and Wei Xu, 'Equity Returns at the Turn of the Month', Financial Analysts Journal 64(2), 2008 - trading rules and magnitude VERIFIED via https://quantpedia.com/strategies/turn-of-the-month-in-equity-indexes/, which specifies 'Buy SPY ETF 1 day (some papers say 4 days) before the end of the month and sell the 3rd trading day of the new month at the close'. Mechanism: Ogden (1990) on standardised payment dates; Lakonishok and Smidt (1988) on calendar anomalies.

kept.name: Amihud Illiquidity Reversal
kept.note: Bar-based Amihud lambda: rolling mean of |log return| / dollar volume. Buys when that ratio sits above its own trailing percentile AND price is more than atr_d ATRs below its 20-bar mean -- a decline produced by very little money changing hands. Exits when the ratio falls back under its trailing median, or price reclaims the mean, or the clock runs out. The percentile is a true rolling rank over the trailing window, not a fixed cut.
kept.source: Bar-based Amihud lambda, AFML pp.288-289, implemented as get_bar_based_amihud_lambda in mlfinlab/microstructural_features/second_generation.py - source read from the archived mlfinlab-master.zip at https://github.com/mnewls/MLFINLAB.

kept.name: Corrado rank event trigger
kept.note: Both the entry and the exit are rank percentiles of the symbol's own abnormal-return distribution, so the rule has no volatility-scaling parameter at all and self-calibrates to a 15%-vol utility and a 90%-vol biotech alike. Rank today's abnormal return within the 251-value set formed by the est_win estimation-window ARs plus today's, giving Corrado's K = rank/(est_win+2). Fade the extreme: long when today is among the rank_k most negative and volume clears vol_mult x the 50-bar median, short on the mirror. The exit is a rank state, not a price - out once K has sat inside [band_lo, band_hi] for `consec` bars (the symbol is back in its own normal-return regime), with a hard max_hold and no price stop. DEPARTURE, stated: no SPY series reaches a single-symbol harness, so the abnormal return uses Brown & Warner's mean-adjusted model rather than a market model. For a RANK that is nearly free - AR_j = r_j - mu with the same mu for every j in the window, and rank is invariant to a common location shift, which is the whole reason Corrado reached for a rank statistic. What is lost is the beta hedge, not the score.
kept.source: Corrado (1989) rank test, K_i,t = rank(AR_i,t)/(1 + M_i + L_2), z = (K_bar_0 - 0.5)/S_Kbar, documented in full at https://eventstudytools.com/significance-tests. Recommended in Kothari & Warner (2006) footnote 6 for well-specified tests under increased event-period uncertainty.

kept.name: Sequential Probability Ratio Kill Switch
kept.note: Wald's SPRT applied at the STRATEGY level rather than the position level. The carrier is a declared Donchian channel break - the honest baseline in this corpus, named so that the only difference from the plain breakout is the test. Its first 20 closed trades are the validation sample and freeze mu_b and sigma_b; from then on every closed trade updates the cumulative Gaussian log-likelihood ratio of 'the edge is the backtested edge' against 'zero edge, same volatility', and the rule keeps trading while L sits between Wald's boundaries B = ln(beta/(1-alpha)) and A = ln((1-beta)/alpha). L >= A confirms and resets the test; L <= B kills the rule permanently - it flattens at the next bar and takes no further entries. The secondary floor is implemented too: a stationary bootstrap of the validation trades gives the 1st-percentile cumulative path at each trade count, and falling below it kills the rule even when the mean has not yet failed. Two parts of the source cannot be expressed here and are not faked: the 1.5x size-up on confirmation (the harness fixes the share count, so a confirmation only resets the test) and re-arming by fresh CPCV/CSCV validation, which lives outside any single backtest. A validation window whose mean log return is not positive arms nothing - there is no edge for H1 to name - so by default the carrier keeps running and the trailing window is re-checked after each trade until one qualifies; rearm=0 in the grid makes the first window the only chance.
kept.source: Wald, A. (1945), 'Sequential Tests of Statistical Hypotheses', Annals of Mathematical Statistics 16(2), 117-186, and Wald (1947), 'Sequential Analysis'; the boundaries A = ln((1-beta)/alpha), B = ln(beta/(1-alpha)) are Wald's approximations. The application to deciding when to stop trading a discovered strategy follows Harvey, C. & Liu, Y. (2014), 'Evaluating Trading Strategies', JPM 40(5), 108-118. The per-trade Gaussian likelihood-ratio construction and the bootstrap equity-path floor are the harvesting agent's synthesis.

kept.name: Consecutive Close-Above-Prior-High Exhaustion
kept.note: Counts consecutive bars whose close exceeds the PREVIOUS bar's high -- a strictly stiffer test than an up close, since the whole prior range was engulfed -- and shorts the first bar the streak reaches its threshold, optionally only beneath a 200 EMA. One entry per streak: the signal fires on the bar the counter crosses the threshold and never while it merely stays there. Covers on the first close beneath the previous bar's low.
kept.source: StockSharp/AlgoTrading, strategy API/1601-1700/1601_Consecutive_Close_High1_Mean_Reversion -- 'counts consecutive closes above the prior high and sells once the count reaches a threshold; position exits when price falls below the prior low; optional 200 EMA filter'

kept.name: Romano-Wolf Stepdown Multi-Rule Book
kept.note: Ten candidate rules run side by side and NONE of them is allowed to trade until it survives a family-wise-error-controlled test. Every rerun bars, each rule's per-bar return over the trailing win bars is studentised with a Newey-West HAC standard error, and B stationary bootstrap paths - the SAME index paths shared across all ten rules, so the procedure exploits how correlated near-duplicate rules are instead of being crushed by them - build the null of the max studentised statistic. Rules above the (1-alpha) quantile are rejected as genuine, removed from the active set, and the null is REBUILT over what is left, so the critical value falls and the second and third best rules get a fair hearing. Only the rejected set votes; the book is the equally-weighted net of their positions, and with an empty rejected set the book is flat and stays flat until a later rerun finds something. The k-FWER variant (kfwer > 1 uses the k-th largest bootstrap statistic) is the power-for-false-positives trade the idea lists.
kept.source: Romano, J. P. & Wolf, M. (2005), 'Stepwise Multiple Testing as Formalized Data Snooping', Econometrica 73(4), 1237-1282. Also Romano, J. P., Shaikh, A. & Wolf, M. (2008), 'Formalized Data Snooping Based on Generalized Error Rates', Econometric Theory 24(2), 404-447 (k-FWER and FDP-controlling variants that let you tolerate a few false positives in exchange for far more power).

kept.name: Shaved Heikin-Ashi body expansion
kept.note: Trades the GEOMETRY of a Heikin-Ashi candle rather than its colour. A shaved HA bar -- one whose HAopen equals its HAlow (long) or its HAhigh (short) -- means that across the whole averaging window every attempt to trade back through the open failed. Pairing that with a body strictly larger than the previous bar's by body_exp, and with a same-direction predecessor, isolates the part of a trend where participation is accelerating rather than merely continuing. The exit is the mirror shape with the body-expansion clause dropped, exactly as in the source. The 'within one tick' shaved test is expressed as tick_tol times the HA bar's own range so it is symbol-agnostic; tick_tol=0 is the exact equality. mode=-1 inverts the reading (a shaved expanding up bar is exhaustion, not thrust) so the sweep can tell whether the geometry is a continuation or a reversal object. The source's pyramiding on repeated entries is NOT implemented: the shared harness only averages into adverse moves, which is the opposite of what the source does, so faking it with max_adds would be a different rule. No stop and no target: the source has neither, the structural exit is the whole exit.
kept.source: je-suis-tm/quant-trading, file 'Heikin-Ashi backtest.py' -- the four-condition entry block (HA up bar, HAopen equal to the HA extreme, body larger than the prior body, prior bar the same direction) and the three-condition mirror exit.

kept.name: Turn-Of-Month Cash Cycle Window
kept.note: Pure calendar exposure: long from the (entry_off+1)-th-to-last trading day of the month through the exit_day-th trading day of the next, with an optional short leg over the following days. There is no price condition anywhere. Trading days are counted as weekdays from the date itself, which is a priori calendar knowledge -- exchange holidays are not modelled, so a holiday shifts the window by at most one session. Stated as a condition to be in, so exit_on_zero closes it when the window ends; the paper's 'no intra-window stops' is a sizing instruction, and the shared execution model is left alone so this stays comparable with every other family.
kept.source: Ogden, "Turn-of-Month Evaluations of Liquid Profits and Stock Returns: A Common Explanation for the Monthly and January Effects," Journal of Finance 45(4), 1990, 1259-1272; Etula, Rinne, Suominen & Vaittinen, "Dash for Cash: Monthly Market Impact of Institutional Liquidity Needs," Review of Financial Studies 33(1), 2020, 75-111

kept.name: Homing pigeon / descending hawk
kept.note: Two-bar body containment where BOTH bars are the same colour, which is what separates it from the harami (opposite colours) and from the inside bar (defined on highs and lows, not on the body). Long on Goo/Chen/Chang's O1>O2>C2>C1 with bar1 closing under its EMA(10); short on the mirror C1>C2>O2>O1 above it. Bar1's body must be at least min_body_atr x ATR(14) and bar2's at most body_ratio of it: a second down bar that opens above the prior close and still cannot print a lower close is a failure to extend. Nothing is asked of the highs or lows, so bar2's RANGE may exceed bar1's - that is the set of setups the inside-bar and harami screens both miss. Held `hold` bars, stopped 1 ATR out, no profit target.
kept.source: Goo, Chen & Chang (2007) formal definitions - Homing Pigeon: O1 > O2 > C2 > C1 & downtrend; Descending Hawk: C1 > C2 > O2 > O1 & uptrend - reproduced with the full pattern table in Tharavanij, Siraprapasiri & Rajchamaha (2017), SAGE Open, doi:10.1177/2158244017736799. Abnormal-return evidence for two-day harami-family patterns: Shiu & Lu (2011), cited therein.

kept.name: Correlated Cohort Decay Contagion
kept.note: Pools decay evidence across a cohort of economically identical variants instead of monitoring one rule alone. The cohort here is six RSI mean-reversion members (periods 5/9/14/21/34/50) computed on this symbol - the group that average-linkage clustering at rho=0.5 exists to discover, declared in advance because a single-symbol harness has no cross-idea return matrix to cluster. Each member's trailing Sharpe is compared to its OWN pct_win distribution; when the fraction of members below their own mem_pct percentile reaches dead_frac the whole cohort is DEAD, no member may open, and open members are flattened - killing a healthy-looking member is the intended behaviour. Revival needs revive_frac of members above their own median for revive_bars consecutive bars. The published size = base*clip(1-f_c,0.3,1) term is dropped because sizing belongs to the shared harness.
kept.source: Synthesis. The power-pooling rationale is the harvester's; the cohort-level decay premise follows McLean, R.D. & Pontiff, J. (2016), 'Does Academic Research Destroy Stock Return Predictability?', Journal of Finance 71(1):5-32, and Chordia, T., Subrahmanyam, A. & Tong, Q. (2014), 'Have Capital Market Anomalies Attenuated in the Recent Era of High Liquidity and Trading Activity?', Journal of Accounting and Economics 58(1):41-58. Magnitudes from Chen & Zimmermann, FEDS 2018-033.

kept.name: Bertram Cost-Aware OU Band Optimization
kept.note: SINGLE-SYMBOL ADAPTATION of a multi-symbol idea. The harness supplies one symbol, so the cointegrated second leg is replaced by the symbol's own trailing mean log price: x = log(C) - mean(log C, mu_win). Everything that makes the idea distinct is kept. An AR(1) fit of x gives theta = -log(rho) per bar and the stationary sd; entry a and exit m are then jointly chosen over a grid to maximise the RATE (m - a - cost)/E[T_cycle], with E[T] the exact OU first-passage time (pi^0.5/theta)*(F(w_m)-F(w_a)), F(w) = int_0^w e^(s^2)(1+erf s) ds, verified against the ODE it solves. The full cycle is a->m plus m->a, so capital's idle leg is paid for too. Bertram's Sharpe objective is not offered: at a zero risk-free rate it collapses to sqrt(E[T]/Var[T]), which is independent of the return per cycle and therefore ignores the cost term entirely - the rate objective is the one where cost bites. m* comes out well away from zero, which is the whole point.
kept.source: Bertram (2010), 'Analytic Solutions for Optimal Statistical Arbitrage Trading', Physica A 389(11); large-scale test with data-snooping controls in Cummins & Bucca (2012), 'Quantitative Spread Trading on Crude Oil and Refined Products Markets', Quantitative Finance. Trade-cycle decomposition T = T1 + T2 and the return function r(a,m,c) = m - a - c reproduced from Krauss (2015), FAU Discussion Paper 09/2015, section 4.2 (equations 22-24).

kept.name: Sector-ETF residual s-score
kept.note: Avellaneda-Lee: cumulate the regression residual over a rolling window, fit an AR(1) to it, and read the distance of the cumulated residual from its own OU equilibrium in units of the OU stationary sigma. Long below -sbo, short above +sso, closed at the paper's deliberately asymmetric levels (a short is covered further from zero than a long is sold), and NOT TRADED AT ALL unless the AR(1) coefficient is in (0,1) and the reversion time fits kap_mult times inside the estimation window - the paper's kappa > 8.4 on a 60-day window is exactly kap_mult = 2, so the gate is scale-free and needs no bars-per-year constant. The factor leg cannot be represented: the regression needs the sector ETF's series and a family here sees one symbol, so beta is 0 and the residual is the log return in excess of its own window mean. Everything downstream - the cumulated residual, the AR(1), the kappa rejection, sigma_eq and the thresholds - is the paper's. Overlaps the existing residual s-score family; what differs is that the no-trade condition is re-tested every bar and closes a live position the moment its residual stops mean-reverting, rather than a fixed multiple-of-tau clock.
kept.source: Avellaneda & Lee (2010), 'Statistical Arbitrage in the U.S. Equities Market', Quantitative Finance 10(7), 761-782 - ETF-regression variant; thresholds sbo=sso=1.25, sbc=0.75, ssc=0.50 and the kappa > 8.4 reversion-speed filter confirmed against the Hudson & Thames arbitragelab PCA-approach documentation (github.com/hudson-and-thames/arbitragelab, docs/source/other_approaches/pca_approach.rst).

kept.name: Stambaugh-Corrected Augmented Predictive Regression
kept.note: Bars are aggregated into blocks; a persistent OHLCV predictor (log price/moving average, log realised volatility, or log Amihud illiquidity) is fitted with its own AR(1), the persistence is de-biased with Kendall's small-sample correction, the corrected innovation is put on the right-hand side of the predictive regression as an extra regressor, and only then is the slope used. Long only while the bias-corrected slope has the expected sign AND its Newey-West t-statistic clears the gate AND the forecast is positive -- so the entry condition is a property of the ESTIMATOR, not of the price, and the exit is the slope losing its significance. Monthly rebalancing becomes one decision per block.
kept.source: Stambaugh, R.F., 'Predictive regressions', Journal of Financial Economics 54, 1999 -- the canonical statement of the bias. The implementation is taken from Amihud, Y., 'Illiquidity and Stock Returns', NYU working paper FIN-00-041 (JFM 5, 2002), pp.19-20, where the Kendall (1954) correction, the appeal to Stambaugh (1999) and the augmented model (11) with the AR residual on the right-hand side are all set out. Newey-West lag alternatives and the wild-bootstrap substitute are named in Neely et al., FRB St. Louis WP 2010-008, p.5.

kept.name: Diurnal relative volume thrust
kept.note: RVOL against a TIME-OF-DAY baseline rather than a flat moving average: for each intraday slot the expected volume is the median that slot printed over the previous lb sessions, and RVOL is this bar's volume over that. Entry needs three things at once - RVOL at or above rvol_min, the bar closing in the top clv_frac of its own range, and the close clearing the highest high of the preceding brk_n bars (mirrored for shorts). No entries in the first fifteen minutes or the last forty-five. Exit is the earliest of the harness time stop, RVOL under rvol_cold for cold_bars running, price trading back through the thrust bar's opposite extreme, or the session end; nothing is held overnight, and any bar outside 09:30-16:00 ET counts as session end. The slot baseline is built strictly from earlier sessions and the New York offset is derived from the DST rule rather than assumed. Measured on the four probe symbols the default gate fires 11-25 times per symbol over 33 sessions, so rvol_min 3.0 is a real threshold; rvol_min 5.0 in the grid is deliberately near the edge.
kept.source: Admati & Pfleiderer, 'A Theory of Intraday Patterns: Volume and Price Variability', Review of Financial Studies 1(1), 1988; Andersen & Bollerslev, 'Intraday periodicity and volatility persistence in financial markets', Journal of Empirical Finance 4(2-3), 1997, 115-158 (Fourier Flexible Form deseasonalization). The trading rule is a synthesis of the two.

kept.name: Midpoint reversal with spread hurdle
kept.note: Short-horizon reversal computed on the log range midpoint eta = (ln H + ln L)/2 instead of on the closing transaction price, and gated by a bid-ask spread estimated from the same bars. The estimator is the Abdi-Ranaldo two-day corrected form exactly as the idea states it, S_i = mean over the trailing mr_win bars of sqrt(max((c_d - eta_d)(c_d - eta_{d+1}), 0)), with the round-trip spread 2*S_i; the term for bar d needs eta_{d+1}, so it only enters S once bar d+1 has closed, which keeps it causal. Signal MR = eta_t - eta_{t-mr_look}, entry long on negative MR and short on positive, but only when |MR| both ranks above its own trailing mr_pct-th percentile and exceeds mr_cost * S_i. Exit is the harness time stop at mr_look bars, plus the family's own two: eta crossing back through its mr_win-bar mean (target reached) and the estimated spread more than doubling since entry. ONE SUBSTANTIAL DEVIATION, stated plainly: the idea is cross-sectional (demean MR across the liquid universe, take the 10 most extreme names per side) and this study runs one symbol at a time, so the cross-sectional demean is replaced by a demean against the symbol's own trailing mr_dm-bar mean of MR, and the 'most extreme names' selection by a trailing percentile of |MRdm| on the same symbol. What survives intact is the part the idea calls novel - the signal never touches a closing transaction price, and entry is priced against an OHLCV-estimated round trip. What is lost is the market-neutrality of the cross-sectional book. One measured caveat that matters for reading results: on 5-minute bars the estimated half-spread is 0.7 bp of log price on SPY and 8.5 bp on SOXL, while |MRdm| at the extreme bars is 10x to 500x that (median 20-25x), so the idea's stated 4x hurdle rejects literally nothing on a single symbol - in the paper the hurdle does its work by discriminating BETWEEN names of different spread, which a one-symbol test cannot reproduce. The default is therefore set at 16x, which rejects about half the candidates, and the grid keeps 4x so the non-binding case is measured rather than assumed.
kept.source: Stefan Nagel, 'Evaporating Liquidity', NBER WP 17653 (2011) / RFS 25 (2012) 2005-2039 - the transaction-price-versus-midpoint decomposition of short-horizon reversal. Farshid Abdi & Angelo Ranaldo, 'A simple estimation of bid-ask spreads from daily close, high, and low prices', RFS 30 (2017) 4437-4480, building on Corwin & Schultz, JF 67 (2012) and Roll, JF 39 (1984).

kept.name: Net-the-book internal crossing
kept.note: A pre-trade rule sitting in front of a book of K signals that share one ticker. Instead of sending each signal's desired change d_k, the book computes the NET D = sum_k d_k and the GROSS Gr = sum_k |d_k| and sends only D, so signals trading against each other inside the book cross for free instead of paying two round trips to end up flat. Two things then decide whether even D goes. BAND: suppressed unless the trade notional exceeds max(min_ticket, k_band * c^(1/3) * |current position notional|), with c an Abdi-Ranaldo close-high-low effective spread (the estimator EDGE generalises) plus a square-root impact term on the trade's own size against rolling dollar volume. MARGIN RULE: a net sell while at least one signal still wants to be long is slowed by `slow`, and symmetrically for a net buy against a standing short view - Novy-Marx and Velikov's screens, the mechanism by which a second strategy is taken on at effectively negative transaction cost. The surviving delta moves the book position P and the traded direction is sign(P) once |P| clears pos_min. k_band = 0 with slow = 1.0 and rebal = 1 is the un-netted control, plain sign-of-the-vote, so the sweep measures the rule against its own absence rather than only against itself. The internalisation ratio 1 - sum|D| / sum Gr is computed and written to the run log as the idea asks. WHAT IS NOT HERE, stated plainly: this harness gives a family one symbol and a fixed share size. D_i, Gr_i, band_i and the margin rule are all per-ticker in the source and survive intact, but the cross-ticker portfolio-risk bypass has nothing to act on, and a netted delta can only express itself as a change of DIRECTION rather than a change of size - so what is measured here is the turnover the netting and the band remove, which the harness does charge for on every fill, not the full share-level internalisation of a real multi-ticker book. The per-ticker stop bypass is the harness ATR stop, which liquidates in full and ignores both the band and the margin rule, exactly as specified.
kept.source: Novy-Marx, R. & Velikov, M., 'A Taxonomy of Anomalies and their Trading Costs' (NBER w20721), section 6 'Alternative Cost Mitigation Strategies': 'an alternative cost mitigation technique that allows investors trading one strategy to opportunistically take small positions in another at effectively negative trading costs. We call this technique trading one strategy on the margin of another, but it is also known in the industry as screens or filters. The screened strategies are enhanced by slowing sales (purchases) and short covers (shorts) when the screening variable is in the top (bottom) x%.' Spread estimator: Abdi & Ranaldo (2017), 'A Simple Estimation of Bid-Ask Spreads from Daily Close, High, and Low Prices', RFS 30(12), which Ardia, Guidolin & Kazak's EDGE generalises.

kept.name: PLS Supervised Predictor Alignment
kept.note: Three-pass partial least squares over an eight-column OHLCV predictor panel. Pass 1 gives each predictor a loading by regressing it on the return it is meant to forecast (this is what makes the dimension reduction supervised rather than PCA's variance-maximising one); pass 2 recovers the aligned factor by a cross-sectional regression across the predictors on those loadings; pass 3 forecasts the forward return from the factor, with the Campbell-Thompson wrong-sign fallback and zero truncation. Everything is recursive - a pair only enters the sums on the bar its forward return is realised.
kept.source: Huang, D., Jiang, F., Tu, J. and Zhou, G., 'Investor Sentiment Aligned: A Powerful Predictor of Stock Returns', Review of Financial Studies 28(3), 2015 (working-paper copy https://down.aefweb.net/WorkingPapers/w676.pdf): first-pass time-series regression eq. (4), second-pass cross-sectional regression eq. (5), closed form eq. (6); method attributed there to Wold (1966, 1975) and Kelly & Pruitt (2013, 2014). Campbell & Thompson (2008) sign restriction and zero truncation.

kept.name: Volume-conditioned momentum life cycle
kept.note: Lee & Swaminathan's momentum life cycle: the two diagonal cells of a return x volume double sort. RET is 12-1 momentum, close[t-skip] over close[t-mom] - 1; RVOL is mean volume over the last vol_n bars divided by the mean over the vol_n bars before that, the OHLCV proxy for turnover. Long only quiet winners (top RET tercile AND bottom RVOL tercile), short only loud losers (bottom RET AND top RVOL); the other seven cells are flat -- the LONG leg requiring LOW relative volume is the opposite of a volume-confirmation filter and is the whole point. HONEST LIMIT: the harness is single-symbol, so a cross-sectional tercile cannot be computed. The terciles are taken against the symbol's OWN trailing rank_n-bar distribution of RET and of RVOL, which keeps the double sort and the diagonal-cell rule but makes it a time-series rather than a cross-sectional strategy. The overlapping six-vintage book becomes the harness's single position with a bar-count hold.
kept.source: Lee & Swaminathan (2000), 'Price Momentum and Trading Volume', Journal of Finance 55(5), 2017-2069 -- the momentum life cycle hypothesis and the RET x turnover double sort. RVOL is the stated OHLCV substitution for turnover.

kept.name: Alpha Half-Life Surface
kept.note: Fires the reference signal -- a 20-bar Donchian breakout, close > max(high, t-20..t-1) -- and then deliberately WAITS `lag` bars before entering, dropping the observation if an opposite breakout intervenes. Holding is a fixed `time_stop` bars. Sweeping lag x hold IS the L-by-H surface the idea asks for; the tradeable output is the cell that survives. The 'clean pass' (no stop, no target) cannot be expressed because the shared execution grid always attaches an ATR stop and target, so what this measures is the dirty pass.
kept.source: Moskowitz, Ooi & Pedersen (2012), Journal of Financial Economics 104:228-250, read directly - for the lookback/holding decoupling argument. Garleanu & Pedersen, 'Dynamic Trading with Predictable Returns and Transaction Costs', NBER Working Paper 15205, August 2009 (later Journal of Finance), abstract read directly from the NBER PDF - for alpha decay as the quantity that determines a predictor's weight.

kept.name: Ornstein-Uhlenbeck residual s-score
kept.note: Avellaneda-Lee, one symbol at a time. Over a `win`-bar window the cumulative residual X is accumulated, an AR(1) X_{k+1}=a+b*X_k is fitted, and the score is s=(X_last-m)/sigma_eq with m=a/(1-b) and sigma_eq=sqrt(var(zeta)/(1-b^2)) - a deviation measured in units of the FITTED OU stationary sigma, not of a rolling sample sigma. The gate is the estimated speed of reversion: b must be in (0,1) and the implied half-life ln2/-ln(b) must be at or under max_hl bars (the paper's 'half-life under 30 calendar days' is ~21 trading periods). A wide residual that reverts slowly is explicitly not a trade. Fade at |s|>s_in, cover on the paper's asymmetric bands, force out if kappa collapses or after max_hold bars. DEPARTURE, stated: the harness serves one symbol, so the sector-ETF leg cannot be estimated or hedged; the residual is taken against the symbol's own drift over the same window, which is the degenerate one-factor case. Everything distinctive - the AR(1) fit, kappa, sigma_eq, the asymmetric bands - is intact. Measured on the probe bars, the fitted half-life runs ~5 bars at win=60 and ~10 at win=120, so the paper's daily 21-period gate passes 97-98% of 5-minute windows and barely bites; the sweep therefore carries 4 and 10 bars as well, which is where the gate is actually a gate.
kept.source: Avellaneda & Lee, 'Statistical arbitrage in the US equities market', Quantitative Finance 10(7), 2010, 761-782 (Crossref-confirmed; SSRN 2008 working paper). Entry/exit band values 1.25/1.25/0.75/0.50 are the paper's own.

kept.name: Universal Zero-Shot Bar-Flow Classifier
kept.note: Sirignano & Cont's feature set on bars -- log return, close location value, CLV-signed volume standardised by its own window mean absolute value, and window-standardised bar range -- aggregated over a `win`-bar window as drift t-statistics with FIXED population scales, fed to a three-class softmax, traded on the published thresholds: long when P(up) > p_min and P(up)-P(down) > p_gap, out after `hor` bars or when the condition reverses. There is no CNN, no LSTM and no training: this harness sees one symbol at a time and fits nothing, so the pooled model cannot be estimated here and the coefficients are fixed constants rather than learned weights. What IS tested is the paper's load-bearing claim -- one object with no per-symbol parameter and no per-symbol threshold calibration, deployed unchanged on every symbol, including ones it has never seen. Every constant here is shared by all symbols and the sweep changes them for all at once.
kept.source: Sirignano & Cont (2019), 'Universal features of price formation in financial markets: perspectives from Deep Learning', Quantitative Finance 19(9):1449-1459; arXiv:1803.06917. Verified from the paper: the universal model trained on all stocks beats asset-specific models out of sample, results hold for stocks not in the training sample, including a long price and order-flow history improves accuracy, and standard normalisations (volatility, price level) proved unnecessary. Their inputs are the full limit order book; the CLV and CLV-signed-volume bar features here are my substitution, since we have no level 2.

kept.name: TD Sequential nine-count setup
kept.note: Counts consecutive bars closing on the wrong side of the close four bars earlier -- no average, no band, no ratio -- and enters when the run reaches nine AND the geometric perfection condition holds on the lows of the last two setup bars against bars six and seven. Exits on the mirrored count. Purely ordinal, exactly as published.
kept.source: freqtrade-strategies, user_data/strategies/berlinguyinca/TDSequentialStrategy.py - https://github.com/freqtrade/freqtrade-strategies/blob/main/user_data/strategies/berlinguyinca/TDSequentialStrategy.py (implements Tom DeMark's TD Sequential setup)

kept.name: Kagi yin-yang thickness flip
kept.note: Builds a Kagi line from closes with a reversal amount of kg_mult ATRs, fixed at each session open. Turning points give shoulders and waists; the line's thickness state goes yang above the last shoulder and yin below the last waist and persists until the opposite condition fires. Entry is on the state flip, optionally only when the immediately preceding counter-swing was shallower than the median of its own recent distribution - sellers unable to force a full-sized retracement before buyers reclaimed the prior high. Exit on the flip back.
kept.source: Kagi construction and the yin/yang (thick/thin) shoulder-waist rules: Steve Nison, 'Beyond Candlesticks' (Wiley, 1994), Kagi chapter. Empirical work on Kagi in a systematic context: 'Performance of Pairs Trading Strategies Based on Renko and Kagi Charts' (2025), DOI 10.33138/2957-0506.2025.20.483. The shallow-preceding-swing filter is the harvester's synthesis.

kept.name: Causal a-trous scale disagreement
kept.note: Undecimated (a-trous) causal wavelet decomposition of log close. Trades when the coarse approximation S_J and the mid-scale detail sum D_j disagree: coarse rising while the mid scales sit in the bottom p-th percentile of their own 200-bar distribution, and the mirror for shorts. Shift-invariant and strictly backward-looking by construction, so there is no boundary leakage.
kept.source: Donald Percival & Andrew Walden, 'Wavelet Methods for Time Series Analysis' (Cambridge University Press, 2000) - the a-trous / maximal-overlap (undecimated) transform, its shift invariance, and the boundary-coefficient problem. Evidence on wavelet denoising of financial series: 'Can Denoising Enhance Prediction Accuracy of Learning Models? A Case of Wavelet Decomposition Approach', Forecasting 6(1), 2024, DOI 10.3390/forecast6010005 (open access). The scale-disagreement trading rule is my synthesis.

kept.name: Garleanu-Pedersen Aim Portfolio
kept.note: The Garleanu-Pedersen closed form on one asset. Three signals -- slow momentum, fast reversal, stretch from a long mean -- are z-scored over 252 bars; each gets an AR(1) persistence fit giving Phi_k = 1-rho_k; walk-forward OLS gives the loadings B of next-bar return on the signal vector; Sigma is the 60-bar return variance. The aim portfolio shrinks each signal by 1/(1 + (a/gamma)*Phi_k) (Proposition 4) and the position follows x_t = (1-a/lambda)x_{t-1} + (a/lambda)aim_t with a from eq. (9), so the trading rate is derived rather than chosen. Sigma being 1x1 is the honest cost of a single-symbol harness -- the cross-asset covariance term disappears, the alpha-decay shrinkage and the partial-adjustment rate, which is what the idea is actually about, do not. Entry when |x| exceeds thresh times its own trailing mean; exit_on_zero lets the position unwind when the aim decays back inside the band, which is the discrete version of the geometric unwind. The vol override (flatten when 20-bar realised vol exceeds vol_cut times its 252-bar median) is implemented.
kept.source: Garleanu, N. & Pedersen, L.H. (2013), 'Dynamic Trading with Predictable Returns and Transaction Costs', Journal of Finance 68(6): Proposition 2 eq. (7) and (10), x_t = (1 - a/lambda)x_{t-1} + (a/lambda)aim_t; eq. (9) for a; Proposition 4 eq. (14), aim_t = (gamma*Sigma)^-1 B (I + (a/gamma)Phi)^-1 f_t. Assumption 1: Lambda = lambda*Sigma.

kept.name: Dual-timeframe KST trigger
kept.note: Pring's Know Sure Thing on two timeframes at once. The fast KST (ROC 10/15/20/30 smoothed 10/10/10/15, weights 1:2:3:4, 9-period signal line) fires the trigger on the native bars; the slow KST (ROC 9/12/18/24 smoothed 6/6/6/9) is fitted to the close of every agg-th bar and must be both above its own signal line and above zero before a trigger in that direction is allowed. Entry also requires the fast composite to be rising on the crossing bar. Pring's daily/monthly pairing is preserved as a RATIO (agg, swept) rather than a calendar, because a family here is handed one bar series of unknown size; a slow value is attached only from the bar that closed its block, so no unfinished period is ever read.
kept.source: Martin J. Pring's Know Sure Thing. Parameters KST(10,15,20,30,10,10,10,15,9) for the short-term/daily version and KST(9,12,18,24,6,6,6,9,9) for the long-term/monthly version, the 1/2/3/4 weighting, the 9-period signal line, and Pring's preference for signal-line crossovers over centreline crossovers on longer timeframes - all verified from StockCharts ChartSchool 'Pring's Know Sure Thing (KST)' (fetched 2026-09-02).

kept.name: Kendall NET rank oscillator
kept.note: MyRSI -- the signed (CU-CD)/(CU+CD) oscillator -- passed through Ehlers' Noise Elimination Technology, a Kendall rank concordance of the last M readings against a straight line, so the reading is whether the oscillator has been ORDERING itself upward rather than where its level sits, achieved with no group delay. Long when NET recovers up through -thr, short when it rolls back down through +thr, each closed on the mirror trigger or after hold_mult * M bars. Sign convention follows Ehlers (NET = +1 for a monotonically rising input), which is what makes the paper's own trigger pair coherent.
kept.source: John F. Ehlers, 'NET - Noise Elimination Technology: Clarify Your Indicators Using Kendall Correlation', free technical paper at https://www.mesasoftware.com/papers/Noise%20Elimination%20Technology.pdf - including the stated simplification that sgn(y_i - y_j) is always negative because Y is a straight line, and the MyRSI construction (CU, CD, ratio of difference to sum) from Stocks & Commodities May 2018.

kept.name: Stationary bootstrap lower-bound Kelly
kept.note: Four ordinary candidate rules run side by side, each carrying weight set by the WIDTH of its own Sharpe confidence interval rather than its centre. At every recompute each rule's trailing per-bar P&L is resampled B times by the Politis-Romano stationary bootstrap - geometric block lengths of mean blk, which is what keeps the resampled series stationary and stops an IID bootstrap handing back a far-too-tight interval on autocorrelated P&L - and the rule takes w = clip(SR_lcb/SR_point, 0, 1) * f_kelly where SR_lcb is the pct-th percentile of that distribution. A rule with SR_lcb <= 0 loses its vote and sits out until a later recompute clears it again; dead_n > 0 makes that retirement permanent after that many consecutive failures, and it defaults to 0 because on a run with a few dozen recomputes permanent retirement empties the panel on one bad early window and the family stops producing data at all; with dd_stop on, a rule whose live drawdown over the same window length exceeds the dd_pct-th percentile of its OWN resampled drawdowns is halted for stop_bars, on the argument that a drawdown deeper than its history can produce is evidence rather than luck. Sizing belongs to the shared harness, so the risk fraction becomes the weight the rule carries in the vote and the traded signal is the sign of the weighted sum - which makes f_kelly inert (a constant cannot change a sign), so it is declared but deliberately not swept. Block sums come from prefix sums and one set of draws is shared across rules, so a resample costs O(T*q) instead of O(T); the price of that is that resampled drawdown is measured at block resolution.
kept.source: Politis, D. N. & Romano, J. P. (1994), 'The Stationary Bootstrap', Journal of the American Statistical Association 89(428), 1303-1313. Automatic block-length selection: Politis, D. N. & White, H. (2004), 'Automatic Block-Length Selection for the Dependent Bootstrap', Econometric Reviews 23(1), 53-70 (with the correction in Patton, Politis & White 2009). The under-betting rationale is standard Kelly estimation-risk analysis; combining it with a stationary-bootstrap lower bound and a bootstrap-drawdown stop is my synthesis.

kept.name: Principal-component SDF on the signal set
kept.note: Trades an eigenvector of the signal covariance matrix rather than any single signal. Ten deliberately collinear characteristics (five momentum horizons, a short-horizon reversal, realized vol, range position, a scaled MACD histogram and volume pressure) are rank-transformed, then turned into managed-portfolio return series F_j[t] = z_j[t-1] * r[t]. Every rebal bars, on a trailing win window, Sigma = cov(F) is eigen-decomposed by Jacobi rotations and the dual-penalty problem is solved in the eigenbasis, where D is diagonal, the problem separates and the LARS-EN solution is exactly elementwise soft-thresholding: b_p = sign(mu_p) * max(0, |mu_p| - g1/2) / (d_p + g2). That is Zou and Hastie's orthogonal-design case, not a substitution. gamma_1 is not gridded: it is set, as the idea specifies, to the value that leaves at most k_pc components non-zero, i.e. the (k_pc+1)-th largest |mu_p|. gamma_2 is a multiple of the mean eigenvalue so it is scale-free. The traded weight w = sum_p b_p * (sum_j Q[j][p] * z_j) collapses to one fixed linear combination of the characteristics between rebalances, and the position is its sign once |w| clears dead times w's own trailing sd. Both of the idea's kill switches are implemented causally: a block is not traded if the correlation between its top eigenvector and the previous block's falls below stab_min, or if the strategy's own realized signal-return series has a window t-statistic below sh_floor. WHAT IS NOT HERE, plainly: there is no cross-section. Kozak-Nagel-Santosh rank characteristics across stocks; with one symbol per backtest the rank is taken against the characteristic's own trailing history instead, and the 'stock weight relative to gross' deadband becomes a deadband relative to w's own dispersion. The PC machinery, the sparsity in PC space and the shrinkage are the parts that survive intact, and they are the parts the idea claims are load-bearing.
kept.source: Kozak, Nagel & Santosh, 'Shrinking the Cross Section', NBER WP 24070 section 3.2 and Figures 1b/3b; JFE 135(2):271-292 (2019) - 'even one PC is already sufficient to get close to the maximum OOS R2 and two PCs are sufficient to attain the maximum', while unregularised models with all factors 'perform extremely poorly'. Solver: Zou & Hastie (2005) LARS-EN, which in an orthogonal design reduces to soft-thresholding.

kept.name: Own-Footprint Decay Gate
kept.note: A propagator-model cooldown: every fill of our own leaves a residual footprint sigma*(q/V)^psi that decays as (1+lag)^-beta, and no new entry fires until the signed sum of those footprints has decayed below theta_foot * the 20-bar per-bar return stdev. The base signal it gates is a plain N-bar breakout, so what is being measured is the gate. theta_foot is swept below the paper's 0.1-0.5 band because 100-share slices against five-minute bar volume produce a footprint of order 0.01-0.05, where the published band would leave the gate permanently open.
kept.source: Bouchaud, J-P. (2009), 'Price Impact' (arXiv:0903.2428): propagator p_T = p_-inf + lambda * SUM G(N-n) eps_n v_n^psi with G(l) ~ l^-beta, beta = (1-gamma)/2 ~ 0.25, and the BARRA-style response R(dt,v) = A sigma sqrt(v/V). Motivated by Gatheral (2010), 'No-Dynamic-Arbitrage and Market Impact', Quantitative Finance 10(7); decay level sanity-checked against Zarinelli, Treccani, Farmer & Lillo (2014, arXiv:1412.2152).

cut.name: Dunnigan thrust after a held retest
cut.note: Dunnigan's pre-indicator bar grammar, run as a two-sided state machine. An N-bar low anchors a long setup; the market must leave that low by half an ATR and come back to within a quarter of an ATR of it without losing it (the TEST), or make a lower low and close above the bar midpoint and above the prior close (the CLOSING PRICE REVERSAL); only then does the first UP-THRUST - a higher high AND a higher close - buy. Short is the exact mirror around the N-bar high. Both legs expire if the grammar is not completed in time. Exit is the family's own: the first counter-thrust that also closes beyond the extreme bar of the move, or the initial stop at the tested low. The repeat-thrust pyramiding in the source is NOT implemented - the shared harness adds by ATR distance, which is a different mechanism, and faking it would test something else.
