cut.source: William Dunnigan, 'One-Way Formula for Trading in Stocks and Commodities' (1954), and his earlier Thrust Method; the clearest modern restatement of the thrust definition (higher high plus higher close), the 'test of the low', the closing price reversal and the repeat-signal rule is in Perry J. Kaufman, 'Trading Systems and Methods', in the chapter on event-driven trends. Dunnigan's original tolerances were stated in points for 1950s commodity contracts, so the harvesting agent pinned them to ATR fractions and bar counts to make the rule symbol-agnostic.

cut.name: VNET Depth Surprise
cut.note: Engle and Lange's question inverted: fix the price move, measure the volume it consumed. A price event completes when the log move from the reference close exceeds h = 0.25 daily ATR / price; over its span the tick-rule signed volume is accumulated and VNET is its absolute value. A rolling OLS of ln(VNET) on ln(duration), ln(mean bar volume) and time-of-day dummies strips out the mechanical determinants, and the residual z-score is the depth surprise: strongly negative (far less net volume than usual was needed - the book was hollow) fades the move, strongly positive (unusual size absorbed for the same h) follows it. Target and stop are both one h, plus a 20-bar clock. Two recalibrations, both stated rather than hidden: the 200-event regression window is cut to 60 with a 25-event floor, because 200 five-minute price events is most of a year and no window this study runs would arm the rule; and the event threshold is a quarter of a daily ATR rather than a half, because at a half a liquid symbol produces only about twenty events in two months, which is fewer than the regression needs. The mechanism - a price clock, signed volume per unit move, a residual against duration, size and time of day - is unchanged.
cut.source: Robert F. Engle and Joe Lange, 'Predicting VNET: A model of the dynamics of market depth', Journal of Financial Markets 4(2), 113-142, 2001 (https://ideas.repec.org/a/eee/finmar/v4y2001i2p113-142.html). Bar-level construction of the price-duration and the residual entry rule are the harvesting agent's synthesis.
cut.cut_reason: too few trades out of sample to score

cut.name: Haircut Sharpe Position Sizing
cut.note: Ten ordinary candidate rules run side by side. At every recompute their expanding-window Sharpes become single-test t-stats and one-sided p-values, get adjusted for multiplicity by Bonferroni, Holm and BHY against a trial count of `trials`, are inverted back to a haircut Sharpe, and become a continuous weight w = clip(HSR/sr_target, 0, w_max); the traded signal is the sign of the w-weighted vote, so allocation moves continuously with multiple-testing-adjusted significance instead of switching on and off, and a rule whose w hits zero on retire_n consecutive recomputes is retired for good (retire_n=0 lets a rule come back). Sizing proper belongs to the harness, so the paper's risk fraction is expressed as the weight each rule carries in the vote. The trial count is swept over 4/10/40 rather than the paper's 100/578/5000: at intraday sample lengths a multiplicity of 100 haircuts every rule to zero and the family never trades at all, which is Harvey and Liu's point but produces no data.
cut.source: Harvey, C. & Liu, Y. (2015), 'Backtesting', Journal of Portfolio Management 42(1), 13-28 - the haircut Sharpe ratio and the exact Bonferroni / Holm / BHY adjusted p-value formulas, plus the finding that the haircut is non-linear and that the customary 50% haircut is too punitive for high-Sharpe and too lenient for low-Sharpe strategies. PDF: https://people.duke.edu/~charvey/Research/Published_Papers/P120_Backtesting.PDF . Companion: Harvey, C. & Liu, Y. (2014), 'Evaluating Trading Strategies', JPM 40(5), 108-118.

cut.name: Nine Buying Tests Composite Score
cut.note: Wyckoff's buying/selling checklist as an ensemble score. Eight of the nine tests are computed on every bar - objective met, climax plus secondary test, activity on rallies vs declines, stride line broken, higher supports, higher tops, base forming, reward at least rr times risk - and the entry is the bar on which the total crosses up through thr. T7 (stronger than the market) is DROPPED: it needs a benchmark's bars and the harness supplies one symbol. That leaves a 0-8 scale, on which the paper's 7-of-9 becomes 6-of-8; the default is 5 because 6 fires only a handful of times per symbol on intraday bars, and the grid sweeps 4/5/6 so the cost of demanding more tests is measured rather than assumed. Exit is score decay to exit_thr, the T9 objective, or the structural stop beyond the 60-bar extreme measured at entry.
cut.source: The nine classic buying tests and nine selling tests are Wyckoff's, codified and published by Hank Pruden in 'The Three Skills of Top Trading: Behavioral Systems Building, Pattern Recognition, and Mental State Management' (Wiley, 2007), and taught in the Wyckoff Analytics / Wyckoff Stock Market Institute course material. The mapping of each qualitative test to a specific computable predicate, and the 7-of-9 threshold, are my quantification (synthesis).

cut.name: Point-and-figure triple-top breakout on ATR-scaled boxes
cut.note: A.W. Cohen high/low point-and-figure chart with the box set to box_atr * ATR and refreshed every box_period bars, 3-box reversal. Long on a Triple Top Breakout (the live X column clears the tops of the two preceding X columns), short on the mirror; the exit is a Double Bottom Breakdown, a structural column event rather than a price stop. Time is thrown away: a bar that does not move price by a box does not advance the chart.
cut.source: A.W. Cohen's high/low point-and-figure method; Double Top Breakout and Triple Top Breakout definitions verified from StockCharts ChartSchool 'P&F Classic Patterns' (fetched 2026-09-02): a Double Top Breakout is 'an X-column breaks above the high of the prior X-column' with an O-column between; the Triple Top requires two prior X-columns at equal highs and a third exceeding both, spanning five columns. Traditional box scaling from the ChartCraft table popularised by Thomas Dorsey; I substituted ATR-proportional boxes so the rule is symbol-agnostic and sweepable.

cut.name: Sum-of-the-Parts Multiple Reversion
cut.note: The return is forecast in parts rather than as one number. A 'month' is mbars bars; the multiple is ln(price) minus ln(its smooth_m-month moving average), the drift is the moving average's own average growth over drift_m months, and only the multiple-growth term is regressed. The anchor is state-conditional: the multiple is regressed on a contemporaneous OHLCV state variable (log realised vol, or log Amihud illiquidity), the residual says how far price sits from the multiple that state historically justified, and a second regression of realised multiple growth on the lagged residual - slope shrunk by n/(n+shrink_k) - says how fast that gap closes. Expected multiple growth plus drift, truncated at zero and divided by variance, is the weight; w>0 is long, w=0 is flat. PROXY: this bot has no earnings, so a long moving average of price stands in for the fundamental anchor, which is the part most in need of validation.
cut.source: Ferreira, M.A. and Santa-Clara, P., 'Forecasting Stock Market Returns: The Sum of the Parts is More than the Whole', NBER Working Paper 14571 (Dec 2008), published JFE 100(3), 2011 - read directly at https://www.nber.org/system/files/working_papers/w14571/w14571.pdf. The decomposition is eqs. (13)-(15), the 20-year moving average for expected earnings growth and the random-walk treatment of the dividend-price ratio are on pp.6-7, and the multiple-reversion route with its contemporaneous anchor regression eq. (17), residual eq. (19), reversion-speed regression eq. (20) and shrinkage eqs. (21)-(23) are on p.7. The substitution of a 120-month moving average of price for the earnings-based multiple is my proxy, flagged as such - it is what makes the rule OHLCV-only, and it is the part most in need of validation.
cut.cut_reason: too few trades out of sample to score

cut.name: Characteristic Pure Play (partial slope)
cut.note: Back-Kapadia-Ostdiek pure play, reduced to what one symbol can carry. Six OHLCV characteristics (momentum, short reversal, volatility, Amihud illiquidity, size, trend stretch) are winsorised and z-scored, then at each rebalance the TARGET characteristic is regressed on an intercept plus all the others and the residual is taken. By Frisch-Waugh-Lovell that residual IS row k of W_t = (X'X)^-1 X' up to scale: unit exposure to characteristic k, zero exposure to every other column. What does NOT survive the reduction is the cross-section -- with one symbol the panel dimension is time, so this is a partial-slope exposure and not a zero-cost long-short portfolio, and the row-of-W weights cannot be compared across names. The near-singular X'X exit is implemented directly as its cause: when the target's R-squared on the controls exceeds max_r2 the weights are noise, and the position goes flat. The ridge term on X'X is kept and swept.
cut.source: Back, Kapadia & Ostdiek, 'Slopes as Factors: Characteristic Pure Plays', SSRN 2295993 (2013), later in JFQA. The slope-as-portfolio-return algebra originates in Fama (1976), Foundations of Finance ch. 9, and underlies Fama & MacBeth (1973).

cut.name: Decay-Matched Scale-In
cut.note: Almgren-Chriss slicing with the signal's own decay as the second cost. One entry is split into M tranches taken at consecutive bar closes unconditionally; M=1 is the single-shot benchmark arm. Variant B's front-loaded weights w_i proportional to exp(-i/tau) map exactly onto the runner's geometric add_scale = exp(-1/tau), and total size is held constant across M so the sweep measures the SCHEDULE and not the size. Remaining tranches are cancelled when the signal reverses (exit_on_flip). Two honest gaps: the symmetric scale-OUT arm cannot be expressed -- the runner's only partial exit is ATR-triggered, not time-triggered -- so this file is the single-shot-exit arm only; and the 2-ATR stop is applied per tranche rather than to the average fill, because the runner stops each lot at its own entry.
cut.source: Almgren & Chriss (2000), 'Optimal Execution of Portfolio Transactions', Journal of Risk 3(2):5-39 - the impact-versus-timing-risk trade-off and the endogenous slice count. Garleanu & Pedersen, NBER WP 15205, for 'trade partially towards the current aim' as the optimal response to costly trading against a decaying signal.

cut.name: Full-Range Gap Continuation with a Gap-Fill Stop
cut.note: Oxford Strategies 'Gap Pattern Type A'. Enter when a bar's ENTIRE range clears the prior bar's entire range (low[i] > high[i-1], not merely the prior close) AND the bar makes a new `chan`-bar extreme. The exit is the non-fill of the gap itself: a stop one tick inside high[i-1], so the trade is a bet that nobody transacts back at yesterday's extreme. Held long -- the source found longer holds preferred -- with a 6-ATR disaster stop and no profit target. The intraday no-retest variant of the idea is the same rule at a finer bar size, which is what a 5Min/1Min run of this file already is.
cut.source: https://oxfordstrat.com/trading-strategies/gap-pattern/ - Gap Pattern Type A: long gap Low[i] > High[i-1], channel filter High[i] > UpperChannel[i-1] lookback 2-100, pattern exit 'one tick below the price gap', time exit 1-50 with longer holds preferred, ATR(20)x6 stop, rated B/C over 42 US futures markets. Type B (https://oxfordstrat.com/trading-strategies/gap-pattern-2/) uses the weaker Low[i] > Close[i-1] and rates C.

cut.name: Meta-Labelled Primary Signal
cut.note: Lopez de Prado meta-labelling. The primary (a 20/50 EMA cross, standing in for any of the existing families) sets the side; every primary signal is labelled by its own triple-barrier outcome (+tp*sigma, -sl*sigma, vertical at `vert` bars, sigma = EWM sd of log returns span 50); a logistic secondary is trained online on [ADX, ATR/mean(ATR,100), (C-EMA50)/ATR, ln(V/mean(V,20)), RSI, permutation entropy d=3 over 40 returns, hours since the cash open], using ONLY labels whose vertical barrier has closed plus an embargo. A signal is taken only when the secondary's probability clears the cut, and the exit is the same three barriers the label used, honoured through exit_signal plus a time_stop. ONE DELIBERATE DEPARTURE: the published cut of 0.55 is applied as a lift over the training base rate, cut = 2*base*thresh, which is exactly p > thresh when the labels are balanced. Measured on real bars the triple-barrier base rate is 0.35 on SPY and 0.18 on XLU under the 2:1 barrier, so a fixed 0.55 takes 10% of SPY signals and none at all of XLU's -- an absolute cut is not comparable across symbols or across barrier settings, and the family would be dead on most of its own grid. Not implemented: probability-proportional sizing, because size belongs to the shared runner. Note the exec grid can override tp_atr/st_atr and add a second, ATR-based exit on top of the barriers.
cut.source: Lopez de Prado, Advances in Financial Machine Learning (Wiley, 2018), Ch. 3 (triple-barrier labelling, getEvents/getBins) and section 3.6 (meta-labelling); purging and embargo from Ch. 7. Empirical evaluation: Hudson & Thames, 'Does Meta Labeling Add to Signal Efficacy?'.

cut.name: Multinomial Four-Level VaR Shape Monitor
cut.note: A four-level VaR backtest used as a REGIME DIAGNOSTIC over an ordinary trend participation. Each bar an EWMA-t model forecasts VaR at alpha_j = alpha + (j-1)/N*(1-alpha); X_t counts how many levels the loss pierced; the trailing cell histogram O_0..O_N is tested by the Nass-corrected Pearson statistic against its multinomial expectation. Passing = full size. Reject with the DEEP cell hot and the shallow cell normal = deep-tail misfit: half size, 1.5x rung spacing, no adds, and flatten if it persists. Reject with the SHALLOW cell hot and the deep cell normal = vol-model misfit: full size, lookbacks halved, stop tightened to 1.5 ATR. The trend rule underneath is deliberately plain -- the family IS the monitor and the two opposite responses it prescribes.
cut.source: Kratz, Lok & McNeil (2018), 'Multinomial VaR backtests: a simple implicit approach to backtesting expected shortfall', J. Banking & Finance 88; arXiv:1611.04851 - level construction eq. (2.1), Pearson statistic eq. (2.4), the Nass correction with c = 2E[S]/Var(S), nu = c*E[S], and the finding that N >= 4 dominates the binomial exception test. The ES approximation eq. (1.1) is from Emmer, Kratz & Tasche (2015).

cut.name: Spread Regime Passive-Aggressive Switch
cut.note: An entry-side execution regime switch wrapped around a plain EMA-cross primary. The effective spread is estimated from OHLC alone (Abdi-Ranaldo form, the estimator EDGE generalises) over `edge_win` bars and ranked against its own trailing `rank_win` values; participation is the order size over the 20-bar average bar volume. Wide spread AND small order: post a limit half a spread inside and wait `wait` bars -- if no bar trades through it the TRADE IS SKIPPED, never converted to a market order. Otherwise cross at once. Two honest limits of the harness: the shared runner owns fills, so a touched limit is taken at the next open rather than at the limit price (a conservative version of the same trade), and the mirrored exit branch cannot be expressed because exits belong to the runner -- which matches the rule anyway, since exits always complete.
cut.source: Synthesis grounded in Ardia, D., Guidotti, E. & Kroencke, T.A. (2024), 'Efficient Estimation of Bid-Ask Spreads from Open, High, Low, and Close Prices', Journal of Financial Economics 161:103916 (OHLC-only effective spread; EDGE nests Abdi & Ranaldo 2017 and Corwin & Schultz 2012), plus the Roll (1984)/Hasbrouck (2009) effective-spread cost measure used in Novy-Marx & Velikov (RFS 2016), which caveats that it is 'the costs faced by a small liquidity demander' -- exactly the condition under which posting passively is viable.

cut.name: Adaptive bandpass trough cross
cut.note: Measures the dominant cycle every bar with Ehlers' autocorrelation periodogram - roofing filter, Pearson autocorrelation at each lag, a DFT of those correlations, 0.2/0.8 smoothing, then the power-weighted centre of gravity of the periods above half peak power - and tunes a band-pass filter to it. The output is normalised by its own decaying peak (automatic gain control) so the entry gate means the same thing on a quiet ticker and a violent one, and the trigger is a 0.9-scaled one-bar lag of the signal, which crosses it at the cycle's turning points. Long when the signal crosses up through the trigger while still below -gate. Holding period is 1.5 measured cycles, not a fixed bar count.
cut.source: John F. Ehlers, 'Cycle Analytics for Traders' (Wiley, 2013), autocorrelation periodogram and adaptive band-pass chapters. The harvester verified the correlations-then-DFT-then-0.2/0.8-EMA-then-centre-of-gravity pipeline, the beta1/gamma1/alpha2 band-pass coefficients, the default bandwidth 0.3, the 0.9*DomCycle scaling and the 0.9-scaled lagged trigger against github.com/thetestspecimen/ehlers-indicators-mql5, file mq5/ehlers_adaptive_bandpass.mq5.

cut.name: Deflated Sharpe arming gate
cut.note: An arming layer, not a price rule. Nine deliberately overlapping candidate rules (four breakout lengths, three trend crosses, two reversion rules) each carry their own mark-to-market P&L. Every ds_every bars the trailing window gives each candidate's non-annualised Sharpe, skewness and non-excess kurtosis, the cross-candidate variance of Sharpe, the mean off-diagonal correlation, the effective number of independent trials N_hat = rho + (1-rho)*M, the selection-bias threshold SR_0 and finally the Deflated Sharpe Ratio. Only candidates with DSR >= ds_arm trade; an armed candidate is disarmed once its DSR falls below ds_disarm, and the gap between the two is deliberate hysteresis so the gate does not itself become a high-frequency overfit switch. The traded signal is the net vote of the armed candidates, so a disarmed candidate's contribution disappears and the position flattens when the survivors no longer agree. CALIBRATION, STATED PLAINLY: the paper's own 0.95 arms nothing at all on intraday windows - across the four probe symbols the highest DSR any candidate reached was 0.82, so at 0.95 or 0.90 this family never trades. That is the deflation working rather than a bug, but a family that never fires cannot be measured, so the default threshold is set at the reachable end and the paper's values are kept in the sweep. Read a win at ds_arm 0.90 as the paper's claim and a win only at 0.60 as a weaker, relative-ranking version of it. The DSR arithmetic itself is exact: it reproduces the paper's worked example (SR 2.5 annualised, T=1250, skew -3, kurtosis 10, V=1/500) as 0.9004 at N=100 and 0.9505 at N=46, the two figures the paper quotes.
cut.source: Bailey, D. & Lopez de Prado, M. (2014), 'The Deflated Sharpe Ratio: Correcting for Selection Bias, Backtest Overfitting and Non-Normality', Journal of Portfolio Management 40(5), eqs. (1) and (2) and Appendix A.3 (effective N). PDF: https://www.davidhbailey.com/dhbpapers/deflated-sharpe.pdf . Underlying PSR: Bailey & Lopez de Prado (2012), 'The Sharpe Ratio Efficient Frontier', Journal of Risk 15(2).

cut.name: Two-speed Wald sentinel
cut.note: A parameter-stability test run on a sub-strategy's own P&L rather than on price. The monitored rule is a close-based breakout; its per-bar mark-to-market return is regressed on a constant over a rolling window of wd_T bars and, once per session, a Chow/Wald statistic is computed at every candidate break point in the symmetrically trimmed interior, with a Newey-West HAC variance at lag floor(4*(T/100)^(2/9)). The two statistics are given different jobs, which is the whole idea: the average Wald, which has power against small gradual parameter drift, governs position size, and the supremum Wald, which has power against a large abrupt break, governs the kill switch. Healthy takes every entry; decaying takes them at wd_frac participation; broken takes none and flattens what is open. Two honest deviations: fixed share size cannot express 40% of base size, so reduced size is expressed as deterministically reduced participation at the same rate; and rather than compute Hansen (1997) p-values or run a 500-draw stationary bootstrap per session, the statistics are compared against Andrews critical values directly, which is the same test (p <= 0.05 iff W >= crit) without inventing precision. The sup critical values are Andrews (1993) for one parameter with 15% trimming (8.85 at 5%, 12.35 at 1%); the average-Wald critical value could not be re-verified against a primary table here, so it is swept rather than treated as exact, with 2.3 / 3.1 / 4.22 standing in for the idea's 20% / 10% / 5% de-sizing levels. Measured on the probe symbols, supW runs 1.1 to 16.2 and avgW 0.12 to 6.1, so both thresholds sit inside the range real data produces rather than above it. One measured caveat worth knowing before reading results: at the default 5% kill threshold the decaying state never actually appears on the probe window, because a drift large enough to lift avgW almost always lifts supW too and the kill fires first; move the kill to the 1% level and the de-sizing leg starts doing work, so the grid sweeps that corner deliberately.
cut.source: Andrews, D.W.K. (1993), 'Tests for parameter instability and structural change with unknown change point', Econometrica 61:821-856; Andrews & Ploberger (1994) Econometrica 62:1383-1414; Hansen, B.E. (1997) JBES 15:60-67 for the p-value approximation. Implementation conventions (15% default trimming, avg/exp/sup variants) from the Stata manual entry estat sbsingle, https://www.stata.com/manuals/tsestatsbsingle.pdf

cut.name: Weis Wave swing volume divergence
cut.note: Segments price into waves with an ATR zigzag on the close, then compares each completed leg with the previous leg in the same direction: same ground covered (travel >= previous) on materially less volume (wave volume <= 0.70x) is Wyckoff effort-versus-result at swing scale, so the leg is faded. Holding period is measured in waves - the trade is closed when the next wave running in its direction completes.
cut.source: David Weis's Weis Wave, a computerisation of the wave charts in Wyckoff's course; see Weis, 'Trades About to Happen' (Wiley, 2013). The harvester could not retrieve a primary page for the construction and pinned the wave definition to a 2.0-ATR zigzag itself; that segmentation is the harvester's choice, not Weis's.

cut.name: BVC-VPIN Toxicity Continuation
cut.note: Bulk volume classification splits each bar's volume into buy and sell halves with Phi(dP/sigma), those halves are accumulated in volume buckets of ADV/50 (a bar's volume and its buy fraction are pro-rated across a bucket boundary), and VPIN is the mean absolute bucket imbalance over 50 buckets. Trades the continuation when VPIN is in its own top decile over the prior 250 buckets and the bucket was one-sided in the same direction as its price move. Runs on a volume clock, not a time clock.
cut.source: Easley, Lopez de Prado & O'Hara (2012), 'Flow Toxicity and Liquidity in a High-Frequency World', Review of Financial Studies 25(5); SSRN 1695596 and the NYU Stern working copy at stern.nyu.edu/sites/default/files/assets/documents/con_035928.pdf. BVC buy-fraction f = Phi(dP/sigma_dP) and VPIN = (1/n) sum |V^B - V^S| / V confirmed against the same paper's implementations.

cut.name: Gamma Regime Router
cut.note: Lag-1 autocorrelation of intra-session log returns, fixed once per session from prior sessions only, decides WHICH rule runs today: positive rho (short-gamma, amplifying dealers) trades the break of the prior N-bar extreme, negative rho (long-gamma, dampening dealers) fades it and needs the level reclaimed. |rho| below the threshold stands aside. The paper's cross-sectional dollar-volume filter is omitted -- it needs the whole universe, and a family only sees one symbol.
cut.source: Barbon & Buraschi (2021), 'Gamma Fragility', working paper. Full text read at https://abarbon.com/assets/Barbon_Buraschi_2021_Gamma_Fragility.pdf - autocorrelation/gamma-imbalance panel regressions, persistence of rho (t=32.17), peak at h=60 minutes, stronger for illiquid stocks.

cut.name: Order-Sign Long-Memory Follow
cut.note: Estimates the Hurst exponent of the BVC order-sign series by detrended fluctuation analysis over a rolling window, and follows a one-sided run of signs only while H is high FOR THIS NAME -- its own trailing percentile, plus an absolute floor at 0.50. The absolute 0.60 in the source is a tick-level order-sign figure; a DFA of 5-minute bar signs sits near 0.49 with a 95th percentile of about 0.56 on real bars, so a fixed 0.60 gate would never fire. DFA is computed from prefix sums (the linear detrend absorbs the affine difference between the integrated series and the raw cumulative sum), which is what keeps family_init cheap.
cut.source: Lillo & Farmer (2004), 'The Long Memory of the Efficient Market', Studies in Nonlinear Dynamics & Econometrics 8(3); Santa Fe Institute working paper 03-12-066 (sfi-edu.s3.amazonaws.com/sfi-edu/production/uploads/sfi-com/dev/uploads/filer/d0/d9/d0d92e50-17b7-4072-98a7-293ca01b8d89/03-12-066.pdf); the order-splitting mechanism is from Lillo, Mike & Farmer (2005).

cut.name: Close-Location Absorption Run
cut.note: A run of bars that keep closing near their high (CLV >= threshold each bar, mean above it) while the net close-to-close change is under a fraction of ATR, on wide bars and heavy volume -- the Volume-Spread-Analysis reading of a large seller being absorbed. Entry is the stop order through the run's extreme; the exit is a decisive close on the wrong end, the run's own low, or 10 bars.
cut.source: Synthesis. The CLV statistic is the standard close-location term from the Williams Accumulation/Distribution and Chaikin Accumulation-Distribution Line constructions; the absorption reading (strong closes with no net price change on heavy volume) is the Volume Spread Analysis interpretation from Tom Williams, 'Master the Markets' (1993). The specific inequalities, the flat-price constraint and the CLV-based exit are my own quantification and have not, to my knowledge, been published or tested in this form.

cut.name: Volume-Profile Max-Pain Wall
cut.note: Trailing-session volume snapped to the option strike lattice; the heaviest grid level within a few strikes of price stands in for the largest open-interest strike. Over the sessions running into monthly expiry, trade TOWARD that level whenever price is more than a fraction of a strike interval away, out at convergence, at the expiry close, or on a fixed strike-fraction stop.
cut.source: Ni, Pearson & Poteshman (2005), JFE 78(1), 49-87 - Figure 6 Panel A (clustering conditional on market makers holding net purchased positions, spike ~2% vs ~1% unconditional, and elevated levels on pre-expiration dates). Max-pain framing is practitioner; the volume-profile-snapped-to-strike-grid proxy is my synthesis.

cut.name: Kernel-Regression Smoothed Extremum
cut.note: Fits a one-sided Nadaraya-Watson kernel regression of close on time over a trailing window, picks the bandwidth by leave-one-out CV and then deliberately under-smooths it by 0.3x as Lo-Mamaysky-Wang do, and buys a local minimum of that nonparametric conditional mean once it is confirmed two bars later. Exit is the next opposing extremum. Note on the bandwidth: on intraday prices LOO-CV selects the smallest admissible bandwidth (a near-martingale is best predicted by its immediate neighbours), so 0.3 x h_cv leaves the fit close to an interpolator; the multiplier is therefore swept above 1 as well, which the idea's own parameter list allows.
cut.source: Lo, Mamaysky & Wang, 'Foundations of Technical Analysis', NBER WP 7613 / Journal of Finance 55(4) 2000, 1705-1765. Causal window, confirmation lag and CV cadence are the harvester's own construction.

cut.name: Kyle Lambda Shock
cut.note: Estimates Kyle's price-impact coefficient lambda as the rolling OLS slope of log returns on signed square-root dollar volume, then trades the direction of a large bar that occurs while lambda is both unusually high (z >= 2) and still rising -- the signature of a book that has thinned out ahead of a directional repricing.
cut.source: Kyle (1985), Econometrica 53(6); estimation form (returns on signed sqrt dollar volume, rolling window) from OFR Working Paper 15-11, 'Systemwide Commonalities in Market Liquidity', and Hasbrouck (2009).

cut.name: Model Confidence Set Volatility Ensemble
cut.note: Eight competing HAR volatility forecasts, each driven by a different realised measure (RV, subsampled RV, MedRV, MinRV, bipower, a pre-averaged MRC, a Parzen realised kernel, and a SHAR semivariance split), are scored every bar by QLIKE against realised variance and run through the Hansen-Lunde-Nason Model Confidence Set with a block bootstrap. The signal IS the model-selection step: go long only when the mean of the SURVIVING forecasts sits in the low part of its own distribution, and exit when the forecast that justified the entry is itself eliminated from the set for three consecutive updates. Transplanted to bar frequency, which forces four honest deviations: a 'period' is a rolling window of `period` bars rather than a trading day, sized at half a session from the bar stamps (so the measures overlap, and the bootstrap block length is set to that window to respect the dependence it induces); subsampling uses overlapping two-bar returns rather than a second, finer sampling frequency, which the harness does not supply; B is 100 and the MCS is refreshed every `mcs_every` bars rather than every bar, for cost; and the target_risk / sqrt(f*) position sizing cannot be expressed at all, because size is fixed by the shared execution harness.
cut.source: Hansen, Lunde & Nason (2011), 'The Model Confidence Set', Econometrica 79(2), 453-497 (T_max statistic, block bootstrap, elimination rule); motivation and the estimator comparison from Liu, Patton & Sheppard (2015), 'Does anything beat 5-minute RV?', Journal of Econometrics 187, 293-311.

cut.name: Conditional precision meta-gate
cut.note: Meta-labelling without a classifier. A primary long signal (Donchian upper breakout) is left untouched; what is learned is WHEN to obey it. Every primary signal in history, taken or skipped, is simulated through the same triple barrier the harness will trade (pt ATR up, sl ATR down, tb bars) and filed in one of nbuckets volatility buckets, the bucket being the percentile rank of the EWM(100) return stdev against its own trailing vol_win distribution. A fresh signal is taken only when the last `depth` COMPLETED trades from the same bucket contain at least min_n samples and hit the profit barrier more than prec_min of the time. Below the minimum sample it refuses rather than guesses. Only trades whose exit bar has already passed enter the ledger, so the gate at bar i is built entirely from outcomes known at bar i. Timeouts at the vertical barrier are scored by the sign of their P&L, as in AFML's getBins.
cut.source: Lopez de Prado, 'Advances in Financial Machine Learning', ch.3 meta-labelling (getBins case 2: 'bin in (0,1) <- label by pnl (meta-labeling)'), snippets 3.5/3.7 as reproduced at https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BlackArbsCEO/Adv_Fin_ML_Exercises/master/src/features/snippets.py. The ML classifier is replaced by an explicit bucketed frequency estimate so it is testable without a model - that substitution belongs to the idea's author, not the paper.

cut.name: Fade the close-on-the-low candle in an uptrend
cut.note: Buys the bar every shooting-star scanner reads as weakness: an open-at-high / close-at-low candle (Black Marubozu, Closing Black Marubozu or Gravestone Doji, selected by the pset bitmask 1/2/4) printing while price is above its EMA(10). Tharavanij et al. measured every bearish one-day pattern on SET50 names 2006-2016 and the nominal short lost money in all of them, so this takes the long side. No profit target by default: the published tables pair positive means with sub-0.5 win rates, a right skew a fixed target would truncate. Held `hold` bars, stopped at 2 ATR.
cut.source: Tharavanij, Siraprapasiri & Rajchamaha (2017), 'Profitability of Candlestick Charting Patterns in the Stock Exchange of Thailand', SAGE Open, doi:10.1177/2158244017736799, Table 2 (bearish single-day patterns, 1/3/5/10-day holds, SET50 2006-2016). Pattern inequalities from Goo, Chen & Chang (2007); EMA(10) trend definition from Marshall, Young & Rose (2006).

cut.name: Levered ETF close rebalance drift
cut.note: A daily-reset levered or inverse ETF must finish the session holding its multiple times the new NAV, so the required trade is always in the same direction as the day's move, scales with (L^2 - L) * AUM * return, and has to be done near the close. This measures the session move R against the symbol's own recent daily sigma at a bar trig_min minutes before the close and goes WITH the move when |R| > k_sig * sigma, flattening at the close (leg 1); leg2=1 then takes the opposite side into the next session's open to collect the give-back once the mechanical demand stops. The session close is located from the tape - the heaviest-volume bar in the back half of the session, medianed over the previous slot_days sessions - so no timezone table is needed and a DST shift is followed automatically. TWO HONEST DEPARTURES from the idea as written: R is measured on the traded symbol itself rather than on SPY, because a single-symbol harness cannot read another ticker (the same mechanism applies to any underlying with levered products on it), and leg 2 fills at the first bar after the close rather than at the official 16:00 print, because the runner always fills at the next bar's open.
cut.source: Synthesis of a documented mechanism. Cheng & Madhavan, 'The Dynamics of Leveraged and Inverse Exchange-Traded Funds' (Barclays Global Investors, 2009), derive the (leverage^2 - leverage) x AUM x return rebalancing formula and its end-of-day concentration; also the subject of SEC/FINRA investor alerts on leveraged ETFs. The idea's author could not re-fetch these in their session, so the thresholds and the two-leg structure are their construction on top of the published mechanics, not a rule lifted from a paper.

cut.name: Reflex versus Trendflex
cut.note: Ehlers' two oscillators that differ by exactly one term. The close is SuperSmoothed, then a difference-sum over n bars is taken twice: once with the linear slope of that window added back (Reflex, a detrended cycle reading) and once without (Trendflex, a trend reading). Both are divided by the square root of an EWMA of their own square, which makes them scale-free, so the zero line means the same thing on every instrument. Long when Reflex crosses above Trendflex with Trendflex positive, short on the mirror; mode=1 trades Reflex's zero cross instead. Exit is Reflex crossing back through zero.
cut.source: pandas-ta (fork gopalparashar421/pandas-ta), pandas_ta/cycle/reflex.py (np_reflex, slope-detrended difference sum) and pandas_ta/trend/trendflex.py (nb_trendflex, without it); paired as a crossover system in StockSharp/AlgoTrading API/1501-1600/1587_Reflex_Trendflex. Ehlers, 'Reflex: A New Zero-Lag Indicator', TASC Feb 2020.

cut.name: V-shaped selling pressure overhang
cut.note: The Grinblatt-Han turnover-weighted cost-basis distribution with the ABSOLUTE value taken inside the sum, so a name whose holders are half deep in gains and half deep in losses scores high while the signed capital-gains measure scores it near zero. Weights w_{t-n} = V_{t-n} * prod(1 - V) are built exactly as in the paper but maintained recursively (every stored weight decays by (1-V_t) each bar), and the turnover V is proxied from OHLCV as turn_c * volume / its own rolling mean, capped at vmax - single-symbol bars carry no shares outstanding. Short a rally running into a top-pct_cut overhang, buy a rally running into a bottom-pct_cut one. The paper's +3%-over-5-sessions rally trigger is expressed as rally_atr * ATR over rally_win bars, because a fixed 3% is unreachable on the intraday bars this harness runs and would make the family fire on leveraged names only.
cut.source: Synthesis extending the Grinblatt & Han construction (NBER w8734) with the V-shaped selling schedule of Ben-David & Hirshleifer, 'Are Investors Really Reluctant to Realize Their Losses?', Review of Financial Studies 25(8), 2012, 2485-2532 (cited by the idea's author from background knowledge, not verified in their session). The VSP statistic and the trade construction are the idea author's own. Related: An, Ang, Bali & Cakici on V-shaped net selling propensity.

cut.name: Hill-vs-EPD bias gap reliability gate
cut.note: Fits the trailing loss tail twice at six values of k -- the naive Hill estimator and the bias-corrected extended-Pareto ML (rho fixed at -1, profile likelihood, xi closed-form given delta) -- and takes the base long only while the two agree (BIASGAP) and Hill is stable in k (HILLDISP). Deviation, measured rather than assumed: on 5-minute bars the rho=-1 EPD-ML runs to its delta boundary and BIASGAP sits in roughly 0.3-6.0, not the paper's 0.15-0.30, so the gap thresholds are recalibrated to the observed range; HILLDISP keeps the paper's scale because 0.15 falls near its real quartile. The half-size step is dropped because sizing belongs to the harness; the 3-close persistence flatten is kept as the exit.
cut.source: Maribe, Verster & Beirlant, 'Reducing bias and MSE in estimation of heavy tails: a Bayesian approach', arXiv:1606.05687 - Hill estimator eq. (3), Weissman tail-probability estimator eq. (4), extended Pareto survival function eq. (6) and the EPD-ML bias-reduced estimator; the observation that Hill stability 'is not visible' in most cases motivates the dispersion term. Hill (1975) for the base estimator; Beirlant et al. (2009) for the EPD subclass F(xi, tau).

cut.name: Leveraged ETF rebalance front-run
cut.note: At a wall-clock trigger (14:15 ET by default) measure the day's move from the prior session's regular-hours close; if it exceeds the threshold, take the position in the SAME direction as that move and hold it to the close, because a leveraged fund on this underlying must rebalance (L^2 - L) x assets x r in that same direction into the last hour. Honest adaptation: the published rule reads the underlying and buys a different instrument (the 3x fund), and a family sees only the symbol it trades, so the day's move is measured on the traded symbol itself -- correct for an underlying or a long LETF, sign-flipped for an inverse fund, and the (L^2 - L) size scaling is dropped because sizing belongs to the harness.
cut.source: QuantConnect Lean, Algorithm.Python/Alphas/RebalancingLeveragedETFAlpha.py (docstring cites the leveraged-ETF rebalance literature; academic origin is Cheng & Madhavan, 'The Dynamics of Leveraged and Inverse ETFs') - https://github.com/QuantConnect/Lean/blob/master/Algorithm.Python/Alphas/RebalancingLeveragedETFAlpha.py

cut.name: Return-volatility hedge breakdown
cut.note: Shorts a new N-bar closing high when the normally negative return/volatility relationship has just broken down: rho over the last cwin bars is above break_thr having been below prior_thr within the last `look` bars, and the position is covered when rho falls back under `restore`. Honest substitution: the rule was written on SPY versus VIXY, and a family sees only the symbol it trades, so the volatility series is the symbol's own realised volatility rather than an implied one. The correlation-breakdown mechanism, the prior-regime requirement and the price-extreme anchor are all intact; what is lost is the option market's disagreement with the equity market, so this tests the leverage-effect breakdown and NOT hedging demand into strength.
cut.source: Synthesis. The mechanism rests on the well-documented, strongly negative contemporaneous VIX-SPX return relationship (the leverage/volatility-feedback effect described in the VIX literature and reflected in Cboe's own materials noting implied volatility rises when stocks drop) and on the standard practitioner observation that a positive same-day VIX/index co-movement at a new high reflects hedging demand into strength. I found no single paper that specifies this exact rule, so I have pinned it down myself and flagged it as untested rather than cite something vague.

cut.name: Signal horizon migration detector
cut.note: Measures WHERE IN TIME a signal's alpha sits: the rank information coefficient of a z-scored momentum score against forward returns at h in {1,2,3,5,10,20}, recomputed every step bars, with h* = argmax meanIC(h). The holding period is h* itself, so it contracts automatically as alpha migrates earlier; the signal is retired after retire_chk consecutive checks with max_h meanIC(h) <= 0. Honest adaptation: the paper's IC is CROSS-SECTIONAL across a 30-name universe, which single-symbol OHLCV cannot supply, so the IC here is a rolling time-series Spearman of the score against its own forward returns. The migration response is also partly the harness's: execution timing and position size are not the family's to set, so mig_mode=1 expresses 'cut size when alpha has migrated' as standing aside, and mig_mode=0 sweeps the same family with the detector off, which is the comparison that says whether the detector earns its keep.
cut.source: Volpati, V., Benzaquen, M., Eisler, Z., Mastromatteo, I., Toth, B. & Bouchaud, J.-P., 'Zooming In on Equity Factor Crowding', arXiv:2001.04185 (crowding measured from trade-imbalance fluctuations; momentum rebalancing = 1-2% of order flow and rising). The IC-term-structure migration statistic and the execution/holding-period response are my own synthesis - Volpati et al. use signed order flow, which we do not have, so the horizon shift is the OHLCV-observable consequence of the same mechanism.

cut.name: White Reality Check benchmark gate
cut.note: Five candidate rules are scored bar by bar against a benchmark (buy-and-hold or flat); every recheck bars a stationary-bootstrap Reality Check -- Politis-Romano blocks, ONE common index path across all rules, statistics recentred by the original sample mean -- tests the MAXIMUM of the five against the null that the best of them has no edge over the benchmark. The argmax rule is traded only while P_RC < alpha. Deviations, both for wall clock: the sample is capped at rc_n bars instead of expanding without limit, and B defaults to 200 rather than 1000. The seed is a recorded parameter.
cut.source: White, H. (2000), 'A Reality Check for Data Snooping', Econometrica 68(5), 1097-1126 - Corollary 2.4 and Section 3 'Implementing the Bootstrap Reality Check' (P_RC = 1 - M/N, the recursive V_k updates, q=0.1, N=500-1000). PDF: https://users.ssc.wisc.edu/~bhansen/718/White2000.pdf . Applied to technical trading rules in Sullivan, R., Timmermann, A. & White, H. (1999), 'Data-Snooping, Technical Trading Rule Performance, and the Bootstrap', Journal of Finance 54(5), 1647-1691. Bootstrap: Politis, D. & Romano, J. (1994), 'The Stationary Bootstrap', JASA 89(428), 1303-1313.

cut.name: Jump Share Collapse Continuation
cut.note: Per session, RV = sum r^2 and bipower variation BPV = (pi/2)*(n/(n-1))*sum|r_t||r_t-1| over the RTH returns; the jump share J = max(0,(RV-BPV)/RV) is the discontinuous part of quadratic variation. It trades the RETURN of a diffusive tape: the trailing mean jump share has collapsed to j_lo having been at j_hi within the last back sessions, taken in the direction of the multi-session drift. Thresholds are calibrated to what session-level J actually reaches on 5-minute bars (median ~0.01, 90th pct ~0.15); the paper's 0.08/0.20 pair belongs to a coarser aggregation and never fires here.
cut.source: Barndorff-Nielsen & Shephard (2004), 'Power and Bipower Variation with Stochastic Volatility and Jumps', Journal of Financial Econometrics 2(1), 1-37; and (2006), 'Econometrics of Testing for Jumps in Financial Economics Using Bipower Variation', Journal of Financial Econometrics 4(1), 1-30. Overview: https://www.researchgate.net/publication/5213484_Econometrics_of_Testing_for_Jumps_in_Financial_Economics_Using_Bipower_Variation ; threshold-bipower refinement for finite-sample bias: https://www.researchgate.net/publication/314836310_Threshold_Bipower_Variation_and_the_Impact_of_Jumps_on_Volatility_Forecasting

cut.name: Microstructure Noise Ratio Collapse
cut.note: Two-scales realized variance: RV on the native bar grid against the average of the k subsampled coarse-grid RVs over the same span, each rescaled to that span. With no microstructure noise the ratio tends to 1; bid-ask bounce inflates the fine grid. The entry is the COLLAPSE -- NR crossing down through nr_in having been above nr_hi within the last back bars -- taken in the direction of the last dir_lb bars, away from the open and the close. The fine scale is the bar the study runs on rather than 1-minute, because that is the finest grid the feed gives; the subsampled-average construction is otherwise the paper's.
cut.source: Zhang, Mykland & Ait-Sahalia (2005), 'A Tale of Two Time Scales: Determining Integrated Volatility with Noisy High-Frequency Data', JASA 100(472), 1394-1411 - the two-scales estimator and the subsampled-average construction. Signature-plot diagnostics for noise: Hansen & Lunde, https://public.econ.duke.edu/~get/browse/courses/201/spr11/DOWNLOADS/VolatilityMeasures/SpecificlPapers/hansen_lunde_forecasting_rv_11.pdf
cut.cut_reason: too few trades out of sample to score

cut.name: Ordinal-Pattern Continuation under Low Entropy
cut.note: Symbolic dynamics: the last dim closes are reduced to their argsort - one of dim! ordinal patterns, invariant to scale and to any monotone transform, so volatility is stripped out and only the shape of the sequence is left. Two conditions must hold together: permutation entropy over the trailing pe_win patterns sits below its own pe_pct quantile (the tape is measurably non-random), AND the specific pattern just printed has a forward hor-bar mean return over the trailing stat_win matured samples whose t-ratio exceeds t_min (so we know which way the inefficiency points). Direction comes from that 24-way lookup table, never from a formula. Exit is the same hor-bar horizon the edge was measured over, plus an ATR stop. Overlapping forward windows make the standard error optimistic; that is inherent to the rule as published.
cut.source: Bandt & Pompe (2002), 'Permutation Entropy: A Natural Complexity Measure for Time Series', Physical Review Letters 88, 174102. Financial evidence that under-represented and forbidden ordinal patterns index inefficiency: Zunino, Zanin, Tabak, Perez & Rosso, 'Forbidden patterns, permutation entropy and stock market inefficiency', Physica A 388 (2009). Intraday application: 'Applicability of Intraday Entropy for Trading During Regular Market Hours', Computational Economics, doi 10.1007/s10614-026-11347-2.

cut.name: Realized Skewness Percentile Reversal
cut.note: Realized skewness of intraday returns, RSk = sqrt(n)*sum(r^3)/(sum(r^2))^1.5, ranked against its OWN trailing history rather than a cross-section, so it runs on one symbol. Buys the low-skew tail and sells the high-skew tail, gated on median dollar volume not having thinned out, and held a fixed number of sessions because the published effect is horizon-bound. Windows are in RTH bars (78 = one session); the paper's 252-session ranking history does not exist in an intraday sample, so the rank is against a trailing window of the same statistic.
cut.source: Amaya, Christoffersen, Jacobs & Vasquez (2015), 'Does realized skewness predict the cross-section of equity returns?', Journal of Financial Economics 118(1), 135-167. https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/S0304405X15001257 ; working paper version: https://pure.au.dk/ws/files/67739582/rp13_41.pdf

cut.name: Confirmation Ladder
cut.note: Base state S = close above EMA(20) with ADX(14) over 25 (mirrored for short). Enters only on the FIRST bar of an N-bar unbroken run of that state, so N=1 and N=3 trade disjoint populations rather than being a threshold tweak. Holding period H is swept independently of N via time_stop -- the N-by-H response surface is the deliverable, and tying the two together is the error the source paper names.
cut.source: Moskowitz, Ooi & Pedersen (2012), 'Time Series Momentum', Journal of Financial Economics 104:228-250. Read directly from the published PDF; the argument that forcing lookback to equal holding period masks predictability is in the literature-review section.

cut.name: Fractal Dimension Regime Gate
cut.note: Keeps FRAMA's internal Hausdorff-style dimension estimate and throws away the moving average FRAMA exists to produce. D compares the summed range of two half-windows against the range of the whole: near 1 for a monotone path, near 2 for a space-filling one, so it measures how much of the distance travelled was retraced. D is direction-blind by construction, so the side is supplied separately by close[t] against close[t-N]. Exits when D turns noise-like again or the N-bar price comparison flips against the position.
cut.source: John F. Ehlers, 'FRAMA - Fractal Adaptive Moving Average' (mesasoftware.com/papers/FRAMA.pdf). The N1/N2/N3 definitions and D = log((N1+N2)/N3)/log(2) verified against QuantConnect/Lean, Indicators/FractalAdaptiveMovingAverage.cs. Using D alone as a standalone regime gate is the harvester's synthesis.

cut.name: Heikin-Ashi Shaven-Bottom Streak
cut.note: Trades the GEOMETRY of a transformed candle rather than a level: a run of green Heikin-Ashi candles with no lower shadow -- meaning the raw low never traded below the previous HA candle's midpoint -- and an above-average body. Mirrored shaven-top for shorts. Exits on the first HA candle that either turns against the position or grows a shadow larger than shadow_ratio of its own body. HA_close uses the current close, so every signal is a bar-close signal only.
cut.source: Heikin-Ashi construction is standard; for its systematic use and noise-reduction properties see 'Smoothed Heikin-Ashi Algorithms Optimized for Automated Trading Systems' (2018), DOI 10.31410/itema.2018.514, and 'Study of Heiken Ashi Candlestick for Noise Reduction' (2022), DOI 10.31730/osf.io/phejd. The shaven-bottom streak rule and the shadow-reappearance exit are the harvester's synthesis.

cut.name: Kalman Local-Linear-Trend Slope t-Statistic
cut.note: A two-state local-linear-trend Kalman filter on log close, with the per-bar observation noise set by the Parkinson range estimator so the filter automatically distrusts wide-range bars and trusts narrow ones. The signal is a SIGNIFICANCE TEST, not a level or a crossover: enter when the posterior drift crosses t_in of its own estimated standard errors, which needs no per-symbol retuning. Rbar is a TRAILING mean of the Parkinson variance so the filter stays causal.
cut.source: Andrew Harvey, 'Forecasting, Structural Time Series Models and the Kalman Filter' (Cambridge University Press, 1989), the local linear trend model and its filtering recursions; M. Parkinson, 'The Extreme Value Method for Estimating the Variance of the Rate of Return', Journal of Business 53(1), 1980, pp. 61-65. Combining the two and trading the slope t-statistic is the harvester's synthesis.

cut.name: Self-Adjusting RSI Bands
cut.note: Replaces the fixed 70/30 pair with 50 +/- mult times the dispersion of the RSI itself, recomputed every bar, so 'extreme' means the same statistical thing on every ticker and in every regime. est=0 uses the RSI's rolling standard deviation, est=1 its mean absolute deviation. mode=0 is the breakout reading (buy the cross ABOVE the upper band), mode=1 the fade (buy the cross back above the lower band).
cut.source: TradingView open-source: 'Self-Adjusting RSI (SARSI)' by everget. Exact Pine read from github.com/everget/tradingview-pinescript-indicators/blob/master/oscillators/self_adjusting_rsi.pine

cut.name: Attention U-shape fade
cut.note: Barber-Odean attention buying. Shorts a bar with abnormal volume (vs the trailing 252-bar mean) AND an extreme move measured in trailing-60 sigmas, regardless of the SIGN of that move - the U-shape is the whole idea. Covers on a fixed hold, or early once abnormal volume decays back to normal.
cut.source: Brad M. Barber and Terrance Odean, 'All That Glitters: The Effect of Attention and News on the Buying Behavior of Individual and Institutional Investors', Review of Financial Studies 21(2), 2008, 785-818 - VERIFIED by reading the PDF from Odean's Berkeley faculty page. Table 1 note: 'Abnormal volume is calculated as the ratio of the current day's volume ... divided by the average volume over the previous 252 trading days.' p.14: buy-sell imbalance is '+29.5%' for the highest-volume vingtile versus '-18.15%' for the lowest decile. p.16-17: for stocks sorted on the previous day's return, imbalance 'is 29.4% for the vingtile of stocks with the worst return performance on the previous day', drops 'to 1.8% in the eighth return decile' and rises back for the best - the U-shape.

cut.name: Information discreteness momentum gate
cut.note: Da-Gurun-Warachka frog-in-the-pan. ID = sgn(PRET)*(%neg - %pos) over the formation window, skipping the most recent month - a statistic about the PATH, not the outcome. Takes the momentum trade in the direction of PRET only when ID sits in the bottom quintile of the ticker's own trailing ID history (continuous information), and holds long, with no reversal exit.
cut.source: Zhi Da, Umit G. Gurun and Mitch Warachka, 'Frog in the Pan: Continuous Information and Momentum', Review of Financial Studies 27(7), 2014, 2171-2218 - VERIFIED by reading the PDF at https://academicweb.nd.edu/~zda/Frog.pdf. p.7, equation (1): 'ID = sgn(PRET) x [%neg - %pos]', where '%pos and %neg' are 'the percentage of days during the formation period with positive and negative returns' and 'PRET is defined as a firm's cumulative return over the past twelve months after skipping the most recent month'. Abstract: 'Momentum decreases monotonically from 5.94% for stocks with continuous information during their formation period to -2.07% for stocks with discrete information but similar cumulative formation-period returns.'

cut.name: Alpha-threshold smoothed label
cut.note: DeepLOB's labelling scheme made causal. l = (mean of the last k closes / mean of the k before them - 1), classed +1 / -1 / 0 against an alpha taken as the pct-th percentile of |l| over a trailing training window and recalibrated periodically, with an optional agreement requirement against the next-longer horizon, and the holding horizon set equal to the label horizon k. HONEST LIMIT: the published label averages the NEXT k closes as well, which is future data the harness rightly refuses, and no CNN/LSTM is trained here. What is tested is therefore the labelling machinery -- two-sided smoothing, a percentile-set alpha, three classes, horizon-matched exit -- not the network.
cut.source: Zhang, Zohren & Roberts (2019), 'DeepLOB: Deep Convolutional Neural Networks for Limit Order Books', IEEE Transactions on Signal Processing 67(11):3001-3012; arXiv:1808.03668. Read the full text (ar5iv) and verified: m_minus(t) as the mean of the previous k mid-prices, m_plus(t) as the mean of the next k, l_t = (m_plus - m_minus)/m_minus, three-class labelling at threshold alpha, horizons k in {20,50,100}, and the architecture (1x2 stride-2 convolutions over price-volume pairs, a 1x10 integrating filter, Inception@32 with 1x3 and 1x5 branches plus max-pooling, then 64 LSTM units). Applied here to OHLCV bars rather than LOB levels.

cut.name: Conditional Monday by week-of-month
cut.note: Wang/Li/Erickson's conditional weekend effect. At the closing bar of the last session of a trading week, take the sign of that week's close-to-close return and the calendar day-of-month of the next session: short a down week whose next session lands late in the month, buy an up week whose next session lands early. Held for exactly one session and closed on its 16:00 bar. 'Monday' is generalised to any session followed by a calendar gap of gap_days or more, so a Tuesday after a Monday holiday counts.
cut.source: Wang, Li & Erickson, 'A New Look at the Monday Effect', Journal of Finance 52(5), 1997 - documents that the Monday effect is concentrated in the last two weeks of the month; cited from the literature, not re-fetched this session (search budget exhausted). The prior-week-sign conditioning follows the conditional-weekend-effect literature (Jaffe, Westerfield & Ma and successors); the multi-day-gap generalisation of 'Monday' is my own tightening.

cut.name: Distribution into strength
cut.note: The OHLCV signature of contrarian short flow from Diether, Lee & Werner: a run-up over the prior `lookback` bars, then a heavy-volume bar that makes a new high, closes below its open, and settles in the bottom clv_max of its own range. Short only. The paper's +3% weekly advance is stated in percent of a DAILY bar; here it is carried across timeframes as a multiple of ATR, which keeps 'has advanced meaningfully' the same statement on 1-minute and daily bars instead of a threshold no intraday bar reaches. Every other condition is the rule verbatim.
cut.source: Diether, Lee & Werner (2009), 'Short-Sale Strategies and Return Predictability', Review of Financial Studies 22(2), 575-607 - full text read at https://scholarsarchive.byu.edu/cgi/viewcontent.cgi?article=10102&context=facpub, where relss_t is defined as shorted shares divided by traded shares on day t and the contrarian-then-predictive pattern is shown in their Table 3. Complementary magnitude from Boehmer, Jones & Zhang (2008), 'Which Shorts Are Informed?', Journal of Finance 63(2) - abstract via the OpenAlex works API. The OHLCV bar signature is my own proxy for their short-volume measure, stated explicitly as a proxy.

cut.name: Inventory retracement bar
cut.note: Hoffman's IRB. In an uptrend (close above SMA(n) and that SMA rising over slope_n bars) a wide bar whose ENTIRE real body sits in the bottom `wick` of its range is counter-trend inventory; trading through its high proves the selling was absorbed, so the signal fires on the first of the next `valid` bars whose high exceeds the signal bar's high by a tick. Mirror for shorts. Hoffman's unquantifiable '45-degree MA angle' is replaced by an explicit SMA slope test, as the source note requires. The resting stop order is approximated by the harness's next-open fill, which is one bar later than a real stop fill.
cut.source: Rob Hoffman's Inventory Retracement Bar. The 45% threshold and the 20-period MA trend filter as implemented in https://github.com/m-marqx/Inventory.Retracement.Bar.APP (signal when the wick reaches 45%, 20-period SMA trend filter, entry on a break of the signal candle's extreme, target as a payoff multiple of the signal candle's amplitude, stop at the signal candle's extreme) and the open-source TradingView implementations (e.g. script khxEdmoy, 'Rob Hoffman Inventory Retracement Bar', which computes x = low + 0.45*(high-low) and signals when open and close are both beyond x). Hoffman's original '45-degree MA angle' filter is unquantifiable and is replaced here with an explicit SMA slope test.

cut.name: BOCPD run length gate
cut.note: Runs Adams & MacKay's Bayesian online changepoint detection on the sub-strategy's own per-bar return series -- Normal-Inverse-Gamma conjugate model, constant hazard, the full run-length posterior propagated by the message-passing recursion and pruned to keep it cheap. New entries only while the probability that a break just happened is below p_gate AND the posterior predictive mean of the current run is positive; everything is flattened when that break probability exceeds p_flat, and the strategy stays flat until the new run has accumulated re_r bars and turned positive again -- no manual reset, because the posterior re-estimates the parameters on the new regime by itself. The paper's third output, size proportional to expected run length, is the one part not implemented: position size belongs to the shared execution harness, not to the signal. The gated rule is the study's own EMA-cross floor family, so what is measured is the overlay.
cut.source: Adams, R.P. & MacKay, D.J.C. (2007), 'Bayesian Online Changepoint Detection', arXiv:0710.3742 -- exact online inference of the run-length posterior via a message-passing recursion.

cut.name: Clark-West nested admission test
cut.note: Asks the question a book operator actually faces: does this candidate add anything the incumbent does not already have? The incumbent forecasts the next bar's return from standardised momentum; the candidate nests it and adds short-term reversal. Both are refit every bar on a rolling window, and the Clark-West adjusted MSPE differential -- which removes the estimation-noise penalty that makes plain Diebold-Mariano under-reject in nested comparisons -- is turned into a Newey-West t-statistic. The pair only trades while the candidate is admitted, at the sign of the augmented forecast, and only when that forecast is worth at least band_atr of one ATR; it is dropped and flattened when the rolling statistic falls below zero. holm_m is the number of candidates in flight: 1 is the plain one-sided 5% test, 20 raises the bar to 3.09.
cut.source: Clark, T. E. & West, K. D. (2007), 'Approximately Normal Tests for Equal Predictive Accuracy in Nested Models', Journal of Econometrics 138(1), 291-311. Non-nested case: Diebold & Mariano (1995), JBES 13(3), 253-263, with Harvey, Leybourne & Newbold (1997), IJF 13(2), 281-291.

cut.name: Pre-averaged drift burst entry
cut.note: The Christensen-Oomen-Reno drift burst test, built exactly as the paper specifies: returns pre-averaged with g(x)=min(x,1-x), a left-sided exponential kernel for the spot drift, and a Parzen-kernel HAC spot variance whose lag length carries the 2(k_n-1) correction for the serial correlation pre-averaging itself induces, so it does not fire on bid-ask bounce. Enters when the statistic exceeds the critical value AND cumulative session volume beats its own 20-day time-of-day profile; holds while the statistic stays above the lower (exit) level, flattens at 15:55 ET, and never re-enters the same direction on the same day. Bandwidths are in BARS, not seconds, keeping the paper's 1:3 drift/variance ratio; the critical values likewise cannot be the paper's tick-level 4.6/3.9 because at bar sampling the studentised statistic tops out near 3 -- cv is swept over the range the statistic actually occupies.
cut.source: Christensen, K., Oomen, R. & Reno, R. (2022), 'The drift burst hypothesis', Journal of Econometrics 227, 461-497. Estimator, pre-averaging, HAC variance and default bandwidth ratios as implemented in driftBursts in the R highfrequency package.

cut.name: MinBTL trial budget with 1/e stopping
cut.note: Rations the parameter search itself. Before deploying anything it counts the years of history available and solves Bailey/Lopez de Prado's MinBTL for the largest number of configurations that history can support, enumerates the config list in a seeded random order, capped at that budget, burns the first 1/e of them as pure observation, then deploys the first config that beats the best observed Sharpe. If none does it deploys nothing. A retired config is not replaced until MinBTL(N) years of genuinely new bars have accumulated. The deployed config is an EMA crossover, which is the study's own floor family -- the point being measured is the search budget, not the rule.
cut.source: Bailey, D., Borwein, J., Lopez de Prado, M. & Zhu, Q. (2014), 'Pseudo-Mathematics and Financial Charlatanism', Notices of the AMS 61(5), 458-471 - Theorem 3.1 (MinBTL). The 1/e stopping rule from Bailey & Lopez de Prado (2014), 'The Deflated Sharpe Ratio', JPM 40(5), citing Bruss (1984), Annals of Probability 12(3), 882-889.

cut.name: Minimum regime performance gate
cut.note: Gates a sub-strategy on the worst annualised Sharpe it has ever produced over ANY admissible one-split partition of its own history -- Alexander & Fabozzi's MRP1, a minimax over split points rather than a mean or a rolling window -- recomputed every recheck bars over the trailing history. No new entries while MRP1 is below the floor, and everything is flattened and the strategy retired for three recheck periods whenever MRP1 has deteriorated by more than drop_t against its reading three periods earlier, which is the paper's early-warning signal. The floor and the deterioration trigger are quoted in units of one segment's Sharpe standard error rather than the paper's raw -0.10 and 0.25: on multi-decade daily data one 500-bar segment's Sharpe has a standard error near 0.7, on this study's windows it is near 10, so the raw numbers would be a threshold no real window reaches. The gated rule is the study's own EMA-cross floor family, so what is measured is the gate. Only the s=1 split is computed; s>=2 is quadratic in window length and would dominate the run.
cut.source: Alexander, N. & Fabozzi, F.J., 'Measuring Strategy-Decay Risk: Minimum Regime Performance and the Durability of Systematic Investing', arXiv:2604.08356, Eqs. 3-4 and Exhibits 3-4. Code repository cited by the authors: github.com/nolanalexander/minimum_regime_performance

cut.name: Optimiser permutation test on shuffled bars
cut.note: Re-runs the WHOLE eight-config optimisation on Fisher-Yates surrogates of the same window -- bar (or whole-day) order shuffled, marginal return distribution preserved, re-cumulated from the window's own starting price -- and arms the winning config only when its in-sample Sharpe beats enough surrogate optimisations to give p < alpha. A second paired test holds the rule fixed and permutes only the returns, separating rule edge from optimiser greed; both must pass. Re-tested every refit window, disarmed at p >= 0.20. Default alpha is 0.10 rather than the paper's 0.05 because with P=20 the smallest attainable p-value is 1/21, so a 5% gate demands beating every single surrogate; 0.05 is in the grid. P stays small because the test costs P full sweeps at every refit.
cut.source: Masters, T. (2018), 'Permutation and Randomization Tests for Trading System Development: Algorithms in C++' and 'Testing and Tuning Market Trading Systems' -- the training-set (optimiser) permutation test versus the selection-bias permutation test. Related: Aronson, D. (2006), 'Evidence-Based Technical Analysis', ch.6.

cut.name: Time-series spanning-alpha residual book
cut.note: Four signal books on one symbol -- trend, momentum, band reversion, breakout -- each regressed on the other three over a rolling window. A signal is admitted only when the Newey-West t-statistic on its spanning alpha clears t_in, and what gets held is the RESIDUAL: the signal's own position minus its fitted combination of the other three, so the book is paid only for the part nobody else already owns. Weights are alpha_k / sd(e_k), the whole book closes when fewer than min_admit signals are admitted, and a dropped signal must clear t_in again to return. This is the single-symbol form: the cross-section is unavailable here, so the paper's stock-level weights z_{i,k,t} become timing weights. Defaults sit one t-point below the paper's 2.5/1.5 because over these window lengths the alpha t-statistic is close to a N(0,1) draw; 2.5 is in the grid.
cut.source: Spanning-regression standard from Fama & French (1993, 2015); formalised for model comparison in Barillas & Shanken, 'Which Alpha?', RFS (2017). Redundancy problem documented in Green, Hand & Zhang (2017), RFS 30(12):4389-4436, and Feng, Giglio & Xiu (2020), Journal of Finance 75(3):1327-1370.

cut.name: Extremal index cluster switch
cut.note: Ferro-Segers intervals estimator of the extremal index theta, computed from the inter-exceedance times of |r| above its own rolling 95th percentile, refreshed every re_n bars. theta is the extreme-value parameter for how much LARGE moves bunch, and 1/theta is the mean cluster size - a different quantity from GARCH persistence of the variance LEVEL. Low theta (extremes arrive in clusters) brackets the shock bar with a stop-buy at H+0.1 ATR and a stop-sell at L-0.1 ATR; high theta (extremes arrive singly) fades the shock into the prior close. Nothing is traded on non-exceedance bars or in the dead band between the two thresholds. Stated for daily bars; windows are expressed in bars because the study is intraday, and the estimator is scale-free. A bar where both bracket legs are touched claims neither, since the bar hides its own path.
cut.source: Ferro & Segers (2003), 'Inference for clusters of extreme values', Journal of the Royal Statistical Society Series B 65(2) - the intervals estimator of the extremal index reproduced above. Leadbetter, Lindgren & Rootzen (1983), 'Extremes and Related Properties of Random Sequences and Processes' - the definition of the extremal index. Cited from knowledge; the web search budget was exhausted before I could open these, so verify the two-branch estimator formula against Ferro-Segers before implementation. The trading application is my synthesis.

cut.name: Parkinson efficiency reversion gate
cut.note: Q = Parkinson range volatility / close-to-close volatility over a trailing window of regular sessions - a path-efficiency measure that separates a symbol which oscillated around its open all day from one that trended cleanly open to close, two cases no close-only statistic can tell apart. A session is OSCILLATING when Q sits at or above its own trailing percentile (self-relative, because the absolute level is a property of the symbol: XLU runs near 1.1 and SOXL near 0.7). Only then, and only between 10:00 and 15:00 ET, does it fade a stretch of one band away from the session open that closes back towards it, targeting the open, stopping at stop_mult times the entry distance beyond entry, and flattening at 15:50. Session windows are shorter than the paper-scale 20/120 because the study fetches 85-170 sessions, not decades; the percentile is expanding up to pct_hist so it forms early.
cut.source: Synthesis. The two estimators are Michael Parkinson, 'The extreme value method for estimating the variance of the rate of return', Journal of Business 53 (1980) 61-65, and the standard close-to-close estimator; their relative efficiency and the use of the range as a volatility proxy are established in Sassan Alizadeh, Michael Brandt, Francis Diebold, 'Range-based estimation of stochastic volatility models', Journal of Finance 57 (2002) 1047-1091. The RATIO of the two as a mean-reversion regime classifier, and the session-open reversion trade built on it, are my own construction and I am not aware of a paper that tests exactly this - it should be treated as an untested hypothesis rather than a documented effect.

cut.name: Pre-registered revival trial
cut.note: A strategy lifecycle, not a setup. A rolling t-stat of the sub-strategy's own per-bar return is the decay monitor; when it drops below kill_t the strategy is retired but NOT deleted - a revival trial opens on terms fixed at that instant: a hard deadline of trial_len bars, a running t-stat hurdle that cannot be claimed before min_k bars, and an abort drawdown of abort_pct of the trial's allocated capital (converted back to the strategy's unlevered return, since the trial runs at trial_size of base size). Clear the hurdle and it is promoted and the monitor restarts; hit the deadline or the abort and it is dead for the rest of the run, with exactly one trial per lifetime. A persistent Donchian state is the stand-in sub-strategy, chosen because it is always in the market and so has a well-defined return on every bar; the structure under test is the retire/trial/promote protocol, not that base. HONEST LIMIT: the size ladder (10% during the trial, 50% for 60 bars on promotion, then 100%) cannot be expressed - the shared harness owns share count - so the trial trades at full size and trial_size survives only where it belongs analytically, in the abort threshold.
cut.source: t-stat hurdle of 1.8 from Chen, A.Y. & Zimmermann, T. (2018), 'Publication Bias and the Cross-Section of Stock Returns', FEDS 2018-033 - among predictors that survive journal review, a low t-stat hurdle of 1.8 controls for multiple testing using the statistics of Harvey, Liu & Zhu (2015). The bounded one-shot trial protocol itself is my own synthesis.

cut.name: Vol-scaled time-series momentum
cut.note: Moskowitz-Ooi-Pedersen time-series momentum: the sign of the trailing k-bar log return, sampled at every reb-th bar, with h overlapping sub-portfolios averaged so entries and exits stagger instead of reversing in one bar - the position is the majority vote of the h live formation dates, and a sign flip walks the book out over h rebalances. The exact ex ante variance model (exponentially weighted, centre of mass 60, only returns strictly before the bar) is computed and used as a stand-aside band. HONEST LIMIT: dollar sizing belongs to the shared harness, so the inverse-volatility position size cannot be expressed; what survives translation is the tail of that rule, standing aside when sigma is in the top of its own distribution, which is where the sized position would collapse towards zero. The risk-free leg is dropped - there is no second instrument and it is negligible at these horizons.
cut.source: Moskowitz, Ooi & Pedersen, 'Time Series Momentum' (Journal of Financial Economics 104, 2012, 228-250; PDF fetched from https://w4.stern.nyu.edu/facdir/lpederse/papers/TimeSeriesMomentum.pdf). Section 2.4 equation (1) gives the ex ante volatility model with the 261 annualisation scalar and the centre-of-mass 60-day weighting; Section 3.2 specifies the sign rule, the position size inversely proportional to sigma_{t-1}, and the Jegadeesh-Titman overlapping-portfolio averaging used to avoid overlapping observations.

cut.name: Volume clock variance ratio
cut.note: Two resamplings of the same tape: the bars as they come (clock time) and the same volume repacked into equal-volume buckets of size V = the trailing median bar volume, splitting any bar that overfills a bucket pro rata and interpolating its close linearly to the split point. Q = RV_clock / RV_vol over a rolling window, percentile-ranked against its own trailing history. A high Q means price is travelling per unit of clock time far more than per unit of volume - moving without participation - so the last look bars' move is faded; below the low percentile nothing is taken. Built and traded inside the regular session only, because an extended-hours bar's few hundred shares make the bucket size meaningless.
cut.source: Motivated by Easley, Lopez de Prado & O'Hara, 'The Volume Clock: Insights into the High Frequency Paradigm', Journal of Portfolio Management 39(1), 2012 (SSRN 2034858). I attempted to fetch the SSRN page and received HTTP 403, so this is a bibliographic citation, not a verified quotation; the RV_clock / RV_vol ratio and the trading rule are my synthesis.

cut.name: Volume-conditioned autocorrelation switch
cut.note: Estimates the SIGN of the trade from the symbol's own history rather than assuming it. A rolling OLS of r_{d+1} on r_d and on (detrended log volume x r_d) is re-fitted every re_n bars; the t-stat of the interaction coefficient classifies the symbol LIQUIDITY-DRIVEN (c2 < 0, high-volume moves reverse) or INFORMATION-DRIVEN (c2 > 0, they continue), and anything in between is never traded. The identical setup - big volume, big move - then produces a long in one symbol and a short in another on the same bar. Prefix cross-products make each re-fit O(1) in the window length. Restricted to the regular session, which is what a daily bar is. Detrending is the literal trailing mean of ln(volume) as written; dv_diurnal=1 switches to a same-time-of-day trailing mean, which is the better reading of "typical level" once the bars are intraday, since a plain trailing mean there measures the diurnal U-shape rather than any volume surprise.
cut.source: Guillermo Llorente, Roni Michaely, Gideon Saar, Jiang Wang, 'Dynamic Volume-Return Relation of Individual Stocks', NBER Working Paper 8312 (May 2001), published Review of Financial Studies 15 (2002) 1005-1047. PDF opened this session (custom font encoding decoded); the risk-sharing-reverses / speculative-continues sentence and the small-firm and bid-ask-spread cross-sectional results are quoted from its abstract and introduction.

cut.name: Aim-Portfolio Partial Rebalancing
cut.note: Garleanu-Pedersen for one asset: compute the Markowitz aim weight each bar, then never trade to it -- move a constant fraction M of the way there, with M = (sqrt(k^2+4k)-k)/2 and k = delta*sigma^2/(2c), c the (high-low)/close half-spread proxy plus slippage. The weight path therefore decays exponentially toward zero whenever the aim goes to zero, instead of being cut by any rule about the position. A ternary signal cannot hold a fractional weight, so the emitted signal is 'the smoothed weight is above w_in' -- what is actually under test is the timing content of the trade rate M, which is what delta and cost_mult sweep. The cross-sectional z-score of the source becomes a time-series z-score of log price/MA.
cut.source: Garleanu & Pedersen (2013) 'Dynamic Trading with Predictable Returns and Transaction Costs', Journal of Finance 68(6) (NBER Working Paper 17777). Note: the NBER PDF fetched by the harvester returned unreadable encoded content, so the aim-portfolio and trade-rate formulas are quoted from the published paper rather than verified by fetch; the trade rate given is the standard quadratic-cost closed form.

cut.name: Gap-Cadence Event Calendar Run-In
cut.note: Reconstructs a recurring event calendar from the symbol's OWN bars: take the largest |open/prev-close - 1| jumps in a trailing window, keep the longest subset whose consecutive spacings all fall inside an admissible band, and forecast the next event at last + median spacing. Go long from entry_off bars before that forecast and exit exit_off bars before it -- always flat across the event itself. Self-falsifying: a forecast date that passes without a jump of stale_mult times the typical detected-event jump retires the symbol until a new event is observed. Spacings are in BARS, not sessions, because the probe data is far shorter than a quarterly cycle; on daily bars the band should be set to the 55-70 session spacing the source specifies, and the staleness reference is the median jump of the events the fit itself found rather than a 250-session median. Candidates are chosen with non-maximum suppression (min_sep bars apart, defaulting to half the low end of the spacing band) so that one violent event cannot occupy several candidate slots with its own neighbouring bars -- the source picks the 12 largest gap SESSIONS, which are distinct by construction.
cut.source: Beaver (1968) on announcement-period return variance and trading volume, cited in Kothari & Warner (2006) footnote 1. Frazzini & Lamont (2007) 'The Earnings Announcement Premium and Trading Volume' (NBER WP 13090) for the run-in premium. The gap-cadence reconstruction device itself is a synthesis -- no earnings calendar is available on this feed, so the event dates are inferred from the periodicity of the symbol's own overnight gaps, and the estimator is falsifiable.
