cut.name: Turtle System 1 loser-filtered breakout
cut.note: A 20-bar Donchian breakout that is only taken when the PREVIOUS breakout, phantom-traded whether or not it was taken, would have LOST -- entry at the broken level, 2N stop, 10-bar trailing exit, stop wins a tie. The 55-bar failsafe overrides the filter. State is the outcome of the most recent breakout that has actually RESOLVED by the current bar, so the memory is causal. use_filter=0 is the unfiltered Donchian control, which is the point of sweeping it.
cut.source: Original Turtle Trading rules as published by Richard Dennis's students (Curtis Faith, 'The Original Turtle Trading Rules'), rules summary at https://www.theturtletrader.com/turtle-trading-rules/ -- System 1 20-day entry with the skip-if-previous-breakout-was-a-winner filter, the 55-day failsafe, N as the 20-day Wilder average of true range, 2N stop, 10-day exit.

cut.name: Rolling AdaBoost Stump Margin
cut.note: AdaBoost.M1 over depth-1 decision stumps, refit on a rolling window and traded on the continuous ensemble margin rather than a class label. Fourteen scalar features (multi-horizon returns scaled by sigma_20*sqrt(h), ATR14/ATR100, ADX, RSI, log volume ratio, close location value, bar gap, distance to the 20-bar extremes in ATR, 20-bar realised skew); each stump is a (feature, quantile threshold, polarity) triple found by exhaustive search over within-feature quantile bins to minimise weighted error, with alpha = 0.5*ln((1-err)/err). Labels are triple-barrier signs at +/- barr*sigma_20 with a vert-bar cap, and the vertical (flat) outcomes are dropped. Training samples stop vert bars short of the refit bar so every label was fully observable when the model was fit. Margin M lies in [-1,1]; enter above margin_in, exit when M crosses back through zero or on the vertical barrier. The training window and refit interval are smaller than the published 1000/21 purely so the family is affordable across hundreds of thousands of backtests; the refit interval is on the grid.
cut.source: Freund & Schapire (1997), 'A Decision-Theoretic Generalization of On-Line Learning and an Application to Boosting', Journal of Computer and System Sciences 55(1). Finance instantiation on technical-indicator features, deliberately simplified to depth-1 stumps so it runs in plain Python without sklearn: Zhang et al., Applied Soft Computing 84 (2019), 'Cascading logistic regression onto gradient boosted decision trees for forecasting and trading stock indices'. Labels via Lopez de Prado (2018) Ch. 3.

cut.name: Conservative Formula Vol Screen
cut.note: Blitz and van Vliet's sequential construction: screen on volatility FIRST, rank on momentum SECOND, never a composite score. The published rule is cross-sectional (keep the calmest half of a 500-name universe, then buy the top decile of that half by 12-month return); a single-symbol harness has no cross-section, so each name is ranked against its OWN trailing distribution instead - the volatility percentile must sit below screen_pct and only then must the momentum percentile sit in the top sel_pct. The net-payout-yield leg of the published formula is a fundamental field this bot does not have and is dropped, exactly as the idea specifies. The selection is re-evaluated only every rebal bars (the monthly rebalance) and held in between, and the position is a CONDITION TO BE IN, so exit_on_zero is set.
cut.source: backtrader blog, 'Rebalancing - Conservative Formula', implementing Blitz and van Vliet, 'The Conservative Formula: Quantitative Investing Made Easy' (SSRN 3145152) - https://www.backtrader.com/blog/2019-07-19-rebalancing-conservative/rebalancing-conservative/

cut.name: Implementation Shortfall Abort
cut.note: Perold's decomposition used as an entry rule rather than an accounting one. At the decision bar the close is recorded as P0 and the expected edge as k_edge*ATR/P0; the order is then worked over n_slice bars, each slice filling at that bar's (H+L+C)/3, and the running shortfall of the fills against P0 is tracked. Three branches: shortfall above phi_abort*edge cancels the remainder and the trade never happens; a favourable shortfall accelerates and takes the position immediately; otherwise the schedule completes and the position is taken on the last slice. The shared harness fills atomically, so 'cancel the remainder' becomes 'do not participate' and the partial-fill sizing of the published rule is not expressible here - that substitution is deliberate and is the one thing lost.
cut.source: Perold, A.F. (1988), 'The Implementation Shortfall: Paper versus Reality', Journal of Portfolio Management 14(3), 4-9. Complemented by Almgren & Chriss (2000), which uses expected shortfall and its variance as the objective throughout.

cut.name: Net-Edge Admission Gate
cut.note: Gates a signal on cost rather than on strength. When the base rule fires (close crossing its EMA) three quantities are formed: the AGK EDGE effective-spread estimate over the trailing est_win OHLC bars as a fraction of price, with the Roll half-spread doubled as the fallback when EDGE is undefined; a square-root impact term y_imp*sigma_20*sqrt(Q/V20); and the conditional expected edge, the median forward h_bars log return over every past bar in the trailing edge_look window on which this same signal fired in this same direction, counting only fires at least h_bars old so the outcome was already observable. The trade is admitted only if the expected edge clears hurdle times the round trip, so the identical signal is accepted on a liquid name and refused on an illiquid one at the same dollar size. Cost enters the entry condition, not the P&L accounting.
cut.source: Ardia, D., Guidotti, E., Kroencke, T.A. (2024), 'Efficient Estimation of Bid-Ask Spreads from Open, High, Low, and Close Prices', Journal of Financial Economics 161:103916 (reference implementation at github.com/eguidotti/bidask); Roll (1984) as restated in Novy-Marx & Velikov, 'A Taxonomy of Anomalies and their Trading Costs' (NBER w20721), p.4; Toth et al. (2011) square-root law for the impact term.

cut.name: Anniversary Volume Concentration
cut.note: Frazzini-Lamont's expected-announcer trade rebuilt from volume alone. Two things in the paper are unavailable here and are replaced rather than faked, and both replacements are the point of the family: the calendar MONTH becomes one trading session (a single-symbol intraday backtest has no 24 months of daily history), and the CROSS-SECTIONAL tercile on volume concentration becomes a self-normalising per-symbol ratio. A session is FLAGGED when it contains a bar trading vspike x the normal volume for that time of day and moving rsig sigma -- the paper's 'a month containing a session with a volume and a return spike', one level down, measured slot-relative because a plain trailing median just rediscovers the diurnal volume smile and flags every session. A session is an EXPECTED ANNOUNCER if the session `anniv` back was flagged, which is the paper's 93%-accurate last-year's-announcement-month predictor. Concentration is the share of the trailing vcr_win sessions' volume falling in flagged sessions, lagged one session, divided by the flagged sessions' share of the COUNT: 1.0 means volume is spread evenly and above 1.0 means it clusters in the events. Long an expected announcer whose volume concentrates, short a non-announcer whose volume does not, as a rolling book that re-forms at every session boundary.
cut.source: Frazzini & Lamont, 'The Earnings Announcement Premium and Trading Volume', NBER Working Paper 13090 (May 2007) - PDF fetched and read directly this session. Verified specifics: long expected-announcers / short expected-non-announcers earns 61bp per month, t > 5, annual Sharpe 0.94 (higher than value, size, momentum or the market over the same period); 7-18% per year across specifications; announcement months predicted from last year's announcement month gives 93% accuracy for firms with 4 announcements in the prior year; the sorting variable is the volume concentration ratio (percent of total share volume over the previous four years occurring in announcement months), lagged 3 months; day-0 volume is more than 50% above normal, which is what makes the volume-spike proxy viable; effect present continuously since 1926.

cut.name: Bai-Perron Last-Segment Allocator
cut.note: Bai-Perron multiple mean shifts, fitted by dynamic programming to the trailing return series with a minimum segment length and at most m breaks, the number of breaks chosen by BIC or LWZ. Everything before the LAST estimated break is thrown away and the annualised Sharpe of only the post-break segment sets the weight w = clip(|SR|/sr_norm, 0, 1); a rolling window blends across breaks by construction, and this one refuses to. The harness cannot vary position size, so w acts as a GATE (trade only while w >= w_min) rather than a multiplier, and the base strategy being allocated to is the symbol itself -- long while the current regime's Sharpe is positive, short while it is negative. The daily half of the rule is kept: a fresh break inside the last `fresh` bars whose post-break mean is negative flattens and blocks new entries until the next rebalance. Break dates are searched on a grid of bstep bars to keep the DP affordable per bar.
cut.source: Bai, J. & Perron, P. (1998) Econometrica 66:47-78 and (2003) Journal of Applied Econometrics 18:1-22, sequential sup-F(l+1|l) testing for multiple unknown breaks; empirical motivation from Alexander, N. & Fabozzi, F.J., 'Measuring Strategy-Decay Risk: Minimum Regime Performance and the Durability of Systematic Investing', arXiv:2604.08356, Exhibit 3 (per-factor split dates and left/right Sharpe ratios).

cut.name: Ehlers Autocorrelation Reversal
cut.note: Ehlers' roofing filter (48-bar high pass into a 10-bar super smoother), then the Pearson autocorrelation of the filtered series against itself at every lag from lag_min to lag_max. A reversal is not one lag turning over, it is MANY turning over at once: the count of lags whose correlation crossed zero since the previous bar, against a threshold expressed as a fraction of the lags examined. Ehlers' own SumDeltas > 24 of 46 is 0.52 and is simply unreachable on this series -- the flip fraction on 5-minute bars tops out near 0.29 -- so the threshold is expressed as a fraction and the sweep is centred on the upper tail that actually occurs. The detector has no direction of its own -- the side is read off the filter's slope on the reversal bar. The position is held until the next reversal fires, whichever way it points, so the holding period is set by the market's cycle structure and not by a target. Each lag's correlation is evaluated from prefix sums, which is what keeps 46 lags per bar affordable.
cut.source: John F. Ehlers, 'Cycle Analytics for Traders' (Wiley, 2013), autocorrelation and autocorrelation-reversals chapters. Constants and the exact SumDeltas > 24 rule verified against the open-source MQL5 implementation at github.com/thetestspecimen/ehlers-indicators-mql5, file mq5/ehlers_autocorrelation_reversals.mq5, which I fetched and read. Roofing filter reference: Ehlers, 'Predictive Indicators for Effective Trading Strategies' (mesasoftware.com/papers).

cut.name: High Volume Churn Bar Failure
cut.note: A churn bar is effort without result: volume at or above the vol_pct percentile of the SAME time-of-day slot over the prior sessions, a range in the bottom rng_pct of the last 100, and a high or low that is the 20-bar extreme. Enormous volume at a swing extreme that goes nowhere means the aggressor was fully absorbed. The trade is not the churn bar -- churn precedes continuation too -- it is the FAILURE: the first close back through the whole churn bar within `win` bars, short if the churn bar set the high, long if it set the low. A later churn bar cancels and replaces the setup. Selects for range CONTRACTION on record volume, the exact opposite of an ATR-expansion filter.
cut.source: The 'High Volume Churn' bar type (high volume, low range) is one of the five classifications in the Better Volume indicator, documented at https://www.motivewave.com/studies/better_volume.htm and in the original description doc at https://c.mql5.com/forextsd/forum/147/better_volume_indicator__description.doc (the indicator originates from emini-watch.com). Those sources define the bar type and describe topping/bottoming sequences qualitatively; the percentile thresholds, the failure trigger and the exits are my specification.

cut.name: Novy-Marx Confluence Critical Value
cut.note: A confluence rule that has to earn the right to trade. Five candidate conditions (EMA9/30, RSI vs 50, close vs VWAP, MACD histogram, close vs SMA100) are each SIGNED in-sample to predict positive returns -- the very step that biases every 'enter when three indicators agree' rule -- and the unanimous composite is only armed when its own Newey-West t on that same in-sample window clears the critical value the construction actually implies: eq.(10) sqrt(2/pi)*sqrt(n)+sqrt(1-2/pi)*Phi^-1(1-np/(n+1)) for the equal-weighted composite (2.23 at n=2, 2.46 at n=3), sqrt(chi2inv(1-p,n)) for a signal-weighted one, and Phi^-1[(1-p/2)^(1/n^k)] when the best k of 5 candidates were selected (3.54 for 3-of-5, the same arithmetic that gives 4.05 for 3-of-10). Fitting and arming are redone every `refit` bars, which is the intraday stand-in for the paper's quarterly recompute; when t falls back under the critical value the composite disarms and the position is flattened. The inverse chi-squared is Wilson-Hilferty (7.78 vs 7.815 at n=3, p=0.05).
cut.source: Novy-Marx, R. (2015), 'Backtesting Strategies Based on Multiple Signals', NBER Working Paper 21329 - eq. (5) for the best 1-of-n critical value, eq. (7) for the signal-weighted n-of-n chi-distribution result, eqs. (9) and (10) for the equal-weighted asymptotic approximation, and Fig. 4 plus the abstract for the 'best k of n is almost as biased as best 1 of n^k' finding and the near-4 critical t for best 3-of-10. https://www.nber.org/papers/w21329 . I verified eq. (10) numerically: it returns 3.54 for n=10 and the n^k equivalence returns 4.05 for 3-of-10, matching the paper's 'almost four'.

cut.name: Accumulative Swing Index Lead
cut.note: Wilder's Swing Index scores the QUALITY of each bar from its close against its own open and against the previous bar's open and close, divided by the largest bar-to-bar gap. Buys when the cumulative quality series (ASI) makes a new N-bar high while raw price has NOT taken out its N-bar high - buyers winning the bars without yet winning the level - and mirrors for shorts. The price leg is the published one (close vs the prior N-bar highest high), so it removes only the already-confirmed breakouts; the family therefore fires often and lives or dies on the ASI leg.
cut.source: TradingView open-source: 'Accumulative Swing Index' by everget (original: J. Welles Wilder, 'New Concepts in Technical Trading Systems'). Exact Pine read from github.com/everget/tradingview-pinescript-indicators/blob/master/oscillators/accumulative_swing_index.pine . The ASI-leads-price entry condition is my specification of Wilder's ASI-breakout concept.

cut.name: Amihud Illiquidity Spike Reversal
cut.note: ILLIQ = |r| / dollar volume. A one-bar spike into the 95th percentile of 250 bars is a move that happened on almost no money, so it is a liquidity air pocket rather than information - fade it. The regime filter is the load-bearing part: the 20-bar MEDIAN of ILLIQ must NOT itself be in the top quartile, otherwise the name is simply thin and the reversal premium is eaten by the cost of trading it.
cut.source: Amihud (2002), 'Illiquidity and stock returns: cross-section and time-series effects', Journal of Financial Markets 5(1); Nagel (2012), 'Evaporating Liquidity', Review of Financial Studies 25(7) / NBER WP 17653 (nber.org/system/files/working_papers/w17653/w17653.pdf), which shows reversal-strategy returns are compensation for liquidity provision and are strongly time-varying.

cut.name: Deferred Jump Hedge
cut.note: Baltussen et al. find intraday jumps predict returns but that the hedge lands at the close, because partial hedging under fixed costs defers the residual to where depth is. Detects a jump (|5-min log return| >= k x the trailing 20-session median absolute return) between 10:00 and 14:30 ET, cancels the day if a later jump reverses sign, then opens IN THE JUMP'S DIRECTION at 15:30 ET and exits on the close. Signal and entry are deliberately decoupled by hours.
cut.source: Baltussen, Da, Lammers & Martens (2021), JFE 142(1), 377-403 - 'we do find evidence that large price jumps during the day predict subsequent returns... the bulk of the hedge seems to take place towards the end of the day', citing Clewlow & Hodges (1997) on partial hedging under fixed costs.

cut.name: Take-Profit Cluster Rejection
cut.note: Osler's dealing-bank order book shows take-profit limit orders cluster hard on round numbers, so price reverses when it walks into one. Fades a poke through the nearest UNTESTED round-number grid level (tier-sized: 0.10 / 0.50 / 1.00) that closes back on the wrong side of it and in the far 40% of its own bar range. Target is the next grid level, and everything is flat before the bell.
cut.source: C. L. Osler, 'Stop-Loss Orders and Price Cascades in Currency Markets', FRBNY Staff Report (June 2002), https://www.newyorkfed.org/medialibrary/media/research/staff_reports/sr150.pdf - VERIFIED by reading the PDF. Section III provides 'evidence that rates reverse course relatively frequently when they reach take-profit clusters'; p.7 reports that of 9,655 orders, 'Almost 10 percent of all such orders are placed at rates ending in 00' and 'executed take-profit orders have a stronger tendency to cluster at rates ending in 00 than executed stop-loss orders'. Companion: Osler (2003), 'Currency Orders and Exchange Rate Dynamics', Journal of Finance 58(5).

cut.name: Volume-Clock Duration Collapse
cut.note: Re-bars the tape in volume time: accumulate bars until ADV(20 sessions)/N shares have traded, pro-rating the boundary bar, and record how many clock minutes that took. Easley-O'Hara make the duration itself informative - a fixed quantity absorbed unusually fast is an information event. Enters with the direction of a volume bar whose duration is in the bottom decile of the last 200, and exits when durations normalise.
cut.source: Easley & O'Hara (1992), 'Time and the Process of Security Price Adjustment', Journal of Finance 47(2); Easley, Lopez de Prado & O'Hara (2012), 'The Volume Clock: Insights into the High-Frequency Paradigm', Journal of Portfolio Management 39(1) (researchgate.net/publication/254199259).

cut.name: Extreme-Bar Two-Day Reversal
cut.note: A one-window move of several of the symbol's OWN sigmas that also clears an absolute floor and closes at the extreme of its own range, faded for a fixed clock and nothing else - no profit target, so the test measures the documented short-horizon reversal drift alone. The paper's unit is a daily bar; here the unit is `win_min` minutes (390 = one regular session) converted to bars from the timestamps, so the rule means the same thing on 1, 5 and 15 minute data. The 5% absolute floor is a daily number and is scaled with the window and swept. The liquidity floor on average window dollar volume is kept because the academic reversal is largely an artefact of spread in thin names.
cut.source: Bremer, M. and Sweeney, R. J. (1991), 'The Reversal of Large Stock-Price Decreases', Journal of Finance 46(2) - stocks falling 10%+ in a day rebound roughly 2.2% over the following two days. Cox, D. R. and Peterson, D. R. (1994), 'Stock Returns following Large One-Day Declines', Journal of Finance 49(1) - reversal concentrated in low-price/illiquid names, hence the liquidity filter. Atkins, A. B. and Dyl, E. A. (1990), 'Price Reversals, Bid-Ask Spreads, and Market Efficiency', JFQA 25, 535-547 - reversal largely inside the spread. Zawadowski, Kertesz and Andor, 'Short-term market reaction after extreme price changes of liquid stocks' (arXiv cond-mat/0406696).

cut.name: Quantified Pin Bar at a 20-Bar Extreme
cut.note: A within-bar auction failure measured, not eyeballed: lower wick at least `wick_f` of the range, opposite wick under `opp_cap`, body under `body_cap`, range at least `atr_k` x ATR, and the bar must set the lowest low of the last `ext_n` bars. The three simultaneous ratio constraints are what exclude the dojis and spinning tops that a loose hammer definition lets through - the negative candlestick literature tests the unconditioned pattern, and this is deliberately the conditioned one. Entry emulates the buy stop above the pin high with a 2-bar order life; the stop, the 2R target, the 1R move to breakeven and the 8-bar give-up are mapped onto the shared execution grid.
cut.source: Bulkowski, T., 'Encyclopedia of Candlestick Charts', and the hammer identification guidelines at thepatternsite.com. The filters are a deliberate response to the negative literature: Marshall, B. R., Young, M. R. and Rose, L. C. (2006), 'Candlestick technical trading strategies: Can they create value for investors?', Journal of Banking & Finance 30(8), 2303-2323, find no profitability from unfiltered candlestick patterns on DJIA components 1992-2002, so only the conditioned version is worth testing.

cut.name: Residual s-score stat arb
cut.note: The Avellaneda-Lee OU s-score: cumulative residual over a rolling window, an AR(1) fit, a kappa gate that REJECTS the day when reversion is slower than `kap_win` reversion times per window (exp(-2/60) = 0.9672, the paper's number, so the gate is scale-free), and entry only on large excursions of s with deliberately asymmetric closes. Reduced honestly for a single-symbol harness: the factor leg cannot be read, so beta is 0 and the residual is the log return in excess of its own window mean - the OU machinery, the kappa rejection and the thresholds are the paper's, the market-neutral hedge is not representable.
cut.source: Avellaneda & Lee (2010), 'Statistical Arbitrage in the US Equities Market', Courant Institute NYU working paper, https://math.nyu.edu/~avellane/AvellanedaLeeStatArb20090616.pdf - equations (15), (16), (21), (22), Section 4.1 and Appendix.

cut.name: Strike Grid Pin
cut.note: Option market makers holding net long expiring contracts delta-hedge by buying below the strike and selling above it, and that rebalancing physically drags the close onto the strike. The signal is therefore not an indicator at all but a deterministic distance to a fixed price lattice reconstructed from the listing convention, gated by an expiration date and an afternoon clock, and bounded on BOTH ends - it deliberately does not fire when price is already on the strike or too far from it to be reachable. Exits are the paper's three: pin reached, the closing clock, or the distance widening against the entry. NOTE ON THE DEFAULT: `expiry_mode` defaults to 1 (every Friday expiration, weeklies included) rather than to the paper's monthly-only universe, because monthly expiration gives a single tradeable afternoon per month and a probe over a month and a half cannot tell a working rule from a broken one at that rate. Mode 0 is the paper verbatim and is in the sweep; if the effect is real it should be STRONGER in mode 0, and that comparison is itself a test of the mechanism.
cut.source: Ni, Pearson & Poteshman (2005), 'Stock Price Clustering on Option Expiration Dates', Journal of Financial Economics 78(1), 49-87 - full text at https://optionsoffice.ru/wp-content/uploads/2020/01/Stock-Price-Clustering-on-Option-Expiration-Dates.pdf. The clustering z-statistic of 8.15, the >=16.5bp return effect on expiration dates, and the deficit concentrated $0.50-$1.00 from the nearest strike on a $5 grid (i.e. 0.10G to 0.20G) are all from that paper; the effect disappears when the stocks lose listed options, which rules out generic round-number clustering.
cut.cut_reason: too few trades out of sample to score

cut.name: Abdi-Ranaldo Negative-Product Run
cut.note: Trades the SIGN of the Abdi-Ranaldo spread estimator's inner product, which every published implementation throws away by clamping at zero. pi_t = (c_t - eta_t)*(c_t - eta_{t+1}) with eta the log mid-range. Under a pure bid-ask bounce pi is positive in expectation; a run of strictly negative pi means the close is being pinned to one side of the range by directional pressure instead of bouncing, so the estimator's failure mode is itself the signal. Side comes from the sign of the mean close-minus-mid over the same run. pi_t is only known at t+1, which the code carries explicitly as a one-bar publication lag, so with the harness filling at the next open the trade lands at the open of t+2 exactly as the rule asks.
cut.source: Abdi & Ranaldo (2017), 'A Simple Estimation of Bid-Ask Spreads from Daily Close, High, and Low Prices', Review of Financial Studies 30(12):4437-4480 (SSRN 2725981). Closed form AR_t = sqrt(2*(C_t - 0.5(H_t+L_t))*(C_t - 0.5(H_{t+1}+L_{t+1}))) as reproduced in Entropy 22(7):783, 'Do Liquidity Proxies Based on Daily Prices and Quotes Really Measure Liquidity?'.

cut.name: OPEX Week Hedge Unwind
cut.note: A pure calendar rule with no price condition in the entry at all. The third Friday of each month is derived from the bar timestamps on an exact ET clock (DST included), long from the first trading day of that week to the third Friday's close, and optionally short from that close through the following Friday's close. The only non-calendar condition is the source's universe filter, a trailing median session dollar volume floor. Useful as an overlay or a gate on other rules as much as a standalone book.
cut.source: Stivers & Sun (2013), 'Returns and option activity over the option-expiration week for S&P 100 stocks', Journal of Banking & Finance 37(11), 4226-4240. Abstract and stated mechanisms retrieved from https://ideas.repec.org/a/eee/jbfina/v37y2013i11p4226-4240.html

cut.name: Percentile-Band Spread with Median Exit
cut.note: SINGLE-SYMBOL ADAPTATION of a pairs rule. The harness supplies one symbol, so the second leg is absent and the spread collapses to the leg's own formation-window z-score with mean and sd frozen at formation. What makes the idea distinct is kept intact: entry bands are EMPIRICAL quantiles of the realised formation distribution rather than sigma multiples, the exit is the formation MEDIAN rather than zero, the stop is a quantile of the same distribution, and none of the three ever touches the trading window that uses them. The first-touch rule and the end-of-window time exit are the published ones.
cut.source: Nath (2003), 'High Frequency Pairs Trading with U.S. Treasury Securities: Risks and Rewards for Hedge Funds', applied to GovPX 1994-2000; rules summarized in Krauss (2015), FAU Discussion Paper 09/2015, section 2.1 (page 8 discussion of Nath's percentile triggers, median reversion exit and stop-loss percentiles).

cut.name: Strategy-Volatility Circuit Breaker
cut.note: Barroso-Santa-Clara applied as a gate: the volatility that decides whether to trade is the SIGNAL's own, not the price's. A simulated always-on equity curve is maintained for the base rule (long while the trailing base_lb return is positive, short while negative), SV is the rolling stdev of that curve's returns, and SV is ranked against its own trailing distribution. Entries are armed only below p_enter; crossing p_flat forces flat regardless of what the base rule says and latches until the rank falls back under p_rearm. The paper's inverse-vol position SIZING is deliberately not implemented - share count belongs to the shared harness, and faking it here would make this family incomparable with every other one.
cut.source: Barroso & Santa-Clara (2015), 'Momentum has its moments', Journal of Financial Economics 116(1), 111-120. Leverage-constrained variant and replication: https://www.garp.org/hubfs/Whitepapers/a1Z1W0000054xSXUAY.pdf

cut.name: Temporary vs Permanent Impact Switch
cut.note: Hasbrouck's permanent/temporary impact split, estimated bar by bar from the symbol's own history and used to choose the SIDE of the trade rather than to filter it. An event bar is one whose log return exceeds ev_sd trailing return standard deviations; for every event whose k forward returns are already known, ti = -(sum of the k forward returns)/r_event, and TI is the median of the last `hist` of them. TI high means large moves are liquidity and revert, so fade the next event; TI low or negative means they are informational, so follow it; in between, no trade. The estimation horizon and the holding horizon are the same k by construction, so the estimate is of the exact quantity being traded. THRESHOLDS RECALIBRATED: the idea's +0.5 / -0.2 cuts are unreachable at 5-minute sampling - measured on real bars TI spans roughly -0.45 to +0.40, with XLU sitting near +0.25 (liquidity-dominated) and SOXL near -0.07 at 2sd (informational) - so the defaults are placed inside the range the estimator actually occupies and the cut is swept. The estimator itself is unchanged.
cut.source: Hasbrouck (1991), 'Measuring the Information Content of Stock Trades', Review of Financial Studies 4(1), on permanent vs transitory impact; Huang & Stoll (1996), 'Dealer versus auction markets', Journal of Financial Economics 41(3), for the effective-vs-realized-spread decomposition. The bar-level TI estimator and the sign-switching rule are my synthesis of that decomposition.

cut.name: Volatility-Scaled Symmetric CUSUM Event
cut.note: Page's symmetric CUSUM on log returns with the threshold scaled by an EWM return volatility, so the same code works across tickers and across the volatility cycle. Both accumulators reset on either event, which makes signal spacing endogenous - an identical absolute move cannot re-trigger, and whether it fires at all depends on what has accumulated since the last reset. Only the n_consec-th same-direction event with no opposite event in between is traded. Exit is Lopez de Prado's triple barrier expressed in return units (sigma*sqrt(vertical)) rather than ATR, plus an immediate exit on any opposite CUSUM event.
cut.source: Page (1954), 'Continuous Inspection Schemes', Biometrika 41(1-2). Financial form with volatility-scaled threshold and reset: Lopez de Prado, Advances in Financial Machine Learning (Wiley, 2018), section 2.5.2.1 'The CUSUM Filter'. Reference implementation: github.com/muMAJJI/Trading---CUSUM-FILTER

cut.name: CPCV Purged-Path Lower Bound
cut.note: An arming gate, not a signal generator. Every `refit` bars it takes the trailing window of the base rule's OWN completed hypothetical trades, cuts it into N contiguous groups, enumerates all C(N,2) held-out pairs, purges training bars whose H-bar label window touches a test block and embargoes the bars just after it, picks the breakout lookback on the purged training portion only, scores it on the test blocks, and recombines the splits into phi = k*C(N,k)/N complete out-of-sample paths. It trades the majority-selected lookback only while the WORST path is above min_sr and a bootstrap lower bound over the path Sharpes clears p05_sr. Sharpe here is per-trade (mean/std of trade returns), so the paper's annualised 0.5 does not carry over and the threshold is swept instead. Position sizing by SR_p05/SR_median cannot be expressed -- share count is fixed by the shared harness.
cut.source: Lopez de Prado, M. (2018), 'Advances in Financial Machine Learning', Wiley - ch.7 (purged K-fold with embargo, snippets 7.1-7.4) and ch.12 (Combinatorial Purged Cross-Validation, number of paths phi[N,k] = k*C(N,k)/N). Also Lopez de Prado, 'Backtesting II', Cornell ORIE 5256 lecture 6, https://ssrn.com/abstract=3261943

cut.name: Prior-Peak Reclaim With Volume Ramp
cut.note: All seven of DoubleTop's conditions, kept as written: a first top measured in a bounded historical window, a quantified pullback between the two peaks, a comparability band so the old peak is not a random old spike, the reclaim itself, both trend MAs, and the short-vs-long volume MA ramp. The depth/band/tolerance fractions are the one thing rescaled: 5% and 10% are daily-equity numbers and no intraday bar reaches them, so the defaults are the intraday-scale equivalents and the grid sweeps them.
cut.source: whchien/ai-trader, file ai_trader/backtesting/strategies/strategies/indicators.py class DoubleTop - the seven numbered conditions (cond_1 through cond_7) in its next() method

cut.name: Realized Skewness Session Reversal
cut.note: Third moment of intraday returns: RSkew = sqrt(n)*SUM r^3 / RV^1.5 over one whole session's bar returns, ranked against the symbol's own trailing history of session RSkew values. Bottom percentile -> long the next session, top percentile -> short, held one session. The paper's period is a week of 5-minute returns and its sort is cross-sectional; here the period is one session of whatever bars the study runs and the rank is the per-symbol time-series percentile the source itself flags as the implementable weaker form.
cut.source: Diego Amaya, Peter Christoffersen, Kris Jacobs, Aurelio Vasquez, 'Does realized skewness predict the cross-section of equity returns?', Journal of Financial Economics 118(1), 135-167, 2015 (https://ideas.repec.org/a/eee/jfinec/v118y2015i1p135-167.html) - the long-lowest-decile / short-highest-decile realized-skewness spread earned 19 bp the following week with t = 3.70. NOTE: their sort is cross-sectional; converted here to a per-symbol time-series percentile, which is a weaker but implementable form.

cut.name: Turnover-Decayed Capital Gains Overhang
cut.note: Grinblatt-Han's reference price, exactly: the weight on each past price is the probability a share bought then is still held, V_s * PROD(1-V) over everything since. That sum has a closed recursion, R_t = V_{t-1}*P_{t-1} + (1-V_{t-1})*R_{t-1}, which is what this computes -- so one heavy-volume bar really does wipe the anchor on everything before it. Turnover V uses a rolling volume-share proxy because shares outstanding is not in OHLCV. Overhang g = (C-R)/C; long on gain, short on loss, unwind when g decays back toward zero.
cut.source: Mark Grinblatt and Bing Han, 'The Disposition Effect and Momentum', NBER Working Paper 8734 (published as 'Prospect theory, mental accounting, and momentum', Journal of Financial Economics 78, 2005) - VERIFIED via https://www.nber.org/papers/w8734 (abstract) and the full PDF. Equation (15): g_t = P_t - R_t. Equation (19) gives the recursive reference price R_t = w*nu_{t-1}*F_{t-1} + (1-w*nu_{t-1})*w*nu_{t-2}*F_{t-2} + ... , the turnover-decayed weighted average this implements. Foundational: Shefrin and Statman (1985); Odean (1998).

cut.name: Ehlers Voss Predictive Filter Cross
cut.note: Ehlers' two-pole bandpass on the close, then the Voss predictor -- an IIR stage whose feedback is a linearly ramped sum of its OWN past outputs over Order = 3*Predict bars, engineered for negative group delay. Long when Voss crosses above the bandpass, short on the opposite cross, reverse on flip. Coefficients exactly as published; the filter is clamped to zero for its first bars and guarded against blow-up.
cut.source: StockSharp/AlgoTrading strategy API/1501-1600/1544_Voss_Predictor (entry on the predictive filter crossing the band-pass output); exact coefficients from mihakralj/QuanTAlib, lib/filters/voss/Voss.md, which documents the two-pole BPF recursion and the Order = 3*Predict weighted-feedback predictor from Ehlers' Aug 2019 TASC article 'A Peek Into the Future'

cut.name: Duration-hazard phase reversal
cut.note: Bull and bear phases are dated causally with a Pagan-Sossounov style rule on closes: bar t is a peak if it is the maximum of C_{t-w..t+w} and a trough if it is the minimum, judged only once bar t+w exists, with alternation enforced, a minimum phase length of dh_min bars, a minimum amplitude of dh_amp between consecutive turning points, and the usual replacement rule (a deeper trough found while still looking for a peak simply moves the trough). The empirical distribution of COMPLETED phase durations is kept separately for bull and bear phases and grows as the backtest runs, so the hazard is always estimated from what had already happened. Long when the current phase is a bear, its age exceeds the dh_in-th percentile of completed bear durations, and price has just crossed dh_conf*ATR above the phase's running minimum within the last dh_recent bars; short is the mirror. Exit when a turning point of the opposite type is dated, or when the position's own age exceeds the dh_out-th percentile of the other phase type's durations; the 2.5*ATR trailing stop is left to the shared harness. Deviation from the idea as written: the source rescaled a monthly rule to daily (21-bar window, 8% amplitude) and this study runs 5-minute bars, so the amplitude is rescaled again - 8% between consecutive turning points would date two or three phases in the whole sample and the percentile would be meaningless. dh_minph refuses to trade at all until that many completed phases of the relevant type exist, so the first stretch of every backtest is spent estimating the hazard rather than betting on it. The amplitude grid was chosen by measurement, not taste: at 2% between consecutive turning points a 45-day 5-minute sample of SPY or XLU dates too few completed phases to form a percentile and the family never trades at all, so the swept range is 0.25% to 1%; at the 0.5% default the probe symbols date 15 to 49 completed phases of each type, with median phase lengths of 40 to 93 bars.
cut.source: Pagan & Sossounov (2003), 'A Simple Framework for Analysing Bull and Bear Markets', Journal of Applied Econometrics 18(1):23-46 - the censoring rules for turning-point dating. Lunde & Timmermann (2004), 'Duration Dependence in Stock Prices: An Analysis of Bull and Bear Markets', JBES 22(3) - positive duration dependence in phase termination. Bulla & Bulla (2006), 'Stylized facts of financial time series and hidden semi-Markov models', CSDA 51.

cut.name: Hansen SPA arming gate
cut.note: A data-snooping test that decides whether the family is allowed to trade at all. Twelve candidate rules of deliberately mixed quality (four SMA crossovers, three Donchian breakouts, the three matching FADES of those breakouts, two momentum-sign rules) are run in parallel and each one's per-bar differential f_k against the benchmark (cash by default, buy-and-hold when spa_bench=1) is accumulated. Once every spa_every sessions, over the trailing spa_T bars: omega_k is a Newey-West HAC estimate of the standard deviation of sqrt(n)*f_bar_k with Bartlett weights at bandwidth floor(4*(n/100)^(2/9)); T_SPA = max(0, max_k sqrt(n) f_bar_k / omega_k); each rule is recentred at g_k = f_bar_k unless f_bar_k < -sqrt((omega_k^2/n) 2 ln ln n), in which case it is recentred at ZERO so hopeless rules cannot pad out the null; and B stationary-bootstrap index paths - one set of paths shared by every rule, drawn with geometric block lengths of mean 1/spa_q and wrap-around - give T*_i = max(0, max_k sqrt(n)(f_bar*_k - g_k)/omega_k) and p_SPA. The best rule is armed only when p_SPA < spa_alpha and disarmed (positions flattened through exit_signal) when a later test returns p_SPA >= spa_off. White's Reality Check p-value is computed from the SAME bootstrap paths and logged next to p_SPA, because the disagreement between them is the diagnostic the idea is really about: passing RC but failing SPA means the winner only wins against noise, failing RC but passing SPA means the pool was padded with junk. Deviations: the corpus is 12 rules rather than the 578-rule library, because the study's harness hands a family one symbol's bars and not the other families' returns - the multiplicity correction is therefore over this family's own pool, which is the honest scope of the test as written here; and the re-test cadence is spa_every sessions rather than calendar quarters, since a probe window is about 32 sessions long. Measured on the probe symbols, which is what makes the default thresholds defensible rather than invented: over a 32-session window the test runs about 30 times per symbol and p_SPA has a median near 0.5, so at the idea's stated 0.05 arming threshold the family arms on roughly one probe symbol in four and trades a handful of times - a real property of a multiplicity-corrected test on a short window, not a coding bug. The default is therefore set at spa_alpha 0.20 so the family has a measurable signal to study, with 0.05 and 0.10 both kept in the grid. The two p-values do diverge in the way the idea predicts: on SOXL the smallest p_SPA over the window is 0.080 against p_RC 0.145, the padded-pool case, while on SPY there are tests where p_RC comes in below p_SPA.
cut.source: Hansen, P. R. (2005), 'A Test for Superior Predictive Ability', Journal of Business & Economic Statistics 23(4), 365-380 - the studentised T^SPA statistic, the g_hat recentring rule with the -sqrt((omega^2/n) 2 log log n) threshold, and the demonstration that White's Reality Check is sensitive to the inclusion of poor alternatives. White, H. (2000), 'A Reality Check for Data Snooping', Econometrica 68(5). Politis & Romano (1994) for the stationary bootstrap.

cut.name: Variance-ratio trend gate
cut.note: Lo-MacKinlay overlapping variance ratio VR(q) with the heteroskedasticity-robust z*(q), used as an entry gate for a drift-direction trade. On a window of vr_win log returns ending at the current bar it computes sigma_a^2 (1-period), sigma_c^2 (overlapping q-period, with the m = q(nq-q+1)(1-q/nq) correction), VR = sigma_c^2/sigma_a^2, and theta*(q) = sum_j [2(q-j)/q]^2 delta_j with delta_j the ratio of sum_t d_t^2 d_{t-j}^2 to (sum_t d_t^2)^2. A position is taken only while z*(q) exceeds vr_zin, in the direction of the vr_mom-bar return; it is exited when z* falls to vr_zout (regime over) or the drift sign flips. Two honest deviations from the idea as written. First, the study's bars are 5-minute, not daily, so the 252-bar window and 63-bar direction lookback are bar counts here, not days -- the statistic is scale-free but the horizon it describes is intraday. Second, z* is recomputed every vr_step bars rather than every bar: theta* costs O(q*win) and recomputing it 6000 times per backtest dominated everything else, so the statistic is refreshed on a fixed grid and held between refreshes, which is what a daily statistic does to an intraday tape anyway. Measured on the probe symbols z*(20) runs roughly -2 to +9 with about a quarter of evaluations above +1.65, so the gate is restrictive without being unreachable.
cut.source: Lo & MacKinlay (1988), 'Stock Market Prices Do Not Follow Random Walks: Evidence from a Simple Specification Test', Review of Financial Studies 1(1), 41-66 - the VR(q) estimator and the heteroskedasticity-robust z*(q). Link from VR to trend P&L: Dao, Nguyen, Deremble, Lemperiere, Bouchaud & Potters (2017), 'Tail protection for long investors: Trend convexity at work', arXiv:1607.02410.

cut.name: Volume-clock compression breakout
cut.note: The novelty is the sampling scheme, not the trigger. The 5-minute tape is rebuilt in dollar-volume time: bucket size B = (mean dollar volume of the last vc_adv_days completed sessions) / vc_buckets, each clock bar contributes TP*V with TP = (H+L+C)/3, and a volume bar closes each time the accumulator crosses B with the overflow carried forward. On that series u_j = ln(c_j/c_{j-1}) and sigma_V is the stdev of the last vc_sig u's. Long when c_j is a new vc_look-volume-bar high AND sigma_V sits at or below its vc_pct-th percentile over the last vc_comp volume bars; short at the mirror. Exits are the volume-time time stop (vc_tstop volume bars, counted through exit_signal because the harness's time stop is in clock bars) and a flat-by-vc_flat ET rule, since bucket accumulation is discontinuous across the overnight gap and the accumulator is reset at each session boundary. Deviations from the idea as written: input bars are 5-minute rather than 1-minute, which coarsens the bucket boundaries (a bar that overfills a bucket closes several volume bars at the same price rather than being split pro rata, so a volume spike can emit up to 20 zero-return volume bars); and the 2.5*sigma_V trailing stop is left to the shared execution harness, which trails in ATR, because execution is common to every family in this study. Measured: at the defaults the clock produces roughly 90-110 volume bars per session and about a third of them pass the compression filter.
cut.source: Mandelbrot & Taylor (1967), 'On the distribution of stock price differences', Operations Research 15 - subordination of price to transaction time. Ane & Geman (2000), 'Order Flow, Transaction Clock, and Normality of Asset Returns', Journal of Finance 55(5). Easley, Lopez de Prado & O'Hara (2012), 'The Volume Clock: Insights into the High Frequency Paradigm', Journal of Portfolio Management 39(1) - the dollar-volume bucket construction.

cut.name: Volume share crowding brake
cut.note: A capacity throttle, not a directional signal. The throttled signal S is time-series momentum: score = c_t/c_{t-vs_mom} - 1, traded long when the score enters the top vs_dec decile of its own trailing vs_rank-bar distribution and short at the bottom decile. The crowding measure A is the share of the last vs_av bars' dollar volume that traded on bars S calls extreme; uniform volume would put A at 2*vs_dec, so A above that says the flow is arriving exactly where the signal is looking. z is A against its own trailing vs_z-bar mean and standard deviation. Entries are taken in full below vs_desize, at vs_frac participation between vs_desize and vs_stop, and refused above vs_stop; a name whose own 20-bar average dollar volume is more than vs_volz standard deviations above its 250-bar history is skipped outright, which is the idea's own second gate. Positions are flattened when z is above vs_stop AND S's trailing vs_pl-bar mark-to-market is negative - crowded and not working. TWO DEVIATIONS, both stated plainly. First and largest: the idea is cross-sectional (dollar volume of the extreme-decile NAMES over dollar volume of the whole universe) and this study runs one symbol at a time with no universe feed, so the aggregation axis is moved from the cross-section to time - the share of THIS name's recent volume that arrives while its own score is extreme. That keeps the economics (capital deployed against a signal has to trade, and it trades where the signal is extreme) and loses the universe-level reading of how much capital is in the trade overall. Anyone reading results from this family should read it as a volume-concentration brake, not as Hanson-Sunderam short interest. Second: fixed share size cannot express 50% of base size, so reduced size is expressed as deterministically reduced participation at rate vs_frac, the same convention used elsewhere in this study.
cut.source: Motivating result: Hanson, S.G. & Sunderam, A. (2014), 'The Growth and Limits of Arbitrage: Evidence from Short Interest', Review of Financial Studies 27(4) - short interest measures the arbitrage capital devoted to a quantitative strategy and predicts lower subsequent strategy returns. The volume-share proxy and the z thresholds are the idea author's own synthesis, and the move from cross-section to time series is mine.

cut.name: VPIN toxicity burst
cut.note: Volume-synchronised probability of informed trading, traded as a burst rather than a fade. Bars are bucketed into equal-volume buckets of V = (median session volume over the last vp_days completed sessions) / vp_buckets, with a bar that overfills a bucket split pro rata. Each bar's volume is classified by bulk volume classification, buyVol = v*Phi(dP/sigma) with sigma the rolling stdev of vp_sigma close-to-close changes, so no signed trades are needed. A completed bucket has signed imbalance S = (buy-sell)/V in [-1,1]; VPIN is the mean |S| over the last vp_n buckets. Entry is the bucket at which VPIN crosses UP through its vp_in-th percentile over the trailing vp_hist buckets, taken in the direction of that bucket's S; the exit flag is VPIN back below its vp_out-th percentile, plus a forced flat after vp_flat ET. No entries after vp_last ET. Deviations: the input bars are 5-minute rather than 1-minute, which coarsens both the BVC classification and the bucket boundaries; the 1.5*ATR adverse stop and the 60-minute cap are left to the shared execution harness (st_atr and time_stop) rather than written here; and the bucket accumulator is reset at each session boundary, since carrying a half-filled bucket across an overnight gap mixes two different information regimes.
cut.source: Easley, Lopez de Prado & O'Hara (2012), 'Flow Toxicity and Liquidity in a High-Frequency World', Review of Financial Studies 25(5), and 'An Improved Version of the Volume-Synchronized Probability of Informed Trading' - BVC buy fraction Phi(dP/sigma) and the 50-bucket rolling window.
cut.cut_reason: too few trades out of sample to score

cut.name: ACD A-level breakout with time confirmation
cut.note: Fisher's ACD. The opening range is taken over the first or_min minutes of RTH, the A levels sit a_mult * daily ATR beyond it, and an entry needs conf consecutive bars that both TRADE and CLOSE beyond the level - the dwell requirement that rejects the one-print stop run. The day is gated on the session open sitting outside the prior session's pivot range P +/- |P - (H+L)/2|, and a failed A entry is reversed at the opposite A level (the C point). The family's own exit carries the two exits the idea specifies as structural: the opposite side of the opening range, and flat by the bell. The breakeven move after A and the 3A target are left to the shared execution grid.
cut.source: Mark B. Fisher, 'The Logical Trader: Applying a Method to the Madness' (2002) - the ACD method, A and C levels as an ATR-scaled extension of the opening range with the 22% of 30-day ATR figure for the ES, and the rolling pivot range P = (H+L+C)/3 with pivot differential |P - (H+L)/2|; documented at http://www.dacharts.com/templates/descr/ACDmethod.htm and https://news.cqg.com/workspaces/2016/11/mark-fisher-indicator
cut.cut_reason: too few trades out of sample to score

cut.name: Kalman Efficient-Price Deviation
cut.note: Roll's model written as a state space: observed log price = latent efficient price (a random walk) + c times the trade direction. c2 is calibrated as the NEGATIVE first autocovariance of log returns over a trailing window and sw2 as Var(dy) - 2*c2, refreshed every reest bars; a scalar Kalman filter then tracks the efficient price and the trade is the bounce-normalised gap between the print and that latent state. Bars whose calibration window shows a POSITIVE first autocovariance are hard-vetoed - no bounce, no trade. One correction to the idea as written: the deviation is divided by sqrt(c2 * (1 - K)), the model's own standard deviation of the FILTERED residual, not by sqrt(c2). Under Roll's measurement equation y - m_true = c*q is bounded by c, so two sqrt(c2) units is unreachable by construction - measured on real 5-minute bars the raw quantity crossed |d| >= 2 on six bars in six thousand. The normalised form is what 'two noise standard deviations' denotes.
cut.source: Synthesis. The measurement equation and the two-moment calibration are the standard state-space form of Richard Roll's 1984 model (Journal of Finance, 'A simple implicit measure of the effective bid-ask spread in an efficient market'), which underlies the Roll estimator; the Kalman filtering of the efficient price and the deviation-based entry/exit are my construction. Related in spirit to Hasbrouck's Gibbs-sampler estimation of effective costs from daily data.

cut.name: Momentum Life Cycle Turnover Interaction
cut.note: Lee-Swaminathan's momentum life cycle rebuilt as a within-name two-way sort, because the harness sees one symbol at a time: MOM is the form-bar return skipping the last skip bars, RVOL_LONGRUN is mean(volume over a short window) / mean(volume over a long window), and each is ranked against its OWN trailing distribution instead of against the cross-section. Long the top-momentum / bottom-relative-volume state (early-stage winner), short the bottom-momentum / top-relative-volume state (late-stage loser), rebalance every reb bars, hold exactly hold bars. The cross-sectional tercile sort and the shares-outstanding turnover cannot be reproduced from single-symbol OHLCV; the idea itself proposes the relative-volume substitute, and the time-series percentile is the honest stand-in for the tercile.
cut.source: Lee, C.M.C. and Swaminathan, B. (2000), 'Price Momentum and Trading Volume', Journal of Finance 55(5) - https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/abs/10.1111/0022-1082.00280 ; international confirmation in 'Trading Volume and Momentum: The International Evidence'. PROXY NOTE from the idea: their turnover is volume/shares-outstanding, which we do not have; a within-name long-run relative volume ratio is substituted.

cut.name: Pattern-to-Pattern Variable Holding Period
cut.note: Enter on a white marubozu (closing or opening variant, the Goo-Chen-Chang one-day inequalities with equality tolerance eps = eps_frac * bar range) while price is above its EMA(10); hold with no target, no time stop and no ordinary stop, and exit only when the opposing black marubozu set prints. mode 0 goes flat on that signal, mode 1 reverses and stays always-in. The only price-based protection is the 4 x ATR catastrophic guard the paper specifies, carried as st_atr.
cut.source: Lu, Shiu & Liu (2012), variable-holding-period ('LSL') exit strategy - buy on a bullish signal, liquidate when a bearish pattern occurs - described and contrasted against the MYR and CL exits in Tharavanij, Siraprapasiri & Rajchamaha (2017), SAGE Open, doi:10.1177/2158244017736799. One-day pattern inequalities from Goo, Chen & Chang (2007), reproduced in the same paper.

cut.name: Poor High / Poor Low Repair
cut.note: Builds a real TPO profile from each completed RTH session - rows row_frac * daily ATR wide, every 30-minute period marking every row between its own low and high - and records a POOR extreme when the top two occupied rows each carry min_tpo periods and at least flat_n periods have their high within one row of the session high (a flat, tail-less top). Unrepaired extremes are carried for reg_depth sessions; the trade is TOWARD the level, taken when price comes within approach * ATRd of it on a bar that closes in the direction of the level, targeting repair * ATRd BEYOND it. A level leaves the register once the auction has traded through it.
cut.source: Dalton, Jones & Dalton, 'Mind Over Markets' (1993). Operational definition as documented by marketcalls.in ('Poor High and Poor Low Market Profile Structure Explained': lack of excess or a single TPO at the tail) and the ShadowTrader glossary ('a poor high will have less than two TPOs of excess with at least 2-3 columns of TPOs lining up to form a flat top').
cut.cut_reason: too few trades out of sample to score

cut.name: Rolling Half-Kelly Ledger Sizing
cut.note: The signal is a deliberately fixed harness - a 20-bar Donchian breakout, out on a 10-bar low, stop at 2 ATR - so the only thing under test is the QUANTITY rule. A rolling ledger of the last N closed trades on this symbol gives W, the average win and the average loss, hence f* = W - (1-W)/R; the share count is kelly_c * f* of equity divided by the per-share stop distance, capped at risk_cap, and a NEGATIVE f* vetoes the trade outright. ONE GAP HAD TO BE FILLED: as literally written the veto is absorbing, because f* is only recomputed when a trade closes and no trade can close once trading stops - measured on the probe it froze every symbol at exactly 30 trades and left the whole grid inert. probe_n therefore takes one floor-sized trade after that many consecutive vetoes so the ledger can refresh; the sweep includes an arm large enough to reproduce the literal absorbing rule.
cut.source: Edward O. Thorp, 'The Kelly Criterion in Blackjack, Sports Betting, and the Stock Market' (2006/2007), open PDF at https://gwern.net/doc/statistics/decision/2006-thorp.pdf - the half-Kelly growth/drawdown result is in the fractional-Kelly section.

cut.name: Campbell-Yogo Bonferroni Q Predictor Gate
cut.note: A licensing test that decides, every re-evaluation, whether a persistent predictor is allowed to drive exposure at all. The predictor under test is x = log(close / SMA(close, pw)), the log gap between price and its own long moving average: OHLCV-only, highly persistent, and with an innovation almost perfectly correlated with the return innovation -- exactly the configuration in which a naive t-test on beta is really a 15-20 percent test. Its prior sign is POSITIVE and is fixed before the data is seen: over horizons of days, time-series momentum says price above its own long average predicts continuation, and the opposite value/reversion prior belongs to multi-year horizons that no bar count here reaches. Each re-evaluation the DF-GLS statistic is computed on x and INVERTED to a confidence set for rho, then for each retained rho the paper's Q-statistic gives a confidence interval for beta, and the Bonferroni interval is the union of those. Exposure is taken only while that whole interval lies strictly above zero; the moment it admits zero the predictor is unlicensed and exposure falls back to flat, this harness's version of the prevailing-mean benchmark weight. No stop and no target, per the idea. Three implementation notes, stated plainly. (1) The DF-GLS null bands are read from a lookup table over c = T(1 - rho), simulated once offline at T = 250 with 5,000 Gaussian paths and embedded in the code at three Bonferroni splits alpha1 = 0.05 / 0.10 / 0.30 -- reading the interval for c off a table is exactly what the paper does with the Elliott-Rothenberg-Stock tables, and re-simulating 5,000 paths per rho per period would burn the study's wall clock to reproduce a constant. (2) Q is LINEAR in beta0, so the |Q| < zq retention set is solved in closed form instead of searched over a beta grid; the answer is identical and it costs nothing. (3) The test is re-run every reeval periods rather than at every period end, which is the one O(T) cost the study cannot afford at every bar; nothing else about the test changes. Timeframe map: 'daily bars aggregated to monthly, monthly re-evaluation' becomes agg bars to a period on an expanding sample, which is what the paper itself uses.
cut.source: Campbell, J.Y. and Yogo, M., 'Efficient Tests of Stock Return Predictability', NBER Working Paper 10026 (Oct 2003), published JFE 81, 2006 - read directly at https://www.nber.org/system/files/working_papers/w10026/w10026.pdf. The Q-statistic is eq. (9) on p.8; the local-to-unity framework is section 3.1; the use of DF-GLS (Elliott, Rothenberg and Stock) rather than ADF to build the confidence interval for c, and the reason for it, are on pp.523-527 of the text; the Bonferroni construction and the choice of the Q-test over the Bonferroni t-test of Cavanagh, Elliott and Stock (1995) are in section 3.3. The simulation-based inversion of the DF-GLS statistic over a rho grid is my pinning-down of a step the paper implements via published lookup tables.

cut.name: RLS Adaptive Autocorrelation Sign
cut.note: Runs textbook recursive least squares with exponential forgetting on standardised log returns, z_t = a + b z_{t-1}, updating theta and P every bar with k = Px/(mu + x'Px), theta += k(z - x'theta), P = (P - k x'P)/mu, P initialised to p_init x I. The regime variable is the tracked coefficient itself, so there is no window and no refit schedule: mu alone sets an effective memory of about 1/(1-mu) bars. The traded object is the significance ratio G = b / sqrt(s2 P[1,1]) with s2 an EWM residual variance, not the raw coefficient, which keeps the family out of the long stretches where b is noise around zero. Significantly negative G plus a large last bar fades it; significantly positive G plus a large last bar follows it; both branches mirror for shorts. Exit is the idea's own three-way: hold bars elapsed, |G| collapsing below g_out, or a stop at stop_sig x the bar's own EWM sigma, with the harness target and stop switched off.
cut.source: Synthesis. RLS with exponential forgetting is standard: Ljung, System Identification: Theory for the User (2nd ed., Prentice Hall, 1999), ch. 11 recursive estimation. The pattern of online adaptive-rate learning applied to short-horizon price prediction appears in PLOS ONE 15(6): e0234107, 'Mid-price prediction based on machine learning methods with technical and quantitative indicators' (online learning with adaptive rate for next mid-price move). The specific entry/exit construction above is mine, not taken from a paper.

cut.name: Alpha Half-Life vs Cost-Recovery Admission
cut.note: A cost-aware admission gate wrapped around a normalised-deviation forecast f = (close - SMA(win))/stdev(win). Every `retest` bars it measures the signal's persistence (AR(1) on f -> half-life HL = ln2/-ln(rho)), the cumulative conditional edge curve E(h) for h = 1..h_max on settled bars only, and the round-trip cost RT (rolling high-low spread plus 2*Y*sigma*sqrt(Q/V20) impact). T_BE is the first h where E(h) > RT; the signal may trade only while HL > ratio*T_BE, and is flattened the moment it is de-admitted. Exit at min(HL, h_max) bars or the first zero crossing of f. Spread substitution: Corwin-Schultz stands in for EDGE.
cut.source: Synthesis, built on two verified primary results: Novy-Marx & Velikov (RFS 2016, NBER w20721) turnover taxonomy and the finding that 'few of the strategies with higher turnover' survive costs; and Garleanu & Pedersen (2013) Proposition 4, 'the central relevance of signal persistence in the presence of transaction costs is one of the distinguishing features of our analysis'.

cut.name: CSCV Overfit Probability Gate with Median-Rank Parameter Choice
cut.note: Runs Bailey/Borwein/Lopez de Prado/Zhu's combinatorially symmetric cross-validation over the family's OWN parameter grid (eight trend configurations, long above SMA(L), short below), enumerating every split of the trailing window into S/2 training blocks and their complement. PBO is the share of splits where the in-sample-best column lands below the out-of-sample median; the family trades only while PBO < pbo_max and the median OOS Sharpe of the chosen column is positive, and the configuration deployed is the highest MEDIAN-RANK column across all test sets, never the full-sample argmax. The source's two retirement rules are swept switches (`retire` = permanent retirement above pbo_retire, `slope_gate` = retirement on a negative IS-on-OOS degradation slope) because measured on real bars each of them retires everything -- with J and J' complementary halves of one window the slope is mechanically about -1 at every re-test. Deviations: S = 8 or 12 blocks rather than 16, and enumerations larger than `cap` are thinned by a fixed stride so the result stays deterministic. `slope_gate` stays a parameter rather than a swept one: on every re-test on all four probe symbols the slope came out near -1, so switching it on retires the family immediately and the sweep would spend half its budget on a known off switch.
cut.source: Bailey, D., Borwein, J., Lopez de Prado, M. & Zhu, Q. (2017), 'The Probability of Backtest Overfitting', Journal of Computational Finance 20(4), 39-69 - Algorithm 2.3 (CSCV), Definition 2.2 (PBO), and Section 3 (performance degradation, probability of loss, stochastic dominance). Working paper PDF: https://www.davidhbailey.com/dhbpapers/backtest-prob.pdf

cut.name: Fitted Trend Factor
cut.note: Eight normalised moving averages A_L = SMA_L/close are used as REGRESSORS in a fitted forward-return forecast rather than as signals. The slopes are re-estimated on a sliding window every `refit` bars, smoothed with the paper's EWMA (lam), and the forecast ER = sum_L b_L*A_L is cut at its own trailing q / 1-q quantiles; the position holds until the next rebalance re-ranks it, and the forecast is the only exit. The published regression is cross-sectional across a universe -- this harness sees one symbol, so the fit is in the time series and the tercile is against ER's own history; what is preserved is that the weight and SIGN on each horizon is estimated and time-varying rather than hard-coded.
cut.source: Han, Zhou & Zhu, 'A trend factor: Any economic gains from using information over investment horizons?', Journal of Financial Economics 122(2), 2016, 352-375. Construction reproduced verbatim in Liu & Zhou, 'Trend Factor in China', equations (1)-(2) (MA of the last L closes, normalised by the closing price on the last trading day), (5) (cross-sectional forecasting regression) and (7) (EWMA coefficient forecast, lambda = 0.02, giving a roughly 4-year effective memory). PDF: https://wrds-www.wharton.upenn.edu/documents/1119/WARSP_TrendChina.pdf

cut.name: Half-N Pyramid with Shared Ratcheting Stop
cut.note: Turtle Donchian breakout entry, then the Turtle pyramid's STOP SCHEDULE: a virtual unit is booked every add_n*N beyond the last unit's level (N = ATR at the original entry, frozen), up to max_units, and one shared stop is dragged to (newest unit - stop_n*N), ratcheting only in the favourable direction and freezing once the stack is full. Exit on that stop or on a close through the exit_n channel. The signal contract permits one entry per trade, so the added units are virtual -- the convex position sizing is NOT tested, only the stop geometry it implies.
cut.source: Original Turtle Trading Rules, 'Adding Units' (adds at 1/2 N intervals from the previous unit's fill, max 4 units per market) and 'Stops for Added Units' (all units share one stop, moved up as units are added). Public PDF: https://oxfordstrat.com/coasdfASD32/uploads/2016/01/turtle-rules.pdf

cut.name: Quarterly Reaction Sign Ladder
cut.note: Detects earnings-like events from OHLCV (a k-sigma return on vmult-times-average volume, with a refractory period), scores each by its reaction return EAR, extrapolates the next event from the median spacing of the last three intervals, and takes a position `lead` bars before it in the direction of S = sign(EAR1)+sign(EAR2)+sign(EAR3)+w4*sign(EAR4). w4 = -1 is Bernard & Thomas's lag-4 sign flip; w4 = +1 is the control. Exits `post` bars after the event actually fires, or `abandon` bars after the anticipated date if it never does. Scale note: the literal 50-80 session band needs ~250 daily sessions that an intraday window does not contain, so spacing is tested for REGULARITY (sp_min, sp_tol) instead; on daily bars set sp_min=50, sp_tol=1.6.
cut.source: Bernard and Thomas (1989, 1990). The naive-expectations mechanism - investors fail 'to recognize fully the implications of current earnings for future earnings' - and the seasonal random walk model were VERIFIED via https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Post-earnings-announcement_drift and the Quantpedia PEAD page (which specifies SUE 'calculated using a seasonal random walk model with drift'). The specific lags-1-to-3-positive, lag-4-negative sign pattern is from Bernard and Thomas (1990), 'Evidence that stock prices do not fully reflect the implications of current earnings for future earnings', Journal of Accounting and Economics 13 - I did NOT open that paper in this session; that lag detail is from background knowledge. The S-score ladder and the pre-positioning construction are my own.
