cut.name: Volume Run-Bar Polarity Flip
cut.note: Builds Lopez de Prado volume run bars whose boundaries are endogenous -- a bar closes when one side's cumulative volume exceeds E[T]*max(P_b*E[V_b],(1-P_b)*E[V_s]), all three terms EWMAs of the recent run-bar history -- and signs the flow by bulk volume classification, V_b = V*Phi(dP/sigma_dP). Enters when the polarity of the sampling process itself flips: `confirm` buy-side run bars immediately after `opp` or more consecutive sell-side ones. Exits on the first opposite-polarity run bar or after `hold` run bars.
cut.source: Marcos Lopez de Prado, 'Advances in Financial Machine Learning' (Wiley, 2018), Ch. 2, section 2.3.2.2 'Run Bars' -- the threshold condition max(theta_buy, theta_sell) >= E[T] * max(P_b*E[V_b], (1-P_b)*E[V_s]) is his. Signing via bulk volume classification is the OHLCV proxy for his tick rule, from Easley, Lopez de Prado & O'Hara (2012). The polarity-flip entry is my synthesis.

cut.name: 52-Week-High Recency Gate
cut.note: Nearness to the running 252-bar extreme AND the age of that extreme: long only when the high was set within the last 21 bars and NEAR sits in the top 30% of its own trailing distribution, short on the mirror. The position is closed when the anchor goes stale (older than `stale` bars) rather than on any price event. Cross-sectional ranking replaced by the symbol's own trailing percentile, since a family sees one symbol.
cut.source: Bhootra & Hur, 'The timing of 52-week high price and momentum', Journal of Banking & Finance, 2013 - defines a 'recency ratio' from the number of days since the 52-week high was formed and shows the anchoring effect is far stronger for recent highs.

cut.name: Cumulative Delta Extreme Break
cut.note: Close-location-weighted signed volume accumulated from the cash open; the trade is a new extreme of that ACCUMULATOR against its own trailing 20 bars, not of price -- price can be flat while the accumulator breaks out, and that divergence is the signal. Out on the accumulator crossing back through zero, a percent stop, or the bell.
cut.source: StockSharp/AlgoTrading, strategy API/0001-0100/0054_Cumulative_Delta_Breakout -- 'Cumulative Delta sums the difference between buy and sell volume... trades when it breaks above its highest value or below its lowest value within the lookback period; exit when delta crosses back through zero'. The repo's own PY file uses a coarse sign(Close-Open)*Volume proxy; the close-location-value weighting used here is the standard OHLCV refinement.

cut.name: Effort Result Regression Residual
cut.note: Fits |log return| on log volume over a rolling window and trades the bars whose residual is far NEGATIVE -- enormous volume that produced almost no price change, i.e. someone absorbed the flow at a fixed price. Gated on the bar also being in the top of its own volume distribution and at least median width; the absorber's side is read off where the bar closed in its range.
cut.source: Synthesis, built on two cited pillars: Amihud (2002), 'Illiquidity and stock returns: cross-section and time-series effects', Journal of Financial Markets 5, 31-56, https://www.cis.upenn.edu/~mkearns/finread/amihud.pdf , which establishes |return|/dollar-volume as the price response per unit of trading; and Wyckoff's effort-vs-result law as described at https://www.luxalgo.com/library/concept/effort-vs-result/ . The OLS-residual formulation and the clv direction rule are my own.

cut.name: Even Better Sinewave Saturation Exit
cut.note: Ehlers' Even Better Sinewave (40-bar high-pass, 10-bar SuperSmoother, 3-bar wave/RMS normalisation) traded on its SATURATION rather than its level: enter when the bounded wave un-pins from one rail, hold through the entire pinned stretch at the opposite rail, and exit only when it un-pins from THAT one. The normalisation is amplitude-free, so the rail needs no per-symbol tuning. The shared execution grid still applies an ATR target on top, so the wide-target variants are the ones that actually test the hold-through-saturation claim.
cut.source: John F. Ehlers, 'Cycle Analytics for Traders' (Wiley, 2013), 'Even Better Sinewave Indicator' chapter. Formula, the hpPeriod = 40 / lpPeriod = 10 defaults, the 3-bar wave/pwr normalisation and the +/-1.2 plot bounds verified against github.com/thetestspecimen/ehlers-indicators-mql5, file mq5/ehlers_even_better_sinewave.mq5, which I fetched and read. The saturate-and-hold exit structure is my synthesis of Ehlers' stated intent.

cut.name: Ross Hook After a Closing-Channel Breakout
cut.note: A fresh 20-bar CLOSING high, then the FIRST bar that fails to extend it (the Ross hook), then a stop order at the running high of that leg, live for ten bars and cancelled if anything closes back under the breakout bar's low. The reference level is generated by the impulse itself rather than by an average, so the trigger tracks the leg instead of lagging it.
cut.source: Joe Ross, 'Trading by the Book' (Ross Hook and the Traders Trick Entry). Coded rules, Min_Setup/Max_Hook parameters, buy stop one tick above the highest high of the hook, quick exit at the opposite hook extreme, and rating C across 42 futures markets 1980-2011: https://oxfordstrat.com/trading-strategies/ross-hook-1/ (filter variants at ross-hook-filter-1/2/3). Ross's original 1-2-3 precondition is judgement-dependent, so it is pinned here to a 20-bar CLOSING-channel breakout, which is testable.

cut.name: Body-Dominant Engulfing with Close-Strength Exit
cut.note: An engulfing bar that has to earn the name three ways at once: its body engulfs the prior body (open inside the prior close, close beyond the prior open), that body is body_ratio times the prior body, and the body is at least body_frac of its own range while the range itself is at least rng_atr of ATR(14). The context gate asks that weak_k of the previous weak_n bars closed below their own prior close, so the bar arrives after real one-sided pressure rather than at random. Reversal is NOT assumed -- Bulkowski's outside-day data has these continuing 63% of the time -- so the trade is simply taken in the direction of the engulfing body. The exit is the real idea: a close-strength stop that liquidates on the first decisive close-against-the-position wide bar, CLV = ((close-low)-(high-close))/(high-low) <= clv_exit with the range at least clv_rng_atr of ATR -- bar geometry, not a price level and not an indicator. The engulfing bar's own low (minus low_pad) is also honoured as a stop inside exit_signal; the 3-ATR target is left to the shared execution grid, which sweeps 1 to 4.
cut.source: Bulkowski, T., thepatternsite.com/OutsideDays.html -- an engulfing bar is an outside day with body constraints, and Bulkowski's data show outside days act as a CONTINUATION 63% of the time in bull markets with up breakouts (average rise 10%, 32% break-even failure rate, rank 6 of 23 small patterns), which is why this rule does not assume reversal. Null-result context: Marshall, Young and Rose (2006), Journal of Banking & Finance 30(8), 2303-2323.

cut.name: Liquidity Vacuum Depth Collapse
cut.note: Depth proxy D = close*volume / max(range/close, 1e-6) -- dollar volume per unit of relative range, an Amivest / inverse-Kyle-lambda. The trigger is a z-score of ln D against its own trailing window reaching the low tail on `cons` consecutive bars; price plays no part in it. Direction comes from the sum of the BVC (bulk volume classification) signed imbalance over those same bars: volume times 2*Phi(dP/sigma_dP)-1. Two deliberate choices. The depth series is built on REGULAR HOURS bars only, because on 5-minute data that includes extended hours the raw z-score is a measure of the diurnal volume cycle -- all 203 two-bar collapses on SPY in the probe window landed outside 09:30-16:00, i.e. the rule as literally stated fires only overnight and tests nothing about the book. And the default threshold is -1.5 rather than -2.0 (both are in the idea's own list): on RTH bars, -2.0 yields 2-5 events per symbol per 33 sessions, too few to clear the study's per-symbol trade minimum.
cut.source: Amivest liquidity ratio as introduced in Cooper, Groth & Avera (1985), Journal of Economics and Business 37(1); Kyle (1985) for depth as 1/lambda; the family of volume-to-range and volume-to-return liquidity proxies is surveyed in Fong, Holden & Trzcinka, 'What Are the Best Liquidity Proxies for Global Research?' (cicfconf.org/sites/default/files/paper_337.pdf). The two-bar depth-collapse entry is my synthesis.

cut.name: Range-Bar Flip Count Regime
cut.note: Range bars of fixed height S = s_atr * ATR(atr_n), S recomputed at the first regular-hours bar of each session and then frozen for that session. A range bar opens at the previous one's close and closes as soon as its running high minus running low reaches S; because only OHLC is available and not the path inside a bar, the extreme reached LAST is taken to be the high when that bar closed up and the low when it closed down. F is the number of direction flips among the last flip_win closed range bars -- a unit-free path-efficiency measure, since the price distance per bar is constant by construction, which is exactly what ADX and the choppiness index cannot claim on time bars. Enter with the tape when F <= in_flip and the last run_len range bars all closed the same way; exit on the same statistic at a looser threshold (F >= out_flip), on opp_run range bars against the position, or after rb_max range bars. The 2*S hard stop is 2*s_atr in ATR units, left to the shared execution grid whose stops bracket it. One approximation is worth naming: a single 5-minute bar wide enough to complete more than one range bar closes only one, because the path inside that bar is unknown and inventing the rest would be inventing data.
cut.source: Range-bar construction is standard in futures platform documentation (constant-range bars); the flip-count statistic and the entry/exit thresholds are my synthesis. The path-efficiency reasoning follows Kaufman's efficiency ratio (Perry Kaufman, 'Trading Systems and Methods', Wiley) applied in range-bar space rather than time space.

cut.name: RSRS High-on-Low Regression Beta
cut.note: An ordinary least squares fit of the bar HIGH on the bar LOW over the last reg_n bars -- the two series regressed against each other rather than against time or against price. Beta is how far the ceiling extends per unit the floor extends: large means buyers are winning the range, small means the high is capped while the low keeps sliding. Raw beta drifts with the instrument, so it is standardised against its own trailing z_n distribution, and z is multiplied by the regression R-squared (use_r2) so a reading taken from a noisy high/low relationship is discounted rather than trusted. Long on a cross up through s_in, short on a cross down through -s_in, out through s_out. Computed with offset prefix sums so the 18-bar cross-products stay numerically clean on a $700 index.
cut.source: whchien/ai-trader, file ai_trader/backtesting/strategies/strategies/indicators.py, classes RSRS and NormRSRS (OLS of high on low, z-score over a long window, R2-weighted variant), used by ai_trader/backtesting/strategies/classic/rsrs.py

cut.name: Sign-Autocorrelation z Score
cut.note: Estimates whether the SIGN of a bar return persists at lag m, and trades only when that persistence is statistically significant. p_m is the continuation frequency over the last N valid sign pairs (bars with a zero return are dropped from the pairing rather than counted as up), and z_m = (2*p_m - 1)*sqrt(N) against the random-walk null of 0.5. z <= -threshold takes the OPPOSITE side to the last bar's sign, z >= +threshold takes the SAME side, and nothing is taken in between. Magnitude is deliberately absent from the statistic and appears only as an entry filter, |r_t| >= r_min * stdev(r, r_win). The hold is exactly m bars, implemented in exit_signal from the position's own entry bar so that sweeping the lag sweeps the hold with it, which a fixed time_stop could not do.
cut.source: arXiv 2606.29591, 'The Bounce Has No Direction' -- the FRI sign test, rho_sign(m) = 2*p_{m,0} - 1 with p_{m,0} the continuation frequency and 0.5 the random-walk null; the paper reports z_sign = -1.59 at lag 1 (insignificant) alongside rho(1) = -0.081 with z* = -7.39, and z_sign = -2.32 at lag 3 where rho(3) is insignificant.

cut.name: Vol-of-Vol Collapse
cut.note: Second-order volatility. RV = stdev of the last rv_n log returns; VoV = stdev of ln(RV) over the last vov_n bars; P = the percentile of VoV in its own trailing hist_n distribution. Entry is on the RESOLUTION, not the spike: P crosses down through in_pct having been at or above hot_pct within the previous hot_look bars. Exit when P climbs back above out_pct, or on the shared time stop. The sign is a swept parameter (dirn) because the option-implied version of this effect predicts LOW returns while the mechanical-deleveraging story predicts high ones, and a realized-data proxy cannot settle that a priori. DEVIATION: the unit is the BAR, not the session. The study runs 5- and 15-minute bars over 120 days, in which a 504-SESSION percentile history cannot exist at all, so the 5/20/504 structure is applied to the native bar series -- the statistic is unchanged, its sampling rate is not.
cut.source: Synthesis -- a realized-data analogue of the option-implied vol-of-vol effect documented in Baltussen, van Bekkum & van der Grient (2018), 'Unknown Unknowns: Uncertainty About Risk and Stock Returns', Journal of Financial and Quantitative Analysis 53(4). Since no option chain is available, the proxy replaces implied vol-of-vol with the standard deviation of log realized vol; the proxy is noisier and its sign is an empirical question, hence the two-sided parameter sweep.

cut.name: Elder Triple Screen Ratchet
cut.note: Elder's three screens with the screen-3 detail that is usually dropped: the entry is a resting stop one tick beyond the PREVIOUS bar's extreme, re-priced every bar, so while the pullback continues the buy stop walks DOWN with it and only fills at the turn. Tide is the MACD histogram slope on bars resampled to a higher timeframe; the wave is a short EMA of Force Index that must oppose the tide.
cut.source: Alexander Elder, 'Trading for a Living' (1993) and 'Come Into My Trading Room' (2002) -- the Triple Screen system. Screen-3 trailing buy-stop rule ('place the buy order one tick above the previous day high... the order also moves down, one point above the high, until a buy opens or the main trend reverses') as documented at mql5.com/en/blogs/post/731016 and asktraders.com's Elder triple screen guide.

cut.name: Jump-Penalised Regime Path
cut.note: A K=2 statistical jump model on nine EWM features of the return series (mean, downside deviation and standard deviation at three half-lives, standardised on a trailing window). The state path minimises squared distance to its centroid plus a fixed L0 cost lambda for every state change, solved exactly by dynamic programming and alternated with centroid re-estimation; long while the fitted state is the bull centroid, flat while it is the bear one, with no price stop.
cut.source: Bemporad, Breschi, Piga & Boyd, 'Fitting jump models', Automatica 96 (2018) - the DP plus centroid alternation. Financial instantiation and the risk/return feature set: arXiv:2402.05272, 'Downside Risk Reduction Using Regime-Switching Signals: A Statistical Jump Model Approach'. Deviations from the source recipe, both for cost: two deterministic opposed initialisations replace k-means++ with ten restarts, and the model is refit every refit bars with online state assignment under the same penalty in between rather than refit on every bar.

cut.name: No Supply No Demand Bar
cut.note: Volume Spread Analysis read of an ABSENCE of participation: a narrow-range bar whose volume undercuts each of the previous two bars, closing in the half of its range that contradicts its own direction, taken only in the matching side of the SMA. Mandatory confirmation on the very next bar (close through the signal bar's extreme on higher volume) turns the qualitative read into a rule.
cut.source: Tom Williams, 'Master the Markets' (Volume Spread Analysis). Operational definition -- up/down bar, narrow spread, volume lower than the previous two bars, close position within the bar, confirming next bar on rising volume -- from tradingsetupsreview.com's VSA guide and atas.net's no-demand/no-supply article. 'Narrow spread' is undefined in both sources and is pinned here to a fraction of the mean range of the five bars before the signal bar.

cut.name: Pastor-Stambaugh Gamma Reversal
cut.note: Estimates the Pastor-Stambaugh liquidity coefficient per symbol -- the OLS loading of NEXT bar's return on this bar's signed standardised dollar volume, over a rolling window -- and fades a heavy-volume move only when that symbol's own gamma sits in the most-negative tail of its trailing history. Gamma is the only one of the standard liquidity measures that is predictive rather than contemporaneous, and its sign is the thesis rather than a filter.
cut.source: Lubos Pastor and Robert F. Stambaugh, 'Liquidity Risk and Expected Stock Returns', Journal of Political Economy 111(3), 642-685 (2003) -- the liquidity measure is the OLS gamma in a regression of next-period excess return on the current return and signed dollar volume. Their gamma is estimated monthly from daily data for an aggregate factor; the per-symbol rolling timing signal is the harvested idea's adaptation.

cut.name: Excess tail fade to POC
cut.note: Builds a 30-minute TPO profile of each completed RTH session on rows of row_atr * daily ATR and looks for EXCESS: at least min_rows consecutive single-print rows at a session extreme, spanning at least tail_frac of the session range. That is the auction-theory signature of a finished auction, as opposed to a poor high which asks to be revisited. The tail base and the same session's point of control are registered for depth sessions; when price later trades back beyond the base and a bar CLOSES back inside it, the original rejection has re-confirmed and the trade is taken against the tail, targeting that session's POC with the stop at the excess extreme plus stop_buf daily ATRs, abandoned at flat_min ET of the hold_sessions-th session after entry. A record is erased when a session closes beyond the excess extreme, and fires at most once - without that a single tail re-arms all day and the family degenerates into fading one session's high repeatedly. Execution is one native bar rather than the idea's 15 minutes, since the trigger is bar-size agnostic and the family is handed whatever the study is running.
cut.source: Dalton, Jones & Dalton, 'Mind Over Markets'; excess/tail definitions per the 'Excess + Tails in TPO profile' tear sheet (webflow-hosted, 2020) and the ShadowTrader glossary entries for excess high/excess low ('the minimum number of TPOs necessary to define an excess low is two').

cut.name: MedRV jump-fraction breakout split
cut.note: Computes the nearest-neighbour-truncation realised measures on a rolling window - RV, MedRV, bipower variation and tri-power quarticity - forms the Andersen-Bollerslev-Diebold jump statistic z and the jump fraction JF = max(0, RV-MedRV)/RV, and uses them to split a breakout in two. A new brk-bar high built out of continuous diffusive trading (z below z_lo, JF at or under jf_lo) is bought as a sustained order-flow imbalance; the same new high produced by a discrete jump (z above z_hi, JF at or over jf_hi) is SHORTED instead, because that repricing was already complete the moment it printed. The two branches carry deliberately different exits: the continuous leg runs to a brk/2 clock or a close through the brk/2 low, the jump fade to a brk/4 clock, the entry bar's own extreme, or the jump fraction cooling off. The median triple is indexed so the newest bar is its right edge, which is what makes MedRV computable without reading the next bar. The rule's day clocks are kept as exact ratios of a swept bar count (exit low and continuous hold = brk/2, jump hold = brk/4); mirror=1 additionally reflects both branches onto new brk-bar lows and mirror=0 recovers the rule exactly as written.
cut.source: Andersen, Dobrev & Schaumburg (2012), 'Jump-robust volatility estimation using nearest neighbor truncation', Journal of Econometrics 169, 75-93. MedRV/MinRV constants and tri-power quarticity exactly as implemented in the R highfrequency package (rMedRVar, rMinRVar, rTPQuar, BNSjumpTest), CRAN reference manual pp. 16-17 and 92-96: https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/highfrequency/highfrequency.pdf. Jump statistic form from Andersen, Bollerslev & Diebold (2007), 'Roughing it up', Review of Economics and Statistics 89, 701-720.

cut.name: MRR Adverse-Selection Share
cut.note: Estimates the Madhavan-Richardson-Roomans structural decomposition of every bar's price change on a rolling window: OLS of the log return on the tick-rule trade indicator at t and t-1 gives a = phi+theta and b = -(phi+rho*theta), and with rho, the first-order autocorrelation of the indicator, theta (asymmetric information) and phi (order processing / inventory) come out analytically - rho is what keeps the expected part of order flow from being counted as information. The adverse-selection share ASH = theta/(theta+phi) then routes a run of same-signed flow: FOLLOW the run in the symbol's information-rich state, FADE it in its inventory state, stand aside between. Two honest reductions, both forced by bar data: trades are signed by the tick rule on bar closes (the source note allows this), and the 0.60/0.25 cut is applied to ASH's percentile rank over its own trailing window rather than to its level, because on 5-minute bars the transitory component has averaged out inside the bar and measured ASH never leaves 0.68-1.00 - the paper's low branch is unreachable at this aggregation and would be dead code.
cut.source: Ananth Madhavan, Matthew Richardson, Mark Roomans, 'Why Do Security Prices Change? A Transaction-Level Analysis of NYSE Stocks', Review of Financial Studies 10(4), 1035-1064, 1997 (https://ideas.repec.org/a/oup/rfinst/v10y1997i4p1035-64.html) - the structural model of intraday price formation whose estimates show information asymmetry decreasing and transaction costs increasing over the day. PROXY NOTE: the paper signs trades against quotes; here the tick rule on bar closes is the substitute.

cut.name: BVC Imbalance at Range Edge
cut.note: Bulk volume classification splits each bar's volume with Phi(dP/sigma), the halves accumulate on a volume clock in buckets of (median daily volume of the last 20 sessions)/50, and CI is the signed imbalance summed over the last 20 completed buckets, z-scored against its own 250-bucket history. It buys only where flow and price DISAGREE: price pinned near the low of a narrow 60-bar range while net buying is 1.5 sigma high. Short is the mirror. The two geometric thresholds are recalibrated to five-minute data, where a 60-bar range measures 5-13 ATR (median 9.6) and the distance to the nearer edge is 0.86 ATR at its 20th percentile: the source's 3.0 ATR range cap and 0.30 ATR proximity are unreachable there, so the swept bands are 7.5-11 and 0.6-1.0 ATR, which pick out the same relative narrowness and the same pinning.
cut.source: Easley, D., Lopez de Prado, M., O'Hara, M. (2012), 'Flow Toxicity and Liquidity in a High-Frequency World', Review of Financial Studies, and 'An Improved Version of the Volume-Synchronized Probability of Informed Trading' (Critical Finance Review) - BVC classifies bar volume via the CDF of the standardized price change; VPIN averages |Vbuy - Vsell| over n equal-volume buckets.

cut.name: Forecast Combination Timer
cut.note: Ten univariate predictive regressions of the next period's log return on one OHLCV-derived predictor each (log RVOL, 12-period momentum, 1-period return, price vs long moving average, realised skew, relative volume, log Amihud illiquidity, realised variance, its 12-period change, drawdown depth), each fitted by expanding-window OLS, each forecast Campbell-Thompson truncated, then combined equally or by DMSPE weights built from each model's own discounted squared forecast error. Long while the combination is positive. The paper's monthly clock is rescaled to a period of h bars; the five cross-sectional predictors of the original 14 are dropped because they need a universe, not one symbol's OHLCV.
cut.source: Rapach, D.E., Strauss, J.K. and Zhou, G., 'Out-of-Sample Equity Premium Prediction: Combination Forecasts and Links to the Real Economy', Review of Financial Studies 23(2), 2010, 821-862 (method and the 1.16% figure verified via Neely et al., FRB St. Louis WP 2010-008). DMSPE weighting per Stock and Watson (2004) as adopted by RSZ. Combination benchmark 0.62% from Pettenuzzo, Timmermann and Valkanov, Brandeis WP 57 (2013).

cut.name: FZ-Loss GAS Tail State
cut.note: A one-factor GAS recursion for joint VaR and expected shortfall whose forcing term is zero on any bar that did not breach VaR, so the latent state kappa updates only on tail days. a and b are set from the window's own empirical alpha-quantile and tail mean; beta and gamma are chosen by minimising the FZ0 loss over the trailing window, refitted on a cadence. Long while tail risk is both low (kappa below the median of its trailing 250) and falling; out when kappa reaches the 80th percentile or rises three closes running.
cut.source: Patton, Ziegel & Chen (2019), 'Dynamic semiparametric models for expected shortfall (and Value-at-Risk)', Journal of Econometrics 211(2), 388-413 - FZ0 loss eq. (6), one-factor GAS eqs. (17)-(20), and the finding that omega is unidentified in the one-factor specification.

cut.name: Split-Conformal Zero Exclusion
cut.note: Ridge regression of the forward h-bar log return on seven standardised technical features, refitted on the older 500 of the trailing 750 bars, with the most recent 250 held out purely as a conformal calibration set. The half-width is the empirical quantile of |residual|/(ATR/close) on that held-out set, so it is distribution-free and scales with volatility. Trades only when the whole interval excludes zero, and the stop is that same calibrated half-width. Miscoverage is swept above the source's 0.05-0.35 band because a seven-feature ridge on five-minute bars forecasts far inside its own residual scale, and at 0.20 the interval straddles zero on every bar.
cut.source: Vovk, Gammerman & Shafer, Algorithmic Learning in a Random World (Springer, 2005); Lei, G'Sell, Rinaldo, Tibshirani & Wasserman (2018) split conformal. Coverage under non-exchangeability: Barber, Candes, Ramdas & Tibshirani, 'Conformal prediction beyond exchangeability'; arXiv:2203.15885. Time-series conformal sets: arXiv:2206.07851.

cut.name: Bar location gate on a Donchian breakout
cut.note: The reference signal is the plain Donchian rule -- close above the highest high of the preceding dc_n bars, mirrored short. The manipulated variable is a close-location gate: CLV = (close - low) / (high - low), the close's position inside the bar's own range, taken as the only OHLCV proxy available for whether the imbalance that produced the signal survived to the bar's end. A breakout bar that closes on its low is a breakout that already failed inside the bar. The gate is a TIMING rule rather than a filter: a signal whose bar closes badly is not discarded, it is carried forward for up to `defer` more bars and taken at the close of the first one that both clears CLV and (when require_s is on) still satisfies S. defer=0 in the grid is the pure filter, and clv_hi=0.5 is close to no gate at all, so the sweep spans the gate's whole range from off to strict. On the four probe symbols the median CLV of a 20-bar breakout bar is about 0.88 and 78 percent clear 0.7, so the paper threshold is comfortably reachable rather than aspirational. Execution follows the idea's reference: a hard 2*ATR stop, no profit target, and a 30-bar time stop, so the gate is the only thing that varies.
cut.source: Cont, Kukanov & Stoikov (2014), 'The Price Impact of Order Book Events', Journal of Financial Econometrics 12(1):47-88, arXiv:1011.6402 - near-linear order-flow-imbalance to price relation with the coefficient inverse to depth. Gould & Bonart (2016), 'Queue Imbalance as a One-Tick-Ahead Price Predictor in a Limit Order Book', arXiv:1512.03492. The CLV substitution for book imbalance is the harvesting agent's own proxy, since there is no level 2 here.

cut.name: Live deflated Sharpe re-gate
cut.note: A promotion/demotion gate over a corpus, not a price rule. Nine deliberately overlapping candidates (three breakout lengths, three EMA crosses, two channel-reversion rules, one momentum sign) each carry their own mark-to-market per-bar return series. Every ds_every bars the gate re-runs on the WHOLE history to date - an EXPANDING window, which is what turns a one-shot backtest screen into a live monitor: as realized bars accumulate, a candidate admitted on early luck watches its own DSR fall without any separate decay test. N_eff is the eigenvalue construction the idea specifies - the number of leading eigenvalues of the candidates' correlation matrix needed to explain var_cut of total variance, floored at 2 - and not rho + (1-rho)*M; on the probe symbols that lands at 3 to 9 out of 9 as var_cut moves from 0.90 to 0.99. E[maxSR] uses the Euler-Mascheroni two-term form and DSR carries the Mertens skew/raw-kurtosis correction. Admission at ds_admit, demotion at ds_demote, with the gap as deliberate hysteresis; a candidate paper-only for `patience` consecutive evaluations is struck from the corpus for good. The traded signal is the net vote of the survivors with exit_on_zero, so a demoted candidate's contribution vanishes and the book flattens when the rest no longer agree. CALIBRATION, STATED PLAINLY: over 45 days of 5-minute bars the highest DSR any candidate reaches is about 0.63 and the typical maximum is 0.3-0.5, so the paper's tau = 0.95 arms nothing at all and 0.90 arms nothing either. That is the deflation working rather than a bug, but a cell that never fires costs the study wall-clock and returns nothing, so the swept admission thresholds sit at the reachable end (0.25/0.35/0.6) and the paper's tau is recorded here as measured-unreachable on this window rather than swept. It is not unreachable in general: DSR carries a sqrt(T-1) factor, so a multi-year daily history can clear 0.95 where 45 days of 5-minute bars cannot. Read a win at ds_admit 0.6 as close to the paper's claim and a win only at 0.25 as a weaker, relative-ranking version of it. Sibling of b003-deflated-sharpe-arming-gate, which uses the same deflation with a TRAILING window and the rho-based N_eff; the expanding window, the eigenvalue N_eff and the permanent deletion are the differences, and the pair is the controlled test of which construction matters.
cut.source: Bailey, D.H. & Lopez de Prado, M. (2014), the Deflated Sharpe Ratio. Implementation details from Santoni, Jouanne & Scullin, arXiv:2608.23808 sections 3-4: the tau_DSR = 0.95 gate, the Mertens i.i.d. skew/kurtosis variance correction, and the effective-number-of-independent-trials construction obtained by decorrelating with an eigenvalue-based approach. The same paper reports that its five-gate composite showed no significant forward relationship on unseen data (Spearman rho = 0.013, p = 0.40), so this is a floor on statistical support, not a predictor of profit.

cut.name: Point-and-figure triple top with vertical count target
cut.note: A high/low point-and-figure grid with box b = box_atr * ATR(pf_atr_n), pinned for a block of box_sessions sessions (the daily rule is 'first trading day of the month'; a session block is the honest intraday equivalent) and a rev_boxes reversal. Entry is the classic triple top: the live X column posts a box strictly above the tops of the tops-1 preceding X columns, which needs several completed columns of structure rather than a single new high. The exit is what makes this family its own thing: a VERTICAL COUNT price objective. At the breakout, count the boxes N in the breakout column measured from that column's own bottom and set the target at bottom + N * b * vc_mult, so the profit objective is a function of the congestion height that was just cleared rather than of ATR, an R multiple or an indicator flip. The other exit leg is structural: a double-bottom breakdown (an O column printing one box below the preceding O column's low) kills a long, a double top covers a short. No ATR stop and no ATR target are set, because the 3-box reversal already embeds a rev_boxes * box_atr * ATR filter and the count is the whole point. Sibling of b001-point-and-figure-triple-top, which trades the same entry with a purely structural exit; the vertical count and the session-pinned box are the difference, and the pair is the controlled test of whether the count adds anything.
cut.source: Thomas Dorsey, 'Point and Figure Charting' (Wiley) for the triple-top/bottom signals and the vertical count; Jeremy du Plessis, 'The Definitive Guide to Point and Figure' (Harriman House) for the high/low construction method and count mechanics. On formalising chart patterns into testable algorithms: Lo, Mamaysky & Wang, 'Foundations of Technical Analysis', NBER WP 7613 (2000), DOI 10.3386/w7613.

cut.name: 52-week high proximity level
cut.note: George and Hwang's price level, not a price change: PH = close / the highest high of the trailing lb bars. Long while PH sits in the band [ph_lo, 1.00) AND the close is NOT a new lb-bar closing high AND no new high has been made in the last excl bars -- deliberately the opposite of a breakout, the trade is on price pinned just under the anchor and unable to get through it. Short when PH falls to ph_short. Entries are only considered every `every` bars, the monthly cadence of the original construction, and the hold is the time stop; early exit when PH leaves the band badly. TWO PARTS OF THE PUBLISHED RULE ARE NOT HERE and are not faked: the cross-sectional top/bottom 30% fleet rank needs every symbol at once, which a single-symbol ctx cannot see, and the six overlapping cohorts are a portfolio construction the shared one-position harness has no way to express.
cut.source: Thomas J. George and Chuan-Yang Hwang, 'The 52-Week High and Momentum Investing', Journal of Finance 59(5), October 2004, 2145-2176, read at https://www.bauer.uh.edu/tgeorge/papers/gh4-paper.pdf -- stocks ranked on P_{i,t-1}/high_{i,t-1}, 30% cutoffs, 6-month hold. Grinblatt & Keloharju corroborate the price-level effect on Finnish account data.

cut.name: Ease of movement air pocket
cut.note: Arms's box ratio, volume divided by the bar's range, is the local depth of resting liquidity. This buys a fresh ext_n-bar closing high made on a box ratio in the bottom pct_in percent of its own trailing 100-bar distribution, with the bar closing up and smoothed Ease of Movement positive -- a breakout into a price level where almost nobody was willing to trade. Shorts mirror it at a new closing low. The exit is symmetric and also a box-ratio percentile: the trade is over the moment volume per unit of range returns to the top pct_out percent, i.e. someone is defending the price again. A 2-ATR trailing stop runs underneath.
cut.source: Ease of Movement / box ratio arithmetic verified from the `ta` library source, https://raw.githubusercontent.com/bukosabino/ta/master/ta/volume.py (EaseOfMovementIndicator: emv = (high.diff(1) + low.diff(1)) * (high - low) / (2 * volume) * 1e8). Indicator originally Richard W. Arms Jr.; the air-pocket entry and the percentile exit are the harvested synthesis.

cut.name: ICSS variance break restart
cut.note: Inclan-Tiao cumulative-sum-of-squares test on a rolling T-bar window of demeaned log returns: D_k = C_k/C_T - k/T, IT = sqrt(T/2)*max|D_k|, a break declared at the argmax when IT clears the critical value. A trade is taken only on a NEWLY located break that is recent (within rec_frac of the window) and where the post-break mean square is below vratio times the pre-break one -- the volatility regime just CONTRACTED. Direction is the drift measured only since the break, never across it. Exit on the next declared break, either direction, or the time stop. DEVIATION, stated plainly: the harvested rule asked for a break inside the last 3 bars, which this statistic cannot produce -- D_k -> 0 as k -> T by construction, so an edge break is undetectable at any critical value. Recency is therefore a fraction of the window, the smallest change that leaves the test able to fire at all. Measured on real bars: a contraction break is first locatable roughly 20-30% of the window after it happens, so rec_frac lives there; crit and vratio are left as tunables but are not swept because on real data the argmax break is either an obvious contraction (ratio ~0.35) or an expansion (ratio > 2.5), with nothing in between for them to separate.
cut.source: Inclan & Tiao (1994), 'Use of Cumulative Sums of Squares for Retrospective Detection of Changes of Variance', JASA 89(427), 913-923; critical values 1.358 (5%) and 1.628 (1%). GARCH-robust kappa_2 variant: Sanso, Arago & Carrion (2004). R reference implementation: CRAN package ICSS.

cut.name: Reflex displacement inside a TrendFlex regime
cut.note: Ehlers' SuperSmoother feeds two orthogonal statistics built from the same filtered series: Reflex, the mean gap between the filtered price and the straight line joining it to its value n bars ago, and TrendFlex, the same difference-sum without the slope added back. Both are divided by the square root of an EWMA of their own square, so they read as self-calibrating standard errors and one threshold means the same thing on every symbol. TrendFlex gives the regime; a fresh Reflex cross down through -disp inside an up regime is a measured displacement below the zero-lag trend line, and that is the long entry. Exit when Reflex is reclaimed past +rf_exit, when TrendFlex loses its sign, or on the time stop. Threshold sanity, measured rather than assumed: on real 5-minute bars |Reflex| has a median near 0.62 and a 99th percentile near 2.5, so the published 2.5 setting produces 0-6 gated crosses in 6,000 bars and is not a signal at all. The swept displacements are therefore 1.0/1.5/2.0, which sit at roughly the 75th, 90th and 97th percentiles of the statistic.
cut.source: John F. Ehlers, 'Reflex: A New Zero-Lag Indicator', Technical Analysis of Stocks & Commodities, February 2020. Slope-detrended difference sum, the 0.04/0.96 mean-square EWMA and the division by sqrt(MS) verified against github.com/MathisWellmann/go_ehlers_indicators, file re_flex.go. The TrendFlex-gated displacement entry is the harvested synthesis.

cut.name: Rest-of-day hedging momentum
cut.note: One hard-scheduled decision per session. offset_min before the closing bar, measure rROD = log(price / the PREVIOUS session's closing price) -- a fixed-clock cumulative return that deliberately includes the overnight gap, not a bar-count lookback. Above +thr go long, below -thr go short, otherwise stand aside; the position is closed market-on-close the same session, so entry and exit times are constants rather than signal-driven. The closing bar is found from the data itself as the minute-of-day bucket with the largest median volume inside the plausible US close window, which uses no price information and survives DST and any bar size; close_min pins it manually. No profit target and no stop, because the published rule is a timed hold and a stop would truncate the effect being measured.
cut.source: Baltussen, Da, Lammers & Martens (2021), 'Hedging demand and market intraday momentum', Journal of Financial Economics 142(1), 377-403; full text at https://academicweb.nd.edu/~zda/intramom.pdf. Sharpe 0.87-1.73 at asset-class level across 60+ futures markets, 1974-2020, with the negative-dealer-gamma mechanism verified directly in the paper.

cut.name: Volume clock versus wall clock volatility ratio
cut.note: Builds volume bars on a threshold of (rolling median of the previous nd daily volumes) / div, carrying the remainder, and records each one's clock duration. sigma_v is the dispersion of returns on the volume clock; sigma_t is the dispersion on the wall clock, rescaled to the volume bar's mean duration. R = sigma_t_scaled / sigma_v measures how much of the observed clock-time volatility is an artefact of volume clustering rather than price discovery. Long when R sits in the bottom p_in percent of its own trailing distribution -- volume arriving evenly, price moving proportionally -- and the last mom_n volume bars are cumulatively up. Out when R reaches the top p_out percent, after hold_vb volume bars, or on the ATR stop. The signal is a ratio of two sampling clocks; there is no moving average and no oscillator anywhere in it. Volume bars are cut on the harness's own bar stream rather than 1-minute data, so at most one volume bar closes per source bar.
cut.source: Easley, Lopez de Prado & O'Hara, 'The Volume Clock: Insights into the High-Frequency Paradigm', Journal of Portfolio Management 39(1), 2012, for the volume clock and the IID-normalisation claim. Bar construction from Lopez de Prado, 'Advances in Financial Machine Learning' (Wiley, 2018), Ch.2 'Financial Data Structures', section 2.3. The ratio statistic and the trading rule are the harvested synthesis.

cut.name: BinHV45 Bollinger break with candle anatomy
cut.note: The BinHV45 conjunction: a close below the PREVIOUS bar's lower band (so the breaking bar does not widen the band it must break), no higher than the previous close, and three bar-geometry magnitudes each normalised to a different denominator -- band width bbdelta/close, bar displacement closedelta/close, and wick length tail/bbdelta, which must be SMALL because the close has to sit on the low with no dip-buying absorption yet. THRESHOLD NOTE: the published 0.007/0.017/0.025 were tuned on crypto and the source explicitly says to re-sweep them; measured on real 5-minute equity bars the same three ratios differ by more than 10x across symbols (median bbdelta/close is 0.0015 on SPY and 0.020 on SOXL), so one absolute constant cannot mean the same thing on two names. Each ratio is therefore compared to its own trailing q_win-bar percentile, which is the same conjunction self-calibrated per instrument. Exit is the first close back above the 40-bar mid, with a 20-bar time stop.
cut.source: freqtrade-strategies, user_data/strategies/berlinguyinca/BinHV45.py -- https://github.com/freqtrade/freqtrade-strategies/blob/main/user_data/strategies/berlinguyinca/BinHV45.py

cut.name: Darvas box with three-day confirmed walls
cut.note: The box is built exactly as Darvas described it. A new hi_n-bar high on volume above vol_mult times the 50-bar average opens a candidate ceiling; the ceiling only counts once conf consecutive bars have all failed to exceed it, and any bar that does exceed it resets the ceiling and restarts the count. Then the lowest low made since the ceiling bar becomes the candidate floor, confirmed the same way, restarting on any violation. Entry is the breakout above the confirmed ceiling plus off_atr*ATR. The exit is the box floor and nothing else -- no profit target -- and it RATCHETS: when a new box completes higher the floor rises with it, and it never falls.
cut.source: Nicolas Darvas, 'How I Made $2,000,000 in the Stock Market' (1960); algorithmic box construction with the three-consecutive-day confirmation rule for both ceiling and floor described at https://clickalgo.com/darvas-box-theory and https://investinganswers.com/dictionary/d/darvas-box-theory

cut.name: EMD cycle-versus-trend mode switch
cut.note: Ehlers' empirical mode decomposition regime switch, implemented from his Figure 9 listing. A 2-pole bandpass on (high+low)/2 isolates the swing component; its mean over 2*Period bars is compared to a fraction of the 50-bar average of the tracked local peaks and valleys of the bandpass itself. Mean above Fraction*AvgPeak is UPTREND, below Fraction*AvgValley is DOWNTREND, otherwise CYCLE -- and the mode changes the RULE SET, not just permission to trade. Uptrend: long on a bandpass cross above zero. Cycle: long on a cross above AvgValley, short on a cross below AvgPeak. Downtrend takes no longs (dn_short=1 adds the mirror short on a zero cross down). Exits are the mode's own: the regime at the entry bar decides which exit applies.
cut.source: John F. Ehlers and Ric Way, 'Empirical Mode Decomposition: A novel approach for cycle and trend mode detection', https://www.mesasoftware.com/papers/EmpiricalModeDecomposition.pdf -- Figure 9 EasyLanguage listing (beta/gamma/alpha bandpass recursion, Mean = Average(BP, 2*Period), Peak/Valley detection, AvgPeak/AvgValley = Average(...,50), Fraction thresholds) and the concluding trend/cycle delineation rule.

cut.name: Five-condition pivot reversal bar
cut.note: A demand pivot (fractal low, half-width fw) is broken, then reclaimed within gap bars by a single bar satisfying all five conditions at once: close above the two prior closes, close back above the broken pivot low, close above its own open, close above the midq fraction of its own range, and a range larger than the previous bar's. cut.name: Momentum burst out of a tight base

cut.name: Sharpe-loss momentum network
cut.note: Lim/Zohren/Roberts' deep momentum network, reduced to the one layer that can be fitted inside a backtest. The exact 8-feature vector is built per bar: five volatility-normalised returns over 1/21/63/126/252 bars divided by an EWM return std (span 60) times sqrt(k), plus three normalised MACD signals for (8,24), (16,48), (32,96) -- EWMA with halflife log(0.5)/log(1-1/S), which is exactly alpha=1/S, divided by a 63-bar close std and then by a 252-bar std of itself. The position is X = tanh(w.u / (sd*gain)), and w is refit on an expanding causal window by MAXIMISING THE SHARPE of the traded stream, not by predicting direction: with P&L R = (w.u)*v where v is the vol-scaled forward return, R = w.g for g = u*v, so the Sharpe-optimal w is cov(g)^-1 mean(g), solved with ridge every refit bars. Long above the deadband, short below, flat inside -- the tanh magnitude is the exit. HONEST LIMIT: the LSTM's recurrence and nonlinearity are dropped, since training a network per backtest is not possible here, so this tests the paper's feature set, its Sharpe objective and its tanh/deadband response function with a linear layer.
cut.source: Lim, Zohren & Roberts (2019), 'Enhancing Time Series Momentum Strategies Using Deep Neural Networks', arXiv:1904.04912. Entry is the next bar closing beyond that bar's extreme without taking out its other side. cut.name: Analogue forecast with distance abstention
cut.note: The feature is the whole z-normalised m-bar price path. For every bar, the k closest historical windows inside a trailing history are found, subject to the neighbour's own forward H-bar return already being fully observed and its window not overlapping the query's; the vote is the mean and the sign-agreement of those neighbours' realised forward returns. The part that matters is the third condition: textbook k-NN always returns k neighbours however far away they are, so it always has an opinion. Requiring the mean neighbour distance to sit below its own trailing 20th percentile makes the rule abstain whenever the current shape is unprecedented. Exit is a hard time stop at exactly H bars - the horizon the neighbours voted on - plus the source's 2*sigma_H adverse stop, both in exit_signal, which is why tp_atr and st_atr are switched off. Two implementation notes, both material: shapes are compared in 5-segment PAA space (Lin, Keogh et al., cited in the source) rather than at full resolution, and candidate windows are examined every second bar, because the harness has no numpy and a full-resolution all-pairs join over every bar is not affordable in pure Python. Adjacent windows are near-duplicates, so the stride costs almost nothing; the PAA distance is the standard lower bound on the true z-normalised distance.
cut.source: Yeh, Zhu, Ulanova, Begum, Ding, Dau, Silva, Mueen & Keogh, 'Matrix Profile I: All Pairs Similarity Joins for Time Series', IEEE ICDM 2016 - the z-normalised nearest-neighbour machinery and MASS. Discretised (SAX) variant: Lin, Keogh, Lonardi & Chiu (2003), 'A Symbolic Representation of Time Series, with Implications for Streaming Algorithms', ACM SIGMOD DMKD Workshop. Financial k-NN evidence: Alkhatib & Najadat, 'Stock Price Prediction Using K-Nearest Neighbor (kNN) Algorithm'.

cut.name: Auction blackout breakout
cut.note: A plain N-bar Donchian breakout, restricted to the regular session, with the first k_open minutes after 09:30 ET and the last k_close minutes before 16:00 ET blacked out for ENTRIES only. Exits are untouched - the harness's stop and target run inside the blackout window exactly as outside it, which is the asymmetry the source asks for. k_open = k_close = 0 is the unmodified base strategy and is the control arm in the grid, so the sweep measures the blackout against its own baseline rather than against another family. cut.source: Boyarchenko, Larsen & Whelan, 'The Overnight Drift', Federal Reserve Bank of New York Staff Reports no. 917, February 2020, revised August 2022. Read directly from newyorkfed.org - the characterisation of the 09:00-10:00 hour as large and negative only in recessions and flat otherwise, in contrast to the consistently significant 02:00-03:00 window, is in the paper's introduction.

cut.name: Overnight-only holding
cut.note: Buys the regular-session close on a weak-close day inside an uptrend and sells the next regular-session open, holding exactly one overnight gap and nothing else. IBS is (close - low)/(high - low) over the running 09:30-16:00 extremes at the decision bar; the entry fires on the last session bar before the cut, so the harness fills it at the next bar's open, which is the closing print. The exit fires on the last bar before 09:30 the next morning, whose close is the last price before the opening auction. Two honest deviations: the source's SMA(200) daily trend gate needs 200 daily closes that a 45-day intraday window does not contain, so the gate length is a swept parameter with 0 = off; and the fills are bar-boundary proxies for MOC/MOO, which the source itself flags as the assumption this strategy is most sensitive to.
cut.source: Overnight-edge strategies are a standing published category at quantifiedstrategies.com - their index states the construction directly: 'buying at the close of the stock exchange until the open the next day'. Oddmund Groette publishes several such backtests free and covers them on YouTube. The underlying close-to-open versus open-to-close return decomposition is one of the most widely replicated results in equity microstructure. cut.name: Three-fifths power execution horizon
cut.note: Almgren, Thum, Hauptmann & Li's fitted temporary-impact cost, Cost(T) = eta*sigma_d*|X/(V*T)|^(3/5) + lambda*sigma_d*(X/V)*sqrt(T), grid-searched over the paper's horizon set {0.05 ... 2.0} days to give T* and the minimised cost. Two things fall out and both are used: the horizon T*, converted to N bars, is how far ahead the drift is projected; and twice the minimised cost is the round-trip hurdle the projected move has to clear before the trade is worth doing. Note that sigma_d multiplies BOTH terms and so cancels out of the argmin - the optimal horizon is a function of participation alone - while it scales the cost level, which is why the hurdle moves with volatility even though the horizon does not. The scheduling half of the idea (slice X/N per bar) belongs to the execution harness, not to a signal, so what is implemented here is the model's decision content: when the fitted cost says the round trip is affordable relative to the drift it is chasing. Order size is the desk's standard clip, x_adv of the slow ADV, executed against the fast ADV, so participation rises when recent volume dries up. Calibration check on real bars: at the defaults the median projected move over T* is about the same size as the round-trip hurdle, so roughly half of all bars are refused, and the sweep of x_adv and lambda moves that refusal rate across the whole range from 0 to 99 per cent. The hurdle is the binding constraint, not decoration on a drift sign.
cut.source: Almgren, R., Thum, C., Hauptmann, E. & Li, H. (2005), 'Direct Estimation of Equity Market Impact': fitted exponents alpha = 0.891 +/- 0.10 (permanent, linear not rejected), delta = 0.267 +/- 0.22 (liquidity factor ~ 1/4), beta = 0.600 +/- 0.038 (temporary); coefficients gamma = 0.314 +/- 0.041 (t = 7.7) and eta = 0.142 +/- 0.0062 (t = 23); 'At the 95% confidence level, the square-root model beta = 1/2 is rejected.'

cut.name: Turnover budget greedy queue
cut.note: Every candidate trade is scored as expected edge per unit of trading cost and has to win a share of a hard, exhaustible turnover budget. E is the walk-forward conditional expected H-bar log return, estimated on a trailing window of bars whose forward return was already fully observed, conditioned on which of five z-score buckets the price currently sits in. C is an Abdi-Ranaldo two-period high-low spread estimate plus the Almgren three-fifths temporary-impact term evaluated at the holding horizon. A trade fills only if E/C clears the trailing rank_q quantile of its own recent distribution AND the rolling one-day budget of b_day/clip fills is not already spent. Exits queue for the same budget with their score multiplied by m_exit > 1, so risk reduction outranks risk addition at equal edge per cost, while the harness's stop and target bypass the budget entirely, which is the source's stop-loss exemption. WHAT IS MISSING, said plainly: the source's budget is shared ACROSS a book of symbols, and that cross-sectional competition cannot exist in a per-symbol harness. Here candidates compete against the distribution of their own recent opportunities instead, so b_day buys selectivity over time rather than reallocating between names. The spread estimator is Abdi and Ranaldo rather than the source's EDGE because EDGE's full estimator is not affordable per bar in pure Python; it is the direct simple ancestor in the same high-low family, not a convenience substitute.
cut.source: Synthesis. Grounded in Novy-Marx & Velikov (RFS 2016) turnover taxonomy and cost-mitigation results, and in the cost-penalised model-comparison objective of Detzel, A., Novy-Marx, R. & Velikov, M. (2023), 'Model Comparison with Transaction Costs', Journal of Finance - which argues that models must be ranked on net-of-cost rather than gross efficient frontiers. Spread estimator: Abdi, F. & Ranaldo, A. (2017), 'A Simple Estimation of Bid-Ask Spreads from Daily Close, High, and Low Prices', Review of Financial Studies 30(12). Impact term: Almgren, Thum, Hauptmann & Li (2005), eta = 0.142, exponent 3/5.

cut.name: Diurnal-Scaled Range Breakout
cut.note: Every 5-minute slot of the day gets its own volatility unit D_s -- the median high-low range of that same clock slot over the previous N sessions -- and both the breakout buffer and the risk are quoted in D_s, so a 12-cent midday break and a 40-cent opening break are the same event. The regular session is located from the tape's own volume profile rather than assumed, so it is right in either DST; the stop/target/trail are carried in exit_signal because the whole point is that they re-scale with the clock rather than with a flat ATR.

cut.name: FLOSS Arc-Curve Segmentation
cut.note: Regime boundaries from the topology of nearest-neighbour arcs rather than from any moment of the return distribution: each finished subsequence is joined to its closest earlier match, and where the market's shape vocabulary changes almost no arc crosses, so the corrected arc curve collapses. Entry is the direction of the new regime measured against the m bars before the boundary; exit is the next boundary. Arcs are the causal backward form (a new subsequence matching the past), which is the only version knowable in real time; distances are z-normalised PAA so the whole thing stays cheap.

Financial application survey: 'Financial Time Series: Market Analysis Techniques Based on Matrix Profiles', MDPI Engineering Proceedings 5(1):45.

cut.name: KAMA noise-scaled excursion filter
cut.note: Kaufman's adaptive moving average, then his own percent-of-standard-deviation filter: go long only once KAMA has travelled f x stdev(KAMA differences) up from its running low, short once it has fallen that far from its running high. The reference is a high-water mark that only resets on a signal, so the system cannot flip on one bar's turn, and f = 0 nests the naive slope-sign version.

cut.name: Laguerre RSI Unpinning
cut.note: The four-stage Laguerre cascade saturates LRSI at 0 or 1 for as long as the four stages stay perfectly ordered, so being pinned is a STATE, not a level. The entry is the termination of that state -- the first bar that comes off the rail after three or more pinned bars -- and the exit is the traverse to the opposite rail or a fall back onto the one it left.
cut.source: John F. Ehlers, 'Time Warp - Without Space Travel' (mesasoftware.com/papers/TimeWarp.pdf) for the Laguerre filter and Laguerre RSI. cut.name: Renko Brick Velocity Burst
cut.note: Close-only Renko bricks, then the signal is the CLOCK rather than the price: two consecutive same-colour bricks that both printed faster than the 20th percentile of the last 50 brick durations is urgency, and urgency is autocorrelated over the next few price quanta. Brick size is frozen each week at brick_mult x ATR of the trading timeframe (the idea's DAILY ATR makes bricks so large that an intraday run produces a handful of them), and durations are measured in bars, which equals wall-clock inside a session and neutralises the overnight gap.

cut.name: Roughness Index of Log-Volatility
cut.note: Estimates the Hurst exponent of LOG-VOLATILITY (not of price) with the q=1 absolute-increment scaling m(D) ~ D^H of the rough-volatility literature, on realised volatility measured over non-overlapping blocks of bars. When vol is unusually PERSISTENT and high it follows the tape; when it is unusually ROUGH it fades a 2-ATR excursion from the mean, because a one-bar vol spike has no follow-through mechanism. The literature's absolute 0.25/0.08 cutoffs are daily-calibrated and unreachable intraday (measured H is 0.0-0.15 on every probe symbol), so the two branches are cut on H's own trailing percentile, which is what 'H drifts up toward persistence' actually means.

The rolling-window trading application and the two-branch entry are my synthesis.

cut.name: Value Area Overlap Regime Switch
cut.note: The Jaccard overlap of today's 70% value area with yesterday's says which auction you are in, and that decides what the SAME price means tomorrow: heavily overlapping value areas (balance) fade a close beyond yesterday's VAH/VAL back to the POC, disjoint ones with a migrating POC (discovery) go WITH the break. Between the two thresholds it stands aside. The profile is built from the execution bars rather than 1-minute bars, and the session is located from the volume profile itself so no exchange calendar or DST rule is assumed.

cut.name: GARCH-POT conditional-EVT regime
cut.note: McNeil & Frey's two-stage conditional EVT, traded as the regime switch its sizing rule implies. An AR(1)-GARCH(1,1) filter standardises returns; a generalized Pareto is fitted to the residual exceedances below the thr_pct quantile; one-step VaR and ES follow in closed form from the composition. Long while the conditional tail is well behaved - GPD shape xi below xi_max, forecast |ES| at or under es_mult x its own med_win median, and fewer than breach_n VaR_0.01 breaches in the last breach_win bars - and flat the moment any of those fails, with re-entry only after |ES| has been under its median for `cool` consecutive bars. The exit is a MODEL breaking down, not a price level: two charts that look identical give different answers because their residual tails have different shape parameters. DEPARTURES, stated: position sizing off ES is the harness's job, not the signal's, so what is traded is the in/out state; the GARCH parameters are fixed with variance targeting rather than re-maximised each bar (persistence becomes a swept parameter instead of an optimiser call per bar); and the GPD is fitted by probability-weighted moments rather than MLE, which is the standard cheap estimator over the xi < 0.5 range this rule is willing to trade at all. Checked on the probe bars, the one-step VaR_0.01 forecast is breached on 1.02% / 1.03% / 1.12% of bars for SPY, SOXL and XLU, so the tail estimate is calibrated rather than decorative; fitted xi medians run 0.30 (SPY), 0.40 (SOXL) and 0.22 (XLU), and the xi_max rejection excludes 11% / 32% / 0% of their fits respectively - the shape parameter really does separate the symbols.

cut.name: Sign-count z-score TSMOM
cut.note: S = (1/sqrt(M*L)) * sum of the last M*L one-bar return SIGNS. Magnitude is thrown away entirely, so a single gap or crash bar can neither flip nor dominate the signal, and the volatility estimator drops out because sign(r/sigma)=sign(r). The 1/sqrt(ML) scaling makes S a genuine unit-variance z-score under serially independent returns, so sweeping M and L is a sweep of the signal rather than a volatility sweep in disguise. Recomputed only on bars whose index is a multiple of L and forward-filled in between - the paper's L-period rebalance - and long above +s_min, short below -s_min, flat inside the deadband. No stop, by construction. The paper's notional scaling S x min(sigma_target/sigma_ann, cap) is position SIZING, which belongs to the shared harness; the deadband is what survives of it.

(A.16); optimal M = L = 10 from Section 7.1. Generalises Moskowitz, Ooi & Pedersen (2012) eq. (A.15) and the sign-of-normalised-returns averaging of Dudler, Gmur & Malamud (2015).

cut.name: Wyckoff spring in a bounded base
cut.note: A spring only counts inside a base that is genuinely bounded: over the base_n bars ending at bar[-1] the range must be at most width_atr x ATR, and support must have been tested at least `touches` times by bars at least touch_gap apart. The spring bar then needs a shallow undercut - deeper than min_pen ATR but NO DEEPER than max_pen ATR - a close back inside the base, a close in the top 1-close_frac of its own range, and volume at or under vol_cap x the 20-bar average. The depth BAND is the structural difference from a liquidity sweep, where deeper is stronger: a deep flush disqualifies the setup here because it is a real breakdown, not a test. Upthrust is the exact mirror at the range top. The objective is the opposite edge of the base, not an R multiple, and the trade is abandoned on a close fail_atr beyond the broken edge. GRID NOTE: the harvested idea asks for a base_n sweep of 20/30/40 against a fixed ATR width cap, and that cross product is empty by arithmetic, not by market behaviour - a 40-bar range is naturally about sqrt(2) wider than a 20-bar one, so at base_n=40 a 2.5-ATR cap admits nothing (measured: 0 setups across SPY/XLU/SOXL at any cap up to 3.0). base_n is therefore left at the 20 the inequality was written for and the sweep runs the axes that do discriminate; the cap range is shifted one step up to 2.5-3.5 because 2.0 also admits almost nothing (3 setups across the three symbols).

cut.name: Notional Equity Drawdown Ratchet
cut.note: The Turtle size ratchet, isolated. Position size is taken off a NOTIONAL equity of actual_equity * (1-cut)^k with k = floor(current drawdown / step), restored only on a new all-time equity high, so 30% down leaves about half size on 70% of the capital. cut.name: Technical Signal Principal Components Premium Regression
cut.note: Neely-Rapach-Tu-Zhou: fourteen binary technical rules (six MA crossovers, two momentum, six OBV crossovers) are never traded themselves - they are standardised on data through t, reduced to their leading principal components, and the components are fed to an expanding-window OLS forecast of the NEXT periods return. Long when the fitted value is positive, flat when it is truncated at zero. K is re-chosen each period by adjusted R-squared unless n_pc pins it. The papers monthly rebalance is mapped onto blocks of period_bars bars; PCA is a pure-Python Jacobi rotation, no numpy.

cut.name: Unfilled Order Ledger
cut.note: Not a signal - an order-type experiment. The signal set is frozen (20-bar Donchian breaks) and only the arm changes: 0 takes the next open, 1 rests a limit k ATR back and simply never trades if it is not touched within n_life bars, 2 rests the same limit and chases at market when it expires. Exits are identical across arms (2 ATR stop, 3 ATR target, 40-bar time stop), so comparing arm 1 with arm 0 over the identical signal dates prices the opportunity cost of the unfilled orders - they are missing from arm 1 and present in arm 0. Honest limitation: the harness fills at the next open, so arm 1 gets the touch bars successor open rather than the limit price itself, which understates the price improvement and leaves only the adverse-selection half of the effect.
cut.source: Perold (1988), 'The Implementation Shortfall: Paper versus Reality', Journal of Portfolio Management 14(3):4-9 - the delay/execution/opportunity-cost decomposition. The adverse selection framing of resting limit orders is standard market microstructure.

cut.name: Cube-Root No-Trade Band
cut.note: An impulse-control position rule. The target weight is w* = clip(z/zdiv, -1, 1) with z the 50-bar z-score of (close - SMA50). Each bar a live round-trip cost fraction is estimated as spread_hat + 2*Y*sigma_d*sqrt(Q/V20) - a bar-by-bar OHLC spread estimate plus a square-root impact term - and the no-trade half-width is Delta = k * cost^(1/3), the cube-root law, so a tiny cost still buys a surprisingly wide band. The held weight only moves when it leaves the band, and then only to the NEAR EDGE (w* +/- Delta), never to w*, which is what halves the turnover again. The traded side is the sign of that held weight, so the position closes only when w* has crossed zero by more than Delta. SUBSTITUTION, stated plainly: the spread input is the Corwin-Schultz high-low estimator over the same window rather than EDGE - EDGE's GMM moment conditions are heavier than family_init can carry, and the substitution is on an input, not on the band law or the near-edge rebalance that are the actual idea.
cut.source: Novy-Marx, R. & Velikov, M., 'A Taxonomy of Anomalies and their Trading Costs' (NBER w20721), footnote 6, which cites Arrow, Harris & Marschak (1951) for the sS inaction region, Davis & Norman (1990) for 'an inaction region and a return to the closer boundary when rebalancing', and Abel & Eberly (1996) which shows 'the size of this region is proportional to the cube-root of the price wedge for small wedges, which makes its derivative with respect to the wedge infinite'. Spread input: Corwin & Schultz (2012), 'A Simple Way to Estimate Bid-Ask Spreads from Daily High and Low Prices', Journal of Finance 67(2).

cut.name: Honest Pullback Test
cut.note: One complete signal - close crossing above EMA(20) while ADX(14) is above adx_min - and TWO entry arms selected by pb_atr. pb_atr = 0 is Arm I: act on the signal bar itself. pb_atr > 0 is Arm P: arm a limit at min(EMA20, close - pb_atr*ATR) for the next pb_bars bars and act only on the first bar whose LOW touches it; a signal no bar touches produces no trade at all, which is exactly the sample the folklore quietly deletes. Exits are identical for both arms - a 2*ATR trail off the best close since entry plus an unconditional 30-bar time stop - so the only difference between two grid cells is WHEN the entry happened. The opportunity-cost ledger the idea asks for (scoring Arm P's unfilled signals at Arm I's realised return) is a report over the two arms' trade lists, not something a signal function can emit; putting both arms in one sweep is what makes that report computable downstream.
cut.source: Perold (1988) implementation shortfall opportunity-cost term, framework confirmed via the implementation shortfall literature; the survivorship-in-entries critique and the test design are my own synthesis.

cut.name: Naked POC Magnet
cut.note: A real volume-at-price profile is built for each regular-hours session: bins bin_pct percent of the session open wide, every bar's volume spread evenly over the bins its [low, high] covers, and the POC is the midpoint of the fullest bin. A finished session's POC joins a list and stays on it only while it remains NAKED - the moment any later session's range contains that price it is struck off, so membership is a topological fact about the tape rather than a threshold. Between start_min and end_min ET the nearest naked POC above and below the last price are measured in units of the SESSION ATR(14) built from the same profiles; the setup trades toward whichever is nearer, provided it sits between min_atr and max_atr away - close enough to be reachable, far enough to be worth the trip. One trade per level per day. Exit is the level itself, or flat at flat_min ET. The 1.0 x session-ATR stop the idea specifies is carried as st_atr in BAR-ATR units, which is the only stop unit the shared harness has.
cut.source: Market Profile / volume profile lineage (Steidlmayer, CBOT Liquidity Data Bank). Definitions and the naked/virgin POC concept per LuxAlgo concept library, https://www.luxalgo.com/library/concept/naked-poc/ and https://www.luxalgo.com/library/concept/point-of-control/ ; profile construction per TradingView docs, https://www.tradingview.com/support/solutions/43000502040-volume-profile-indicators-basic-concepts/ . Exact bin widths, ATR gating and the 60-session horizon are the harvesting agent's specification.

cut.name: Online Logistic Regression with Dead Band
cut.note: Eight technical features, each standardised by an EXPANDING mean/sd that only ever sees bars strictly before the current one, are fed to a logistic regression whose weights are updated by online SGD. The update is DELAYED and causally honest: the sample built at bar t is held in a queue and only learned from at bar t+hor, when its label (did the close rise over hor bars) has actually matured. Trading starts after warmup bars. The dead band is the point: long only when p > 0.5+band, short only when p < 0.5-band, silent in between, so the model abstains whenever its features disagree. Because the weights are never batch-refit they drift with the tape, and the sign of the coefficient on the momentum feature is free to flip, which is what makes one piece of code a momentum model in one regime and a reversion model in another. Exit is the same hor-bar horizon the label was defined over, plus a 2*ATR stop; a still-valid probability simply re-enters on the next bar, so a persistent signal rolls.
cut.source: Standard online SGD logistic regression. Finance instantiation with technical-indicator features and a cascaded architecture: Zhang, Zhang et al., 'Cascading logistic regression onto gradient boosted decision trees for forecasting and trading stock indices', Applied Soft Computing 84 (2019). Adaptive online mid-price learning with Hessian-based adaptive rate: PLOS ONE 15(6): e0234107, 'Mid-price prediction based on machine learning methods with technical and quantitative indicators'.

cut.name: Price-Impact Compression (Amihud)
cut.note: Amihud's ILLIQ - the mean of |log return| divided by dollar volume over illiq_win bars, scaled by 1e6 - is price move per dollar traded, i.e. the SLOPE of the demand curve rather than how far price has already gone. It is ranked against its own trailing pct_hist history to give P_I, and ATR(14)/close is ranked the same way to give P_V. The distinctive cell is the DIVERGENCE: P_I >= p_i with P_V <= p_v, high impact while volatility is ordinary, which says the calm is an absence of participants rather than an absence of disagreement. That arms the setup for arm_win bars; the trade itself needs a directional close (close location in the bar range beyond clv or 1-clv) confirmed by volume at vmult times its 20-bar average, because in a thin book a genuinely sized order travels much further than its size warrants. Exit is a 2*ATR trail, a 10-bar time stop, and an unconditional exit when P_I drops under exit_pi - liquidity has come back and the edge is gone whatever the P&L says.
cut.source: Amihud (2002), 'Illiquidity and stock returns: cross-section and time-series effects', Journal of Financial Markets 5(1) - the ILLIQ measure, defined as the daily average of |return| divided by dollar volume. Cited from knowledge; the harvesting agent's attempt to fetch a reference page 404'd. The impact-versus-volatility divergence condition and the entry structure are its synthesis.

cut.name: Volatility-Targeted Time-Series Momentum
cut.note: The sign of the trailing lb-bar return is the entire entry condition, re-evaluated only every hold bars and held untouched in between - the monthly rebalance of the published rule, in bars. Everything else is risk: ex-ante annualised volatility from an EWMA of squared returns with a centre of mass of com_frac*lb bars (0.25*252 = 63, the paper's 60), annualised by the bar rate inferred from the timestamps, gives the target leverage vol_target/sigma capped at lev_cap. LIMITATION, stated plainly: the shared harness sizes every family identically, so the continuously varying vol-inverse NOTIONAL - which is the idea's real content - cannot be expressed. What survives is the part of it that changes the trade decision rather than its size: the book goes FLAT whenever the vol-scaled target leverage falls below min_lev, so exposure is cut by a volatility spike before any price signal moves, plus the paper's optional intramonth overlay that flattens on a drawdown from the position's high-water mark beyond dd_mult*sigma/sqrt(12).
cut.source: Moskowitz, T.J., Ooi, Y.H., and Pedersen, L.H., 'Time Series Momentum', Journal of Financial Economics 104(2), 2012, pp. 228-250 - sign of the past 12-month excess return, one-month holding period, position scaled to a 40% annualised volatility target using an exponentially weighted ex-ante volatility estimate with a 60-day centre of mass.
